articleTitle: Multi-level Context Aggregation Network for Skin Lesion Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The automated segmentation of skin lesions constitutes a crucial phase in the computer-assisted diagnosis of skin cancer, providing a foundation for further analysis. With the advancement in convolutional neural networks, the segmentation effectiveness of skin lesions has experienced marked enhancement. However, challenges still exist in skin lesion segmentation, such as variations in lesion size, irregular lesion shapes, and fuzzy boundaries between lesions and the background. To achieve efficient and precise segmentation of skin lesions, we present the Multi-level Context Aggregation Network (MLCANet). In the encoder section, we adopt an InceptionNeXt network based on large kernel convolutions to expand the receptive field and enhance the extraction capability of contextual information. In the skip connection section, we introduce the Gated Fully Fusion method to effectively reconstruct skip connections, aggregating multi-level contextual information. This method leverages the advantages of different layer feature maps to strengthen the encoder features. Additionally, we propose a residual multi-scale channel attention module at the end of the model to emphasize critical channel information, thereby enhancing the performance of the model. Our experiments on the publicly ISIC 2018 skin lesion dataset reveal that our approach surpasses other methods across five commonly employed evaluation metrics, affirming the outstanding segmentation performance of our approach.

articleTitle: Reducing Complexity of CSI Feedback based on Deep Learning for Massive MIMO using Tensor-Train Decomposition
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: To further reduce the complexity of the channel state information (CSI) based on deep learning for massive multiple inputs and multiple outputs (MIMO) system, we propose a method called TT-CsiNet, based on the original CsiNet framework, using Tensor-Train decomposition to decompose the weights of the fully-connected layers, at the UE side. Experimental results show that the memory requirement is reduced by 99% of the original CsiNet for UEs, depending on the compression ratio. Moreover, TT-CsiNet can reduce the number of floating point operations (FLOPs) by about 17.27% to 80.44%, depending on the compression ratio. In addition, TT-CsiNet has comparable performance to the original CsiNet and other variants of the low complexity CsiNet using pruning, quantization, and weight clustering.

articleTitle: Carbon Emission Data Calculation and Interaction Model in Multi-modal Transportation based on the Identification and Resolution System for Industrial Internet
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In the carbon neutrality strategy, transportation is one of the critical areas for global emissions reduction. Multi-modal transportation, as a primary mode of international trade logistics, plays a significant role in the carbon neutrality strategy. There are numerous studies on optimizing carbon emission calculation models in multi-modal transportation. However, the accurate and real-time acquisition of carbon data and the computation, identification, querying, and sharing of carbon emissions data with different enterprises, regions, and industries remains a problem. The identification and resolution system for Industrial Internet, serving as a network infrastructure for heterogeneous data mapping and sharing, will play a crucial role in facilitating the interaction and sharing of multi-modal transportation carbon emissions data. Hence, this study proposes a multi-modal transport carbon emissions calculation model. The model considers distance, time, and weight for different modes of transport. Also, this study gave the method of carbon emission data collection and sharing, and proposed a blockchain-based carbon data trusted storage certificate. Finally, case analysis and experimental verification were proposed for the transportation from Yiwu, China to Berlin, Germany.

articleTitle: Multi-Way Compression for Channel Neural Decoding with Quantization
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The performance of model-driven channel neural decoding has surpassed that of traditional channel decoding algorithms, but at a higher complexity, making it difficult to implement on resource-constrained communication hardware. In this paper, we propose a quantization scheme for model-driven channel neural decoding, and combine the quantization scheme with TR decomposition and weight sharing algorithms to form different types of multi-way compression methods. Experimental results on LDPC, BCH and Hamming codes show that the proposed quantization and multi-way compression methods can effectively reduce the complexity of channel neural decoding without significant performance degradation.

articleTitle: Robust Adaptive Beamforming Based on Interference Covariance Matrix Reconstruction and LS criterion
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Array signal processing plays a crucial role in various domains such as communication, radar, and sonar. Among them, beamforming technology is highly regarded for its capability to effectively suppress noise and interference, thereby enhancing the quality of desired signals. In this paper, a robust adaptive beamforming spatial interference suppression algorithm based on LS criterion with matrix reconstruction is proposed. The interference steering vector is obtained by overlapping projection of the interference plus noise covariance matrix reconstructed by multiple signal classification spatial spectrum and the signal interference subspace to reduce the influence of the steering vector error on the algorithm. And by finding the weight in the null space of the interference steering vector that maximizes the output power of the signal direction, the performance degradation caused by the covariance matrix and steering vector error is reduced. The simulation results show that the proposed algorithm has good performance and strong robustness in jamming suppression when there are guidance vector estimation errors and limited snapshots. And compared with other two interference-plus-noise covariance matrix reconstruction algorithms, the proposed algorithm has better performance and lower complexity.

articleTitle: IMRP-Loc: An Indoor Localization Method Based on CSI Images of Multiple Reflection Paths
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Fingerprint-based indoor localization methods have become an important technology for indoor localization due to their wide availability, low hardware cost, and fast growing localization needs. In this paper, we propose a method called IMRP-Loc based on channel state information, which uses images of multiple reflection paths information generated by the 2D-MUSIC algorithm as the input for machine learning. We train the machine learning model in the offline phase, and then test it in the online phase. The scheme was successfully implemented in two different classical experimental scenarios and validated with multiple network models, the test results were maintained at high accuracy and the feasibility of using the approach was confirmed by the experimental results.

articleTitle: Wireless Street Lighting Network Optimization to Alleviate Plane Earth Loss
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: With wireless technology is widely used in outdoor lighting control systems, the wireless network performance determines the system operation quality. The lighting pole distance and antenna height influence the wireless performance of the street lighting system due to the plane earth loss. In this paper, theoretical plane earth loss of wireless street lighting systems is analyzed. Then the hybrid wireless street lighting system is presented and the wireless link quality targets are given. Based on theoretical analysis and these targets, simulation with different parameter settings is performed. Therefore, a wireless street lighting network optimizing method by changing the antenna height or pole distance is clearly proposed to enhance the wireless network performance.

articleTitle: Service Based RAN Decoupling Method Based on Graph Theory
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Driven by the higher demand for flexible networks, Service based Radio Access Network (RAN) has been proposed. Service based RAN offers flexible network by decoupling the control plane of monolithic RAN into Network Functions (NFs) and combining NFs flexibly. It is currently unclear how to decouple monolithic RAN. Most decoupling methods can’t avoid the influence of experience. This paper tackles that challenge by proposing a graph theory-based decoupling method. The decoupling method can generate NFs with different decoupling granularities depending on procedures and scenarios. The evaluation shows that the balance between performance and adaptability will be achieved when the decoupling granularity is 4. In the procedures of "RRC (Radio Resource Control) Inactive" and "PDU (Protocol Data Unit) Modification", decoupling result have the same latency performance as the monolithic RAN and provide more flexibility.

articleTitle: Utility Modeling and Optimization Based on Energy Consumption and Latency in Air-ground Integrated Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The integration of communication, caching, and computation in air-around integrated network has become the trend of next-generation mobile communication. Low latency and low energy consumption are considered as the important requirement of next-generation wireless network. In this article, an air-around integrated network framework for joint communication, computation, and caching of multi-subscriber, multi-unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV), and multi-base stations (BS) is proposed. A joint utility function oriented to the latency/rate, energy consumption, and the size of the task caches is constructed. The deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) algorithm is exploited to maximize the utility of mobile network operator (MNO). Finally, the effects of computational ability and cache space on MNO utility are discussed. Simulation results show that the algorithm reduces the computational latency and energy consumption of the subscriber and increases the utility of the MNO.

articleTitle: HarFi: Human Trajectory Recognition Based on WiFi CSI Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In recent years, with the popularity of WiFi devices, WiFi-based non-contact sensing technology has attracted the attention of many researchers. Along with the rapid development of the Internet of Things (IoT) technology, numerous applications based on WiFi wireless sensing technology have emerged. This wireless sensing technology utilizes the channel state information (CSI) of WiFi signals to recognize different human activities by detecting their effects on the WiFi signal. In this paper, we propose HarFi, a human motion trajectory recognition system based on WiFi CSI. HarFi combines the concept of Fresnel zones in indoor wireless sensing to select suitable regions for human activity monitoring. It utilizes the CSI ratio signals to eliminate random phase noise in the CSI signal that cannot be removed by simple filtering techniques. HarFi extracts the Doppler frequency shift (DFS) from the CSI signal and the method of wavelet packet denoising is used to remove the high-frequency noise of the Doppler frequency shift. It generates two types of features: feature images and feature vectors. Different deep learning models are trained using these features to find the best-performing combination. We have implemented HarFi on WiFi devices equipped with Intel 5300 NICs. Real experiments have demonstrated that HarFi achieves an accuracy rate of around 97% in recognizing human motion trajectories.

articleTitle: A Method for Detecting Secret-Key Leaks in Public Container Images on DockerHub
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The leakage of sensitive information, including API tokens and cryptographic keys, has been a significant concern due to its potential risks. While these leaks are not only from source code repositories, DockerHub, the largest container registry due to Docker’s widespread adoption, presents an additional possibility for such exposures. In this paper, we propose a method for detecting secret-key leaks within container images. Employing this approach, an evaluation of approximately 20,000 public images from DockerHub revealed that a random sample showed that around 1.96% of these images exposed over 50 kinds of secrets. Furthermore, 4.68% of the recently added chat application images unintentionally exposed their OpenAI API keys. The research concludes with an exploration of the potential reasons for these leaks, alongside some recommendations for developers to protect their confidential information.

articleTitle: Multi-scale Motion Feature Integration for Action Recognition
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Analyzing video data with intricate temporal structures and extracting comprehensive motion information remains a significant challenge. In this work, we introduce the multi-scale motion feature integration (MMFI) network, which leverages two key modules for motion analysis: the progressive local context aggregation (PLCA) module and the multi-scale motion excitation (MSME) module. The PLCA module captures frame-level motion details by incrementally processing frame-wise differences near the input frame in the early stages of the network. The MSME module provides motion-attentive channel weights in deeper layers with higher dimensions, incorporating short- and long-range segment-level motion information. These modules synergistically capture motion details across various scales. Our approach is evaluated on the large-scale video dataset Something-Something V1, yielding state-of-the-art performance with minimal computational overhead.

articleTitle: Rate Splitting Multiple Access Enhanced Visible Light Communications under Fairness Constraint
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Rate splitting multiple access (RSMA) has been recently proposed for visible light communications (VLC) systems to further increase the spectral efficiency (SE) compared with traditional non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) approaches. However, state-of-the-art RSMA-VLC systems usually utilize optimization algorithms to determine the channel precoding matrix, leading to high complexities in achieving optimality. Despite the computational complexities, another major concern is that these schemes only focused on the weighted sum rate (WSR) without considering the fairness issue among multiple users, leading to poor BER performances for certain users. This is detrimental for VLC where light is adopted to let each user achieve a high data rate. Neglecting fairness problems may result in inadequate information signal rates for some important users within the system, so that the quality of services (QoS) metric cannot be satisfied. To address the QoS issue, this paper introduces a fairness criterion by considering both public and data rates between VLC users. To cope with the increased system computational complexity issue introduced by RSMA-VLC fairness constraint, we proposed a Genetic Algorithm (GA) based optimization method, named GAF-RSMA, to find the optimal precoding matrix. To thoroughly study the WSR performance of GAF-RSMA under signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) constraints, we conducted numerical simulations. Simulations results show that GAF-RSMA outperforms conventional NOMA in terms of SE, while ensuring fairness between VLC users. For different scenarios, RSMA brings up to 15.23% improvements in SE. It is worth pointing out that as the SINR requirement becomes more stringent, i.e., with the increment of minimum SINR constraint, the WSR of the GAF-RSMA system dropped. Our results indicate that the GA algorithm can be applied to achieve an optimal precoding matrix for RSMA VLC systems while maintaining system’s WSR and user’s SINR values.

articleTitle: Improved Impulsive Noise Suppression Method: Joint Myriad Detection and Gaussian Fitting Robust Local Weighted Smoothing
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Impulsive noise is a common impediment in many wireless communication systems, which prevents the system from error-free transmission. To this end, this paper aims to investigate the clipping and robust locally weighted regression (RLOESS) to mitigate the adverse effects of impulsive noise. To improve the impulsive noise suppression performance, a Myriad detection - Gaussian fitting robust local weighted regression smoothing (M-GLOESS) algorithm is designed. The proposed M-GLOESS finds the outliers with the help of the Myriad filter and realizes a better impulsive noise suppression performance by introducing a Gaussian fitting robust correction coefficient diagonal matrix. Simulation results are presented to verify the effectiveness of the proposed M-GLOESS, which is robust to the impulsive noise and has better performance than the traditional algorithms.

articleTitle: Multi-level Classification of Hazards Based on the Hierarchical Topic-wise Model
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The characteristics of large-scale, imbalanced, and hierarchical safety hazard labels pose challenges to the hazard classification. Current methods have not fully exploited the relationships between hierarchical labels and have overlooked the issue with class imbalance. To address these challenges, we propose a hierarchical topic-wise model (HiToM). Our approach aims to improve hierarchical hazard classification by modelling the connections between labels based on their topic features and using a topic-based graph convolutional network to encode the hierarchical structure. Additionally, we apply active learning based on hierarchical structure entropy to optimize the model training process. On a dataset of safety hazard descriptions from a large city, HiToM achieves impressive Micro-F1 (0.7358) and Macro-F1 (0.7101) scores. Our proposed method effectively tackles the class imbalance problem and improves the overall prediction performance compared to other baselines.

articleTitle: Towards Efficient Development for Collaborative and Heterogenous IoT Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The collaboration issue among heterogeneous Internet of Things (IoT) devices is currently a hot topic. The primary obstacle in the collaboration among heterogeneous IoT devices is the disparity in data exchange protocols among applications running on these devices, which hinders efficient data sharing. Existing efforts based on proposed global protocols incur high overhead, while those relying on custom tools designs lack the flexibility to support diverse scenarios and fail to meet the demand for efficient interconnection. In this study, we introduce HDIS, which automates the processes of topology design, glue code generation, and executable file distribution, enabling low-cost and rapid interconnection among heterogeneous IoT devices. We have designed a visual topology arrangement module to reduce the entry barriers while addressing the limitations of single-scenario and non-programmable network topologies. Additionally, we provide automated parsing and compilation model to reduce development costs. Experimental results demonstrate that HDIS outperforms high-level programming code implementations by a minimum of 72.54% in terms of performance.

articleTitle: Integer frequency offset algorithm based on DRM system
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: This article proposes an integer frequency offset estimation algorithm based on time pilot for digital radio mondiale (DRM) systems. This algorithm fully utilizes pilot symbols and effectively reduces the difficulty and complexity of the algorithm by creating a difference set between the predetermined pilot symbols and the pilot symbols recovered from the actual signal at the same carrier position. By using mathematical processing to calculate the variance and then sum the two difference sets at the corresponding carrier positions, the reliability of the algorithm is increased while further optimizing and improving the computational efficiency and accuracy of the algorithm. In order to reduce the randomness of algorithm results, the calculation results of multiple sets of symbols are summarized and statistically analyzed. Compared with traditional integer frequency offset estimation algorithms, the algorithm proposed in this paper has higher accuracy in frequency offset estimation.

articleTitle: Improving Classification Efficiency Based on Combination of Extreme Gradient Boosting and Deep Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The leading causes of blindness and low vision are ocular disease. Ocular disease such as glaucoma, cataract, diabetic retinopathy, and macular degeneration, which are diseases in which the risk of vision loss. Unfortunately, some ocular diseases have no symptoms until the late stages. Therefore, early-stage diagnosis of ocular disease is the best way to prevent vision loss. This work proposed the classification models for ocular disease classification using XGBoost in combination with deep transfer learning of CNN as the feature extractor. In the model training process, we used the pre-trained model including Xception and ResNet50 based on the transfer learning technique to extract different features. The proposed model was used to classify ocular disease into eight patterns. The XGBoost in combination with the ResNet50 model achieved an accuracy level of 87.82%, precision of 88.15%, sensitivity of 87.82%, and F1 score of 87.82%. The XGBoost in combination with the Xception model acquired an accuracy level of 87.02%, precision of 87.35%, sensitivity of 87.02%, and F1 score of 87.02%. By considering the F1 score, XGBoost in combination with transfer learning of CNN models gave a high score. Therefore, all evaluation parameters clearly indicate the high performance of the ocular disease classification model. The conclusion presents that the proposed method acquires more excellent performance than individual deep learning models.

articleTitle: Adaptive Repartition Heuristic for the Two-Echelon Capacitated Vehicle Routing Problem with Backhauls
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Solving the two-echelon capacitated vehicle routing problem (2E-CVRP-B) has shown increasing importance in urban logistics network. This problem involves two types of fleets responsible for satisfying customers’ linehaul and backhaul demands within a two-echelon logistics system. The mainline haulage fleet transports freight between the depot and intermediate facilities (satellites), while the feeder-line fleet operates between satellites and customers. The VRP is a classical NP-hard problem, while for 2E-CVRP-B, the mutual coupling effect of the two echelons further complicates the solving process, especially in the realistic large-scale application scenarios. To address this challenge, we have developed an iterative optimization algorithm with adaptive RePartition and k-opt edge-exchange. The method is able to effectively decompose the two-echelon optimization problems, and adaptively refine the partitioning of the second echelon according to the last iteration results, which contribute to discovering an optimal solution. Comprehensive experiments have been conducted on 2E-CVRP benchmark instances and the results demonstrate the performance advantage of our solution in comparison with alternative methods.

articleTitle: A Hybrid MAC Protocol with Topology and Traffic Adaption for UAV-Assisted Maritime Communication Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a topology and traffic adaptive medium access control (TTA-MAC) protocol for UAV-assisted maritime communication networks. The proposed MAC protocol takes into account the impacts of rapid topology changes and dynamic network traffic in FANETs. In TTA-MAC, a new slot structure and packet structure is firstly introduced to suit for heterogeneous nodes under different working modes. A coordination mechanism is then designed to prevent collision between nodes working at time division multiple access (TDMA) and carrier sense multiple access (CSMA) modes. Finally, we use a deep Q-learning network (DQN) to make decisions on switching between modes. Simulation results shows that the proposed TTA-MAC achieves a better performance in delay and throughput in comparison with CSMA and TDMA when number of nodes reaches 60.

articleTitle: HIFANet: A Hierarchical Feature Aggregate Network for Change Detection of High-Resolution Remote Sensing Images
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Change detection (CD) is a crucial task in remote sensing, requiring high precision and accuracy. Traditional CNN-based siamese network have been successfully applied to CD tasks in numerous research studies. However, these methods still face several challenges. Firstly, mainstream CD networks lack effective image feature extraction capabilities, despite the rich object details present in high-resolution remote sensing images. Secondly, as the networks become deeper, there are issues with the loss of image details and the increasing number of network parameters, which impact training costs. To address these challenges, we propose a hybrid architecture CD network called Hierarchical Feature Aggregate Network (HI-FANet). Through the integration of the Convolution-Involution Module (CIM) and Transformer structures, our approach not only enhances the capability of extracting informative features from images but also addresses the limitation of inadequate feature extraction in existing methods. Moreover, compared to a purely Transformer-based architecture, our hybrid network achieves comparable performance while significantly reducing the number of parameters, resulting in a substantial reduction in the training cost. In addition, our network employs skip-dense connections to facilitate feature fusion, demonstrating superior capability in mitigating the loss of fine-grained image details compared to alternative fusion methods. Furthermore, we introduce the Efficient Attention Predict Head (EAPH) by combining Channel Attention Module (CAM) in a residual way to address semantic differences between features, resulting in better detection results. Experimental results on the CDD and LEVIR datasets demonstrate that our proposed method achieves higher accuracy and F1 scores compared to existing methods.

articleTitle: Joint Delay and Throughput Network Resource Orchestration in SAGIN Based on SDN
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Due to the convergence of rapidly evolving terrestrial, airborne, and satellite communication networks, the space-air-ground integrated network (SAGIN) will be an important architecture to support 6G communications in the future. This architecture can coordinate different levels of networks in real time and dynamically provide efficient and personalized services to users according to different situations. However, due to the complexity and heterogeneity of its architecture, it is extremely difficult to realize resource scheduling and dispatching. In this article, A reconfigurable SAGIN architecture integrated with software defined networking (SDN) is proposed to address the above issues. To further satisfy the quality of service requirements (QoS) of users. The optimization problem of joint unmanned air vehicle(UAV) trajectory design and link selection is formulated for maximizing the ratio between downlink throughput and link delay. Then, the k-means-DDPG (K-DDPG) algorithm is applied to determine the optimal UAV trajectories and links. Finally, simulation results show that the adopted algorithm has good convergence. The performance of the adopted algorithm is significantly better than other algorithms.

articleTitle: UbceNet: An Underwater Image Enhancement Network for Processing Underwater Images
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Due to the exponential attenuation of light propagation in water, underwater images often exhibit poor quality. In this paper, we propose the UbceNet model designed to enhance the quality of underwater images. It comprises two primary modules: image processing and color stretching. In the image enhancement module, significant features within the image are extracted through pooling operations to reduce noise in the feature map. Additionally, we employ Dwise convolution to enhance dimensionality, mitigating the risk of model overfitting. In the color stretching module, we introduce a Coordinate attention and a HardSwish residual enhancement module to enhance color performance by focusing on key image features. Our model outperforms the state-of-the-art models on the dataset, achieving a PSNR metric of 24.04dB and an SSIM of 0.83%. These results highlight the model’s strong performance in optimizing underwater image quality. In the future, this model can serve as the foundation for practical applications such as underwater robot vision, water quality testing, underwater target detection and other fields.

articleTitle: FPGA based I-FIR Non-uniform Filter Banks
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: A low-complexity non-uniform filter bank based on Interpolated-Finite Impulse Response(I-FIR) filter for the receiver in the DVB-RCS2 reverse link is introduced. We firstly demonstrate the efficient I-FIR technique to design the high stopband attenuation prototype filter with a lower order than conventional methods of Equiripple and Least-Squares. Subsequently, we present the structure of I-FIR non-uniform filter bank, illustrating the application of the I-FIR technique in filter bank design. Furthermore, this paper outlines the hardware architecture for the unique I-FIR filter bank. We employ a commutator instead of conventional delay lines and downsampling structures in each path of the filter banks. In the hardware architecture, the commutator can be realized using the IP core known as FIR Compiler, providing significant convenience for obtaining the filter banks. We conduct simulations to evaluate the proposed non-uniform filter bank’s performances and showcase its frequency response. The superiority of the I-FIR technique and benefits of implementing this filter bank for the receiver in the DVB-RCS2 reverse link are demonstrated. In addition, we present an example detailing the computational load and resource utilization of DSP48s and RAMs within the I-FIR filter bank.

articleTitle: A Lightweight Remote Sensing Aircraft Target Detection Network Based on Improved YOLOv5n
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Aiming at the problem that the target detection algorithm based on deep learning has a large number of network parameters and high requirements for computing resources, so that it is difficult to deploy on small hardware terminals. This paper proposes a lightweight remote sensing aircraft target detection network based on improved YOLOv5n, which fuses ShuffleNetV2 and Coordinate Attention (CA) mechanism. Firstly, we replace the Backbone part of the YOLOv5n network with the lightweight network ShuffleNetV2, which works well on target extraction and greatly reduces the model volume of the network; Secondly, we add the CA mechanism of cross-channel information to focus on direction perception and position information, and significantly improve the efficiency of target detection; Finally, in the loss function part, we use EIoU loss to speed up convergence and improve regression accuracy. The experimental results show that on the public dataset MAR20, our lightweight network extremely reduces the parameters by 84.4%, improves FPS by 6.5%, and reduces mAP@0.5 by 4.2% compared with the original YOLOv5n model.

articleTitle: TSSR: A Truncated and Signed Square Root Activation Function for Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Activation functions are essential components of neural networks. In this paper, we introduce a new activation function called the Truncated and Signed Square Root (TSSR) function. This function is distinctive because it is odd, nonlinear, monotone and differentiable. Its gradient is continuous and always positive. Thanks to these properties, it has the potential to improve the numerical stability of neural networks. Several experiments confirm that the proposed TSSR has better performance than other stat-of-the-art activation functions. The proposed function has significant implications for the development of neural network models and can be applied to a wide range of applications in fields such as computer vision, natural language processing, and speech recognition.

articleTitle: A Lossless Compression Method for Event Cameras via Removing Spatial Redundancy
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Event cameras are neuromorphic devices with high temporal resolution, high dynamic range, and low power consumption. However, the event stream data generated by these cameras requires a large amount of storage. To address this issue, we propose a lossless compression method. We encode the event data in a specific format by optimizing spatial redundancy and temporal redundancy of the event sequence data. Our method is based on a multi-level dictionary structure. First, the imaging domain is divided into smaller blocks to reduce the size of data type for spatial coordinates. Second, a novel multi-level dictionary is proposed to remove the spatial coordinate redundancy. Finally, a differential array is used to reduce the timestamps redundancy. Our experimental results on both synthesis and real event data show that the proposed method can achieve a higher compression ratio than the state-of-the-art methods. This proposed method can be useful in applications where event data needs to be compressed and stored.

articleTitle: A Hybrid CNN-GRU model for Session-based Recommender Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In many e-commerce recommendation systems, user profiles are mostly not available. In such cases, the recommendation task considers user behaviors like click sessions or browsing history. Traditional recommender methods often rely on users’ past interactions for recommending user interests, which is difficult to apply to session-based recommender systems. However, these methods perform very poorly on this task. Recently, deep learning techniques such as recurrent neural networks (RNNs) and convolutional neural networks (CNNs) showed outstanding performance in session-based recommendation problems. In this paper, we propose a hybrid CNN and gated recurrent unit (GRU) model that exploits the advantages of both CNN and GRU in modeling the rigid order requirement for interactions inside sessions and modeling the sequential long-term dependencies in session data, respectively. Our proposed hybrid model has two architectures: the first part consists of the CNN layers that take input from Item ID to learn local features and relationships in sessions, and the second part is a GRU layer that takes the output from the CNN layer to learn the long-term dependencies in that session. This hybrid technique enables the architecture for modeling prominent features in the session to provide accurate recommendations. Extensive experiments over a real-world dataset demonstrate that the proposed hybrid model performs well and outperforms those GRU and CNN-based models in the state-of-the-art recommendation task on both metrics used.

articleTitle: Enhancing Distributed Sketch under Path Deviation and Multipath Routing
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Sketch-based method has emerged as a promising approach to network measurement. Yet, implementing sketches presents challenges related to memory resources and flow coverage. Recently, Distributed Sketch, a per-flow measurement method that maps fragments of a network-wide sketch into multiple switches, was introduced to address these limitations. However, this approach assumes that all packets of a network flow are forwarded along a single path, without considering the multipath routing and possible path deviation.In this paper, we investigate the impact of multipath routing on Distributed Sketches and propose a sketch update algorithm for counting packets of per-packet multipath flows. Also, we extend Distributed Sketch so that flows deviating from the planned path are visible. Evaluations on the FatTree testbed show that our scheme can more accurately measure network traffic containing multipath flows and cope with path deviations.

articleTitle: VarLog: Mining Invariants with Variables for Log Anomaly Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The invariants used in existing log anomaly detection usually do not contain the variables. The cause is that the dynamic nature of variables makes it difficult to construct the invariants. However, the variables recorded some valuable information in the log, and constructing the invariants containing the variables allow us to discover exceptions more accurately.In this paper, we propose a novel method to mine the invariant with variables, which we call VarLog. VarLog first obtains associated event sequences with the modified aprioir, then identifies valuable variables and fuses them with associated event sequences to form the invariants. We have built the VarLog prototype system and tested it on the dataset provided by LogHub. The experiments show that VarLog is capable of finding invariants with variables in nine kinds of log.

articleTitle: A generative adversarial network for jamming waveform generation in the non-cooperative scenario
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The generation of interference waveforms is a crucial issue in the field of communication engineering. One of the most challenging problems faced with interference waveform generation is constrained by the lack of annotated data and prior information. This work proposes an effective approach for generating interference waveforms using the generative adversarial network in the scenario without the need for prior information. An additional network as a frequency-domain discriminator is incorporated to enhance the interference effect of the generated waveforms. The experimental results on simulated communication datasets show that the interference effect of the generated waveforms is far superior to the most common noise interference and simultaneously achieves results close to or even superior to matched interference. The interference symbol error rate of the generated waveforms experiences a further improvement after incorporating frequency-domain information for auxiliary training.

articleTitle: A Secure Certificate-Based Aggregate Signature Scheme
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Aggregate signature can aggregate different signatures on different messages from different signers into one single signature and require to be verified only once, this enables batch verification of message signatures. Certificate-based cryptosystems not only can simplify the certificate management in traditional public key cryptosystem, but also overcome the inherent key escrow in identity-based cryptosystem and eliminate lower credibility of trusted third-party in certificateless cryptosystem. Based on the advantages of aggregate signature and certificate-based cryptosystem, this paper proposes a secure certificate-based aggregate signature scheme by using bilinear pairing. Under the computational Diffie-Hellman assumption, it is proven secure. Compared with the previous certificateless aggregate signature scheme, our scheme does not need a secure channel, which is more suitable for the application prospects of wireless sensor networks.

articleTitle: Research on Classification of 5G Network Slicing Security Capabilities
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Network slice security is the prerequisite for introducing network slicing to vertical industries. 5G network support many differentiated slicing security capabilities. So the security capabilities of one slice need to be decided based on customers’ requirements and the security capabilities that the network is capable of providing. However, it’ s not easy for the slice customers or the network operators to choose and provision the security capabilities of one slice based on security requirements. This paper introduces the differentiated 5G network slicing security capabilities, proposes a classification methodology mapping between slice security capabilities and slice security effect. We also shows the potential usage scenarios of this methodology including selecting security capabilities for one slice and decomposition and propagation of slice security related intents during slice life cycle to achieve intent-driven slice security provision.

articleTitle: Optimizing Community Detection in Complex Networks by Regrouping Gateways
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Community detection that can extract potential hidden structures and key information of large-scale complex networks has been studied so many years. However, there exists a possibility of grouping the gateway incorrectly which is the central node communicates with the outside, thus resulting in a large loss of modularity. Here we propose a regrouping gateways (RG) algorithm for community detection to optimize the existing community partitions which have been divided by various algorithms. We design a heuristic optimization algorithm based on a breadth-first search strategy with less complexity than Leiden to improve modularity. Experiments carried out on multiple real networks show that RG exhibits good generality in effectively increasing the modularity and reducing the randomness of community detection algorithms.

articleTitle: Siamese-Based Triple Correlation Operation Fusion Network for Visual Tracking
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Correlation operation plays a crucial role in extracting similar information from template and search image features in the field of visual object tracking. Discriminant Correlation Filters (DCFs) have earned recognition for their efficiency and robustness, primarily attributed to their online training and updating capabilities. However, their performance often suffers due to the limited quality of online training samples. For segmentation-based tracker, semantic features are extremely important for generating accurate target masks. While the cosine similarity operation (CSO) is employed to identify locations in the search image resembling the target feature, it has shortcomings in capturing deep semantic features. In Siamese networks, multichannel location and semantic features are achieved through cross-correlation operations between template and search image features. These multi-channel features are combined with DCFs and CSO to compensate for their respective shortcomings. Consequently, in this paper, we propose a Siamese-based segmentation tracker named SiamTcc, which integrates multiple features from triple correlation operations.

articleTitle: Airport Pedestrian Target Tracking Algorithm Based on Surf and Improved Correlation Filtering
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Tracking target pedestrians in airport terminals has always been a challenge, a pedestrian target tracking algorithm based on surf and improved correlation filtering is proposed. Firstly, the SURF bidirectional matching algorithm is used to automatically identify the surveillance video where the target is located, and the state information of the target in the video image is extracted; Then, the hog feature and the color statistical feature of the target are extracted, and the correlation filter and the foreground background model based on the color statistical feature are trained respectively. The target confidence map is obtained through the feature fusion, so as to predict the location of the target and realize the tracking of the specified pedestrian target. The performance of this algorithm is verified by the comparative experiment with the KCF algorithm; Finally, the effectiveness and real-time performance of this algorithm are verified by the target tracking experiment in the real-time video of the airport terminal.

articleTitle: Mining Insights from Virtual Reality Exergame Reviews with Latent Dirichlet Allocation Method
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The increasing popularity of VR games has sparked a notable surge in interest toward VR exergames, particularly in the context of the COVID-19 pandemic. To uphold the quality of VR exergames and provide valuable feedback to developers, it is imperative to consider the perspectives and concerns of players regarding VR exergames and conduct a comprehensive analysis of their reviews. This study employs the Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) algorithm to effectively discern various topics within reviews, thus elucidating players’ reservations concerning VR exergames. Empirical investigations were conducted using a dataset comprising 15,917 English-language reviews of 16 VR exergames on the Steam platform. The experimental findings unequivocally indicate that players exhibit a favorable disposition toward VR exergames (88.31% vs. 11.69%). The analysis encompasses eight distinct topics including user experience, graphics, music, and gameplay.

articleTitle: Cloud-Chain Fusion Certificateless Authentication Scheme for Secure Distribution of Airborne Software
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: With the continuous increase in the number of civil aviation airborne software, the traditional airborne software distribution method has problems such as high cost, low efficiency, and poor security. Combining cloud storage with airborne software can improve the distribution efficiency of airborne software. However, as a third party, the trust of cloud storage cannot be guaranteed. To address the potential issues of malicious damage and illegal access to airborne software cloud storage, we proposed an architecture model based on cloud-chain fusion and designed an identity authentication mechanism for airborne software security distribution. Moreover, we designed an efficient certificateless signature scheme, which reduces the risk of a single point of failure by using smart contracts instead of traditional KGC to generate partial public and private key. And we optimized algorithm to reduce the verification cost during the authentication mechanism. Our signature scheme was demonstrated in terms of the security and efficiency through simulation and security analysis of Type I and Type II adversaries. Through Comparison with existing studies, it can be found that the proposed scheme has reduced by around 95.6% at most in computational overhead and has reduced by around 25% at most in communication overhead.

articleTitle: Distributed Dynamic Radar Spectrum Allocation for Mutual Interference Mitigation
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Mutual interference among unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV) radars have become a critical concern in modern times. Nevertheless, the conventional static spectrum allocation method widely used in cognitive wireless networks faces challenges due to its limited effectiveness in dynamic environments characterized by the unpredictable nature of obstacle appearances, where the problem of spectrum allocation turns out to be a Markov decision process. To address the aforementioned issues, this paper introduces a novel spectrum allocation method based on reinforcement learning (RL) to effectively mitigate mutual interference between radars by minimizing the long-term interference, and the interference intensity is measured by the noise power. Moreover, the proposed approach adopts a distributed spectrum allocation method based on RL to overcome the curse of dimensionality that arises with the exponential growth of the state/action space caused by an increasing number of radars in the centralized method. Simulation results show that the kernel-based approach reduces the average decision time of this model compared to the traditional approach obased on fully-connected deep neural network. By leveraging the RL-based approaches, the radars can adaptively and intelligently allocate spectrum resources, thus enhancing overall radar performance in dynamic scenarios.

articleTitle: Prompt-Based Few-Shot Text Classification with Virtual Class Representation
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Over the past few years, "Pre-training + Fine-tuning" has been highly successful in Natural Language Processing (NLP) tasks, but it has limitations in few-shot tasks and zero-shot tasks. Recently, "Prompt-based Tuning + Pretrained Language models (PLMs)" has achieved great success in few-shot stage and zero-shot stage, including few-shot text classification. Prompt-based tuning wraps suggestive characters and [MASK] tokens into a raw input sequence. Additionally, Prompt learning uses a verbalizer to map the semantic information of the [MASK] position to the final classification prediction. The verbalizer contains manual verbalizer and automatic verbalizer, etc. However, manual verbalizers are too dependent on human experience and external knowledge, while automatic verbalizers still face significant challenges. In this work, we introduce a novel approach for constructing a verbalizer termed as “virtual class representation”. This method entails assigning a fixed-length sequence of digits to represent each label in the dataset. We train a small-scale randomly initialized embedding mechanism to achieve preliminary semantic information for each class when virtual class representation is introduced into the embedding mechanism. The semantic information of each category is then further extracted by a convolution operation, and the final model regression value is obtained by calculating the similarity between the last hidden state of PLM and the semantic vector of the class. Our extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method on few-shot text classification tasks.

articleTitle: Towards Efficient and Secure Verifiable Aggregation for Federated Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Federated learning is an advanced technique that outperforms traditional centralized approaches in machine learning. It allows participants to keep their data locally and obtain a global model through aggregation. However, this technique introduces parameter exchange processes, increasing privacy risks. In this study, we investigate two privacy concerns: protecting users’ data during training and verifying the accuracy of aggregation results from the server. To address these issues, we propose a verifiable Federated Learning aggregation scheme based on the RSA accumulator. We employ double-masking techniques for secure federated learning and to accommodate disconnected users. Using the RSA accumulator and homomorphic hash function, our scheme offers efficient correctness verification with minimal storage requirements and constant verification time, even with more users. Through experiments and analysis, we demonstrate that our scheme reduces computation and communication costs while ensuring lightweight verifiability.

articleTitle: SLPSO-Based Resource Allocation Strategy for Layered UAVs-Assisted MEC System with MCR-WPT
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Aiming at the problem that the ground terminals (GTs) often suffer from difficulties in energy harvesting and data processing in remote areas, a resource allocation strategy for layered unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs)-assisted mobile edge computing system is investigated in this paper. According to different functions, the UAVs are deployed in three layers. By using a magnetic coupling resonance wireless power transfer (MCR-WPT) technology, the GTs can obtain sufficient energy from the first layer of UAVs equipped with transmitting coils. The computational tasks of the GTs are divided into popular, private, and non-popular tasks. The popular and private tasks are both offloaded to the second layer of popular tasks UAVs (PT-UAVs), while the non-popular tasks are offloaded to the third layer of non-popular tasks UAV (NPT-UAV). The resource allocation problem is formulated as an optimization problem. The optimization objective is to minimize the system overhead by jointly optimizing the PT-UAVs caching policy, the GTs partial offloading factor, the charging time of the GTs, the trajectory of the NPT-UAV, and the bandwidth and computational resource of the system. The suboptimal solution is derived by introducing a social learning particle swarm optimization (SLPSO) algorithm. Simulation results show that the SLPSO algorithm outperforms other benchmark methods in terms of the system overhead.

articleTitle: A Study of Mobile Network Indoor Deep Coverage Evaluation and 3D Visualization
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The traditional test methods of mobile network indoor deep coverage evaluation are introduced. A novel approach, which is based on MR positioning trajectory fitting, combined with operator's B-domain user profiles and O-domain resource data, using big data technologies, is proposed. The key indicators, challenges and corresponding solutions of 3D visualization for mobile network indoor deep coverage evaluation are analyzed. An efficient and cost-effective visualization solution, which automatically identifies Internet map building contours, relates address data to the identified contours, and pre-models the buildings with software Blender, is proposed.

articleTitle: Trajectory Optimization and Resource Allocation for Throughput Maximization of IRS-Aided UAV WPCN
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: This paper aims to maximize the sum throughput of an Intelligent Reflecting Surface (IRS)-assisted wireless powered communication network (WPCN), where the IRS located between several sensors and an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV). The system first performs wireless power transfer to the sensors and then assists forwarding the information of each sensor to the UAV based on TDMA protocol. To address each problem’s non-convexity, we propose an algorithm to obtain the nearoptimal solution. The method of block coordinate descent is used to improve the throughput through joint optimization of allocation of time slot, transmit power of ground nodes, phase shifts of the IRS, and trajectory of the UAV. Simulations show the considerable gain achieved by the joint optimization scheme.

articleTitle: An Iterative Receiving Structure for Polar Coded Serially Concatenated Continuous Phase Modulation
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: This paper proposes a low-complexity iterative decoding scheme for CRC-Polar code and continuous phase modulation cascaded systems. By simplifying the receiver and utilizing Laurent Decomposition approximation algorithm, a low-complexity general approximation algorithm is derived. Furthermore, an algorithm for parameter selection is developed to achieve a balance between simplified detector structure and good bit error rate performance. An iterative receiving structure is designed, by employing iterative processing of soft information, notable improvements in performance are attained, and the CRC is employed as an early stopping condition to prevent superfluous computations. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm in comparison with CRC aided successive cancellation list algorithm.

articleTitle: A Privacy Preserving Federated Learning Aggregation Algorithm for Noise Label
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: To solve the problem that a large number of noise labels lead to the reduction of the efficiency of existing aggregation Algorithmic efficiency and the difficulty of extending existing methods to the privacy protection framework, a noise label oriented privacy protection Federated learning aggregation algorithm PP-ASNL is proposed. This algorithm is mainly divided into two parts: a client-side noise label sample detection model and a server-side model rating aggregation mechanism. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm has higher model accuracy and Rate of convergence than the existing methods.

articleTitle: Dynamic Access Control for LEO Satellite Networks Based on Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite networks play a crucial role in achieving the ubiquitous connectivity. Due to the limited radio resources and large moving coverage area, the access procedure of LEO networks exhibit a dynamic nature. Traditional access class barring (ACB) scheme adopted in terrestrial networks is able to deal with the access conflicts of massive terminals, but is not suitable for LEO networks with fluctuated serving terminals. To this end, a dynamic access control based on reinforcement learning (DACRL) is proposed in this paper to improve the access adaptation of LEO networks. DACRL iteratively conducts the access terminal quantity adjustment and access conflict control. To achieve a fine access terminal quantity adjustment, a deep Q-network (DQN) with state windows is designed to generate the proper access parameters without knowing the number of access users. To relieve the conflict access, reward of the proposed DQN is formulated by obtaining the tradeoff between the access success rate and the average access delay. Simulation results show that, compared with the reference algorithms, DACRL significantly improves access efficiency and is able to satisfy the access requirements of dynamic terminal quantity.

articleTitle: Electricity Price Forecasting in the Electricity Market Using a Multi-Dimensional Time Series Hybrid Model
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Real-time electricity prices are crucial for balancing supply and demand in the electricity market, and predicting them accurately can benefit all market participants. In this paper, we propose a hybrid model based on multi-dimensional time series, which leverages the strengths of Prophet and TimesNet models, and employs ensemble learning to mine the latent temporal information for both short-term and long-term forecasting of real-time electricity prices. The Prophet model can effectively extract the short-term trends and seasonal patterns in the real-time electricity price data, while the TimesNet model can uniformly capture the temporal variations within and across cycles, as well as the long-term periodicity. We evaluate our model on real-world data from Shanxi electricity market from 2020 to 2022, which includes real-time electricity prices and various influencing factors such as market conditions, weather, and renewable energy generation. We compare our model with several baseline models, both single and hybrid ones. The experimental results demonstrate that our model outperforms other models on different time scales, and offers a valuable approach for real-time electricity price forecasting for the electricity market participants.

articleTitle: Multi-label Text Emotion Detection Based on Multi-level Information
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Detecting multiple emotions in text is an important research topic in Natural Language Processing(NLP), which can be widely used in human-computer dialogues, public opinion monitoring, movie and TV evaluations, product surveys and other fields. Therefore, emotion detection based on text has important research significance. There are two problems with existing methods, one is that some methods do not recognize the complexity of human emotions and only use polarity division, which makes it difficult to detect fine-grained emotions; the other is that many works don’t take advantage of the information of text. Based on the above problems, this paper proposes multi-label text emotion detection based on multi-level information (MLI-ED), which composed of multi-level feature extraction module and multi-level feature prediction module. The multi-level feature extraction module extracts feature information from word level, sentence level, and context level, and the multi-level feature prediction module is used for final prediction. The experimental results show that the model proposed has significant improvement on the emotion detection task.

articleTitle: UAV-Assisted Covert Data Collection: When Remote Monitoring Meets Covert Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) assisted remote monitoring and data collection are prevailing applications thanks to its deployment flexibility and strong mobility. To meet security and privacy requirements, this work investigates a UAV-assisted covert data collection scenario, where the collection scheduling, three-dimensional trajectory and transmit power of the involved UAV are jointly optimized while communicating with another UAV receiver in the presence of adversaries. Taking into account the channel uncertainty at the transmitter, the optimization problem is first formulated to maximize the average covert communication rate for the worst case and the average case, respectively. Then, due to the mixed-integer non-convex nature of the optimization problem, the penalty successive convex approximation (P-SCA) scheme is introduced as a solver in association with proper mathematical approximation of some constraints. The numerical results are finally provided to validate the covertness performance of the proposed scheme, which outperforms the baseline who has no information of channel mismatch.

articleTitle: A Fine Granular Relational Reasoning KGQA model Based on Weak Supervised Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Knowledge graph question-answering (KGQA) task aims to provide answers in the form of entities from the knowledge graph for natural language questions. Conventional information retrieval modeling methods focus on controlling the size of the candidate reasoning path set through effective relationship filtering. However, these methods often perform iterative relational reasoning solely based on the overall semantic information of the question, neglecting the local relevance of relationships within the question statement and the value of fine granular information for filtering. KGQA task datasets typically lack annotations for inference paths, and existing weak supervised learning strategies may not effectively eliminate the misleading influence of erroneous reference reasoning paths on model reasoning capabilities. Based on the fundamental ideas of “reducing the size of candidate path sets” and “eliminating erroneous reference reasoning paths,” this paper proposes a knowledge graph question-answering model for fine granular relational reasoning based on weak supervised learning. First, it enhances relationship and path filtering capabilities from a model structure perspective and then, on this basis, improves the model’s ability to differentiate erroneous reference reasoning paths from a supervised strategy perspective. Compared to state-of-the-art KGQA models, the weak supervised fine granular relational reasoning KGQA model proposed in this paper achieves significant performance improvement.

articleTitle: A Server Anomaly Detection Method Based on EWC and LSTM-GAN
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In the realm of server operations and maintenance, anomaly data is often characterized by its rarity, evolving over time with the influx of new data. Models require continuous parameter updates to adapt to these shifting data distributions. To address these challenges, this paper introduces a method for detecting anomalous server data based on Adversarial Learning and Elastic Weight Consolidation (EWCAD-GAN). Firstly, this method employs stacked Long Short-Term Memory networks (LSTM) as both the generator and discriminator, using adversarial training principles to obtain an initial model. Secondly, the Elastic Weight Consolidation (EWC) algorithm is applied to fine-tune the model obtained after adversarial training, bolstering the model’s ability to remember temporal patterns within time- series data. This approach alleviates the difficulties associated with training models on rare anomalous data and facilitates online learning through the use of the EWC algorithm. Experimental evaluations of this method were conducted on two publicly available datasets for intelligent operations and maintenance anomaly detection. The results clearly demonstrate that EWCAD- GAN outperforms other similar methods, achieving significantly higher anomaly detection accuracy while simultaneously addressing the challenges associated with model training and online learning.

articleTitle: Efficient Track Association of Ships through AIS and shipboard Video Fusion via Ad Hoc Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: This paper presents a shipboard equipment-based method that fuses multi-camera and AIS sensing information, enabling intelligent sensing and recognition of encountered ships. This approach maximizes the strengths of both AIS and shipboard cameras, achieving more precise, comprehensive, and rapid sensing of surrounding vessels. To address issues with measurement accuracy and range in existing methods, a dual-camera ship-ranging technique is proposed for spatial localization using video image data. Utilizing multi-camera setups, ship targets are detected and tracked. The ship detection algorithm provides target frame information, which is then used in the dual-camera ranging method to convert ship pixel coordinates into the world coordinate system. To improve track correlation rates, a novel two-branch track correlation network, with an LSTM backbone network, is introduced, enabling ship track correlation through deep learning. By establishing an AIS and video track association model based on deep learning algorithms and creating a ship track association dataset, an efficient and reliable track association process is achieved.

articleTitle: Near-field Channel Estimation for Dynamic Metamaterial Antenna Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The next generation of wireless technology, 6G, will likely incorporate advanced technologies such as extremely large-scale antenna arrays (ELAA) and millimeter wave (mmWave) communication. These cutting-edge features have the potential to revolutionize the way we communicate wirelessly, near-field communication (NFC) can not be ignored in future 6G mobile networks. Compared to far-field communication, the waves that propagate in the near-field region have a spherical wavefront. By utilizing the time agile of DMA and the correlation between near-field guidance vectors, we propose a novel channel estimation algorithm. Compared with the classic two-dimensional (2D) multiple signal classifier (MUSIC) algorithm, this algorithm effectively reduces computational complexity and ensures estimation accuracy. Simulation results show that the proposed channel estimation scheme achieves the expected results.

articleTitle: Research on Real-Time Linux Task Scheduling Algorithm for Multiprocessors Based on Particle Swarm Optimisation
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Schedulability analysis in real-time operating systems is one of the hot research topics in the field. While Linux has become the preferred choice for industrial systems due to its excellent portability, it cannot meet the hard real-time requirements of specific industrial environments as a time-sharing operating system. To address this issue, we introduce the Real-Time Application Interface (RTAI) 5.2 real-time operating system kernel patch and combine it with Linux 4.4.176 to form the RTAI-Linux dual-core real-time system. Building upon this foundation, we proposes a Particle Swarm Optimization algorithm based on Earliest Deadline First (PSO-EDF) to improve task scheduling in real-time Linux multiprocessor environments. This method introduces a metric for evaluating processor utilization, when a new task arrives, it considers the allocation of free processor resources. Compared with the original method EDF, PSO-EDF provides a broader search space with better global characteristics. The algorithm finds the globally optimal scheduling scheme through iteration, which effectively improves the processor resource utilisation and alleviates the task deadline missing problem encountered in the original method to a certain extent, thus improving the real-time task completion rate. Through extensive simulation experiments, the PSO-EDF scheduling algorithm proves that the scheduling model can further improve the real-time performance of the RTAI-Linux system compared with the classical EDF algorithm.

articleTitle: EEG-based Emotion Recognition using Crystal Graph Convolutional Neural Networks with Functional Connectivity and Spatial-Frequency Features
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Convolutional neural networks (CNN) have achieved promising performance in EEG-based Emotion Recognition. However, CNNs focus more on learning local features from regular Euclidean data rather than global features. Recently, graph neural networks (GNN) have received much attention in EEG-based emotion recognition because it can handle both local and global features. The proposed functional connectivity and spatial-frequency feature graph neural networks (FCSF-GNN) can handle both local and global features by combining dynamic functional connectivity between different electroencephalogram (EEG) channels and fixed spatial information (physical connectivity). Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves better recognition performance than the state-of-the-art methods in the DEAP dataset. For the tasks of valence and arousal recognition, the proposed method (using 32 channels) achieves the average accuracy of 96.80% and 96.90%, precision of 96.44% and 97.51%, recall of 96.37% and 97.20%, and f1 scores of 96.36% and 97.33%, respectively. Meanwhile, with only about 30%(using 10 channels) of the EEG channels retained, the method achieved an average accuracy of 97.21% and 96.93%, precision of 97.31% and 97.55%, recall of 96.35% and 97.29%, and f1 scores of 96.78% and 97.39%, respectively.

articleTitle: Research on Multi-Sensor Fusion SLAM Algorithm Based on Outlier Rejection and Boundary Rendering
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: R3LIVE is an innovative laser-visual-inertial SLAM fusion framework. This framework leverages the error-state iterative Kalman filtering method to tightly couple Laser Inertial Odometry (LIO) and Visual Inertial Odometry (VIO) for mutual state optimization. It allows the construction of geometric structures under LIO and texture rendering under VIO, facilitating the real-time reconstruction of dense RGB threedimensional maps of the environment. However, in the VIO subsystem, when laser map points are projected onto image frames, issues such as point duplication, occlusion, and depth discontinuities at edges often arise between adjacent image frames, significantly affecting the precision of the VIO system. To address these challenges, we propose an improved R3LIVE algorithm based on outlier rejection and boundary rendering. Specifically, within the VIO system, we project map points from the previous scan into the camera coordinate system and employ a selection process to retain only those map points with optimal states for visual localization and mapping. In the global mapping thread, we use a pixel-wise comparison with neighboring pixels to identify edge-rendering points based on a specified pixel color difference threshold. For non-edge points, we apply bilinear interpolation for smooth rendering, while for edge points, we use nearest-neighbor interpolation for direct rendering. This approach not only preserves the smooth rendering effect but also mitigates the impact of noise colors on the map, effectively resolving the issue of the appearance of blue points in tree and building edges during the construction of dense point cloud maps.

articleTitle: Intrusion Detection with Set-Valued Classification: Leveraging Dempster-Shafer Theory and Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) are fundamental in fortifying computer networks against security threats. While numerous neural network classifiers have been developed for multi-class intrusion detection, conventional hard partitioning of feature spaces frequently lead to misclassification, particularly near decision boundaries, causing ambiguity. To address these challenges, we propose an innovative evidential classifier that combines deep learning and the Dempster–Shafer (DS) theory for enhanced network intrusion detection. Our classifier consists of three key components: a feature extractor, a D-S theory-based layer, and an expected utility layer, leveraging Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN), and Long Short-Term Memory Networks (LSTM) as feature extractors. The novel approach embraces set-valued classification, where the classifier’s output represents a subset of all possible labels, effectively handling imprecision and ambiguity. We evaluate the performance of our evidential classifier using the NSL-KDD and UNSW-NB15 datasets, demonstrating its proficiency in making cautious decisions. It excels in assigning complex samples to multi-class sets while maintaining high overall accuracy. These results highlight the potential of the evidential deep learning classifier in addressing imprecise intrusion detection challenges, promising a more robust defense against network threats.

articleTitle: A Low-light Image Enhancement Method with Histogram Equalization Prior
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Visual based robot perception methods are usually based on the assumption of normal lighting, so when deployed in low-light environments, they may fail to perceive and even cause serious errors. To address the issue of visual perception failure caused by low lighting, we propose a low-light image enhancement method based on histogram priors. This method is achieved by training an unsupervised generative adversarial network (GAN), which mainly consists of two stages. In the first stage, we designed a generation network based on U-net network, and trained the low-light images after histogram equalization as prior information guidance; In the second stage, we use adversarial loss to minimize the distance distribution between the real light and the output light, and use image level global and local discriminators to determine whether it is true or false. To verify the effectiveness of the proposed method, we conducted a quantitative comparison with the current state-of-the-art methods. The experimental results show that the proposed method outperforms other methods in restoring image features and brightness in real scenes. The value of the Structural Similarity Index (SSIM) tested on the Low-light dataset (LOL) is 0.862, which improves the image quality by 14.8% compared with the value of the EnlightenGAN method. The Mean Square Error (MSE) and Peak Signal to Noise Ratio (PSNR) show improvement by 56% and 18% respectively.

articleTitle: Towards Digital Representation and Evaluation of Cigarette Appearance Based on Computer Vision
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: This study present a computer-vision-based framework for the digitized analysis and evaluation of cigarette appearance defects. First, the YOLOv5s algorithm is utilized for an exhaustive defect detection process, followed by feature extraction across full sample sets. Subsequently, these extracted features are numerically quantified. Building on these quantification, the study introduces a comprehensive digital model aimed at evaluating cigarette appearance quality. Empirical validation is conducted to substantiate the method’s feasibility and effectiveness.
