This research contributes a methodologically digital representation approach for the systematic analysis of cigarette appearance defects, with significant implications for quality control mechanisms within the tobacco industry.

articleTitle: Advancing Towards 6G: Challenges, Key Technologies, and Applications of the Internet-of-Intelligent-Things
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: This paper investigates the critical role of the Internet-of-Intelligent-Things (IoIT) in propelling the evolution toward 6G wireless communication technologies. The ensuing 6G era, characterized by augmented bandwidth, transmission rates, and connection volume, sets the stage for a synergistic interplay between 6G and IoIT. This synergy is envisioned to introduce novel capabilities including energy-efficient computing, endogenous safety and security, ubiquitous intelligence, along with differentiated and refined services. However, the current maturity of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) technologies is yet to meet the practical application demands of the 6G-IoIT paradigm comprehensively. This paper delves into the principal enablers and challenges, shedding light on promising research avenues crucial for the advancement of the 6G-IoIT. Moreover, we propose four prospective use cases: mobile Extended Reality (XR), human digital twins, smart space, and Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) communications, which underscore the multi-faceted benefits and real-world applicability of the 6G-IoIT framework.

articleTitle: Geographical Aggregation of Distributed UAVs for Channel Rendezvous
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: This paper investigates the problem of geographical aggregation in distributed unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) swarms for channel rendezvous. Designing an effective geographical aggregation method is challenging due to the high mobility and restricted geographical sensing range of each UAV. To address the challenge, based on genetic algorithm, gradient descent algorithm, and motion control, this paper formulates a distributed UAV motion model and proposes a novel integrated genetic algorithm and gradient descent for aggregation in motion (IGAGD-AIM) method for the UAV swarms. The simulation results demonstrate that the IGAGD-AIM method can effectively achieve geographical aggregation in distributed UAV swarms, thereby improving the efficiency of channel rendezvous in UAV swarms.

articleTitle: Multi-objective Resource Allocation across Multiple IoT Device Categories in Space-Air-Ground Integrated Network
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Space-Air-Ground Integrated Network (SAGIN) is a crucial component of 6G technology. SAGIN offers a promising solution for Internet of Things (IoT) applications in areas lacking ground network coverage. In data acquisition scenarios, multiple types of IoT devices are utilized to collect diverse data, leading to varying and time-sensitive channel capacity requirements. However, effectively and fairly allocating resources to different IoT device categories based on dynamic requirements remains a challenge. This paper formulates a multi-objective optimization problem to maximize the minimum link capacity for various categories of IoT devices. To solve this non-convex problem, we propose an improved multi-objective evolutionary algorithm for the multi-party fair allocation of resources. It optimizes the deployment location of the UAV and the bandwidth allocation for IoT devices. Comparative analysis against classical algorithms validates the superior performance of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Code Defect Detection Method Based on BERT and Ensemble
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: A code defect detection method based on Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) and ensemble learning was proposed to solve the low accuracy and reliability of the existing neural networks in the task of code defect detection due to insufficient feature extraction and weak generalization ability. This method involves extracting the Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) and the Token depth feature information vector of the source code using the BERT model. Then, the different feature information expressions of text vectors were learned by establishing the heterogeneous multi-base classifiers of such neural network models as Graph Convolutional Networks (GCN), Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), and Bidirectional Long Short-term Memory (BiLISM). Subsequently, the different feature information of text vectors was fused via Stacking ensemble learning for training and prediction. This fusion aimed to bolster the model feature extraction and generalization abilities. As demonstrated by the experimental findings, the proposed method exhibits an enhanced accuracy, showcasing improvements of 7.08% and 11.76% when juxtaposed against VulPecker and SySeVr, respectively.

articleTitle: Cross-Modal Multi-Source Public Data Fusion and Retrieval using Knowledge Distillation Method
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In the burgeoning field of Vision-Language Pretrained Models (VLPs), there is a notable gap in the application and development of these technologies in the Chinese public healthcare sector. Despite the promising advancements of VLPs in English-centric settings, their adaptation for multimodal data fusion in Chinese remains inadequately explored. This paper addresses this lacuna by introducing a specialized Chinese cross-modal data fusion retrieval model, grounded in the framework of knowledge distillation. Utilizing a novel, multi-modal healthcare dataset tailored for the Chinese context, the model is fine-tuned through knowledge distillation techniques to optimize data fusion strategies. The study identifies critical challenges—such as model scarcity, data bottleneck, and cultural-linguistic barriers—hampering the efficient and secure transmission of multimodal data in Chinese healthcare applications. By leveraging knowledge distillation, our approach demonstrates substantial improvements in data retrieval efficiency and security, thus laying a foundational groundwork for future advancements in public data management within the Chinese context.

articleTitle: Intelligent Multi-resources Allocation for Emergency Communications with Limited User Equipment Energy in UAV-assisted Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In wireless system, unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) can play an important role as it can be deployed flexibly to help improve coverage and quality of communication. In this paper, we investigate how a UAV acts as a wireless base station to provide services for a post-disaster area with unknown user distribution. Since the users have different requirements for quality of service, users need to offload some computing tasks to the UAV for processing. Meanwhile, the UAV needs to make an optimal resource decision to meet the requirements of users. By combining optimization of task offloading, bandwidth resource allocation, ground users’ local computing resource allocation and UAV computing resource allocation, an algorithm based on deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) in reinforcement learning (RL) was proposed to minimize the ground users and the UAV energy consumption. Simulation results demonstrate that the DDPG-based resource management scheme can converge at about 100 episodes and compared with the baseline algorithms, the proposed algorithm performs significantly better in terms of energy consumption in post-disaster areas where the distribution of location users is unknown.

articleTitle: Hybrid Optical Wireless Channel and Fiber Channel based High-Throughput Space Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: With the development of space information networks, scientific experiments are becoming larger and more complex, necessitating networks with superior scalability, flexibility, low latency, and high throughput. While the FC-AE-1553 protocol is widely adopted by existing space information networks due to its high reliability and throughput characteristics, wired networks face significant challenges in access node scalability, ease of installation, and maintenance. To address these issues, we propose a high-throughput space network based on a hybrid of optical wireless channels and fiber channels. This network structure can significantly enhance the throughput and flexibility of the network. We also analyze the factors affecting network bandwidth and latency under the new architecture and establish a system simulation model to validate the performance of the new network architecture. we believe that Hybrid Space Networks hold the potential to bolster the development of future space information networks, offering higher bandwidth and more flexible network access capabilities for space science applications.

articleTitle: A object detection method with dynamic real-time constraints
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Object detection techniques have proven their usability in many conventional domains. However, in driverless vehicles, the task of object detection faces new challenges: Driverless vehicles are highly sensitive to real-time performance, but existing object detection methods do not have the ability to sense and comply with real-time constraints in the real world. In addition, most of the existing models are static and cannot make dynamic trade-offs between efficiency and accuracy based on real-time constraints. Based on the shortcomings of the existing techniques, this paper proposes a dynamic network based on Faster R-CNN, which adds short-circuit blocks and routing units with lower computational costs to the existing models, enabling the network to select the appropriate blocks to execute based on real-time constraints. In addition, the network contains a dynamic RPN module that dynamically adjusts the number of proposals to achieve a dynamic balance between efficiency and accuracy.

articleTitle: HiFi-Sim: A High-Fidelity Simulation Platform for Intelligence Assessment of USV
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The Unmanned Surface Vessel (USV) is one of important equipments for river and marine activities. During the development stage, full process simulation plays a key role due to the coupling relationship between the USV sub-systems. Nonetheless, there are few open source platforms available in the community, and existing ones are outdated and not suitable for intelligent evaluation. Thus, we propose this paper to promote our platform, a simulation platform for USV. The biggest feature lies in its high fidelity, mainly manifested in the following aspects. First, a great deal of effort was put into building the river scenes in Unity, where the lighting and rendering characteristics can be well guaranteed. Second, the input and output controls are achieved through Robot Operating System (ROS), which is test-friendly for personnel engaged in unmanned system development. Third, we have developed and imported a large number of sensor plugins in Unity to ensure various types of sensor data, including multiple cameras and LiDARs, and that is vital for evaluating intelligent algorithms of USV. Integration between ROS and Unity is achieved through TCP/IP communication, facilitating data transfer via topic-based mechanisms. Environmental impacts are also taken into account by including water wave, wind and rain scripts in Unity3D. We have conduced some representative experiments of USV to verify its effectiveness, including direct LiDAR odometry and water segmentation.

articleTitle: A Survey of Harnessing Self-Supervision Against Adversarial Attacks
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Nowadays, there has been a strikingly remarkable success in computer vision, owing to the boom of deep learning. Nevertheless, the revelation of adversarial examples has highlighted the reality that even highly potent deep learning models possess fatal vulnerabilities. On the other hand, the abundance of unlabeled data has fueled the surge in self-supervised learning, which has emerged as a prominent avenue for leveraging unlabeled data to enhance model performance. To address adversarial examples, this paper reviews the research results related to adversarial examples from three main aspects, namely adversarial attack, adversarial defense, and the fusion of adversarial defense and self-supervised learning framework, and analyzes the challenges that may be faced by the current research on utilizing self-supervised learning to fortify the adversarial robustness of deep learning model and discusses the prospect of remarkable methodologies on counteracting adversarial attacks and acquiring informative representation from self-supervised learning in the future.

articleTitle: Efficient Order Dispatching and Route Planning for On-demand Delivery
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: On-demand delivery has surged in popularity owing to its capacity to swiftly cater to customers’ immediate requirements and deliver a seamless and efficient delivery experience. However, the potential for improving delivery efficiency through the operations of order handoff and relay has not been considered in the existing related work. To solve this problem, in this paper, we propose an efficient order dispatching and route planning algorithm (E-ODRP) to improve the delivery efficiency for the system profit maximization. Specifically, E-ODRP consists of the online scheduling and the offline preparation algorithm. In the online scheduling algorithm, first, the load-aware greedy algorithm assigns orders to couriers to minimize delivery costs while ensuring that the order loads among couriers does not exceed a threshold value. Second, the proposed fuzzy logic-based path planning algorithm integrates distance, density, deadline metrics of delivery points for the effective scheduling of courier delivery paths. Third, the handoff triggering condition determines the handover area by the discretization method to improve delivery efficiency. In the offline preparation algorithm, the modified K-Means++ algorithm clusters the locations of the historical orders and set the centers of the clusters as the locations of the relay points. The proposed estimated revenue determines the number of the established relay points. We conduct extensive experiments based on real-world data from an on-demand delivery platform in Chengdu, the results show that our E-ODRP outperforms the state-of-art approaches in terms of overall system profit and total driving distance.

articleTitle: Informer-Based Channel Prediction in Wideband Massive MIMO Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) combined with orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) provide orders of magnitude improvements in spectral and energy efficiency. However, user mobility as well as changing environment leads to channel aging that degrades the performance of the system. Therefore, it is critical to perform channel prediction to achieve acceptable system performance. Because of error propagation, in existing methods, the accuracy of channel prediction rapidly decreases as the number of prediction steps rises. To address these issues, we propose a deep learning-based channel prediction algorithm for wideband massive MIMO systems. Specifically, we introduce Informer, its attention mechanism can automatically give greater weights to the historical channel state information (CSI) that offers more valuable insights for prediction. In addition, it can generate channel predictions for multiple future moments simultaneously by using a generative decoder. Further, inspired by the sparsity of angle-delay domain channels, a pre-processor that transforms the space-frequency domain channel response matrix (SFCRM) to angle-delay domain channel response matrix (ADCRM) through inverse discrete Fourier transform (IDFT) is developed at the input of the neural network. This preprocessing reduces the dimensionality of the network input while better capturing the channel features. Simulation results verify the superiority of the proposed algorithms.

articleTitle: A Joint Distributed Computation Offloading and Resource Allocation Scheme for MEC Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Multi-access edge computing (MEC) technology is a potential solution to the conflict between resource-constrained unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and various emerging computationally intensive, delay-sensitive applications of UAVs. In this paper, we study the joint optimization problem of distributed computation offloading and resource allocation in MEC-supported UAV application scenarios, where the task of each UAV can be divided and offloaded to multiple servers deployed in ground wireless access points (WAPs) for parallel processing. To enhance the quality of user experience (QoE) while avoiding excessive optimization, we propose a new user satisfaction function to evaluate the task processing level of MEC network, which respectively scores the actual task processing delay and energy consumption based on different criteria determined by task requirements. We aim to trade off delay and energy consumption by jointly optimizing server selection, computing resource allocation, transmission power control, and task allocation to achieve maximum user satisfaction. The joint optimization problem is formulated as a mixed-integer nonlinear programming (MINLP) problem. To reduce the complexity of the joint optimization problem, it is decomposed into three sub-problems based on the divide-and-conquer approach: server computing resource allocation, transmission power control, and task offloading decision. We propose a three-layer intelligent optimization (TIO) algorithm, which employs the Lagrange multiplier method, the AdaDelta gradient descent method, and our proposed multivariate decoupling-particle swarm optimization (MD-PSO) algorithm to solve the above three sub-problems alternately for gradually approaching the maximum user satisfaction. The numerical results show that our proposed algorithm is significantly superior to the benchmark algorithms in terms of solving speed, accuracy, and stability.

articleTitle: SFC Mapping Algorithm Based on Prediction and Node Resource Ability Awareness
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Service function chaining (SFC) is an important application in network function virtualization (NFV). In this paper, we propose a SFC mapping algorithm based on prediction and node resource ability awareness (SMPRA) to solve the load balancing problem in dynamic SFC mapping. In order to prioritize the deployment of virtual network functions (VNFs) in resource-rich nodes, we adopt three approaches. First, we price the usage cost of a node based on its remaining resources. The less remaining resources a node has, the higher its usage cost. Second, we use deep learning to predict the node's resource status after a number of time steps, and calculate the remaining resources of a node taking into account not only the current node's resource status but also the remaining resources after a number of time steps. Third, we employ the PageRank method, by which the remaining resources of nodes are combined with the importance of nodes in the network topology, to evaluate of node resource more accurately. For our proposed algorithm to be applicable more widely, we support the dependency between the bandwidth change factor and the VNF in the deployment of the SFC. Simulation results show that the proposed SMPRA algorithm can reduce mapping costs and load imbalance effectively compared with the conventional MRACM algorithm.

articleTitle: Drone-assisted Communication for Traffic Load Balancing: Air-Ground Collaborative Perspective
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: This paper studies the Air-Ground Collaborative Traffic Load Balancing (AGC-TLB) problem. Under such a setup, user equipment sets (UEs) perform different tasks requiring different data rates, and the macro base station (MBS) collaborates with several drone base stations (DBSs) to balance the network load condition. The user association and DBSs deployment are jointly optimized. We formulate the AGC-TLB problem as a generalized α-fairness minimization problem. Different load balancing degrees can be achieved with different coefficients α. The studied problem is a mixed-integer nonlinear programming (MINLP) problem that is challenging to be solved. To address this problem, an alternating optimization algorithm is developed. Specifically, the user association is solved by penalty-based successive convex approximation (P-SCA), whereas the DBSs deployment is modeled as an exact potential game. We analyze the existence of Nash equilibrium and propose the constrained Gibbs-sampling algorithm. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm can achieve a load-balanced network condition compared to benchmark algorithms.

articleTitle: Implementation of a Low-Complexity Pre-Equalizer for Visible Light Communications
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Recent years have witnessed the rapid development of visible light communications (VLC) for next-generation wireless applications due to its wider bandwidth, higher security, and better electromagnetic immunity compared with conventional radio frequency (RF) microwaves. Although state-of-the-art VLC systems can achieve Gbps data rates by employing equalization schemes, designing a general low-complexity VLC transmitter with hundreds of MHz 3-dB bandwidth is still challenging due to the narrow modulation bandwidth nature of light emitting diodes (LEDs). In this paper, we first present a second-order equivalent circuit model for the LED, based on which we propose a general second-order equalizer (GSE) with low complexities, consisting of less than 5 passive capacitors, inductors, and resistors. We show that the GSE can enlarge the LED transmitter’s bandwidth to a few hundred MHz. To validate our GSE, we build a broadband VLC transmitter using commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS) red LED, whose bandwidth is 7 MHz. Experimental results show that our proposed GSE can extend the transmitter’s 3-dB bandwidth from 7 MHz to 546 MHz. Furthermore, we demonstrate that our proposed GSE transmitter in a VLC system can achieve 400 Mbps data rates at a distance of 250 cm with a bit error ratio (BER) below the forward error correction (FEC) limit 3.8×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−3</sup>, by employing non-return to zero on-off keying (NRZ-OOK) modulations. Going forward, to demonstrate the feasibility of our GSE transmitter in practical IEEE 802.11bb systems, we will combine the GSE transmitter with a 320 MHz WiFi board to test its performance with high-order OFDM modulations.

articleTitle: Chaotic Analysis of Pedestrian Flow Series for Vehicular Networking in Complex Interaction Environment
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Interaction between self-driving cars and pedestrians is a key issue for the design of vehicular networking and auto-drive algorithms. Pedestrian movement usually exhibits irregular and complex behaviors, dramatically increasing the difficulty of such design. By choosing a suitable method to analyze the pedestrian flow and obtain its major features, self-driving cars and service robots could intelligently avoid collision with pedestrians. Therefore, this paper analyzes the chaotic characteristics of the pedestrian flow time series of different locations in real campus scenes qualitatively and quantitatively. The optimal delay and optimal embedding dimension of pedestrian flow time series are obtained by the mutual information method and Cao’s method, respectively. The largest Lyapunov exponent, correlation dimension, and Kolmogorov entropy are used to quantitatively analyze its chaos, and recurrence plot is used for qualitative demonstrations. According to this study, pedestrian flow time series are definitely chaotic, which provides essential theoretical support for pedestrian flow prediction and auto-drive algorithm design in future vehicular networking.

articleTitle: Dynamic Task Scheduling in LEO Satellites Mega-constellations: A Domain-based Perspective
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite mega-constellations have become an essential part of future networks to achieve global coverage. With the significant development of edge computing, LEO satellite mega constellations are becoming capable of on-orbit computing. To address the constraints imposed by limited computing resources, satellite cooperative task scheduling has become a promising paradigm. However, most of the existing studies focus on small-scale task scheduling between neighboring nodes. They do not fully reflect the large-scale characteristics of mega constellations. Therefore, we consider a computational domain-based architecture. Based on this architecture, we investigate a scheme for solving large-scale task scheduling in LEO satellites mega-constellations, which enables intra- and inter-domain task scheduling optimization. Specifically, we use a reinforcement learning-based approach to obtain the lowest task processing cost in intra-domain scheduling. For inter-domain task scheduling, we balance the load of each computational domain from a global perspective. Then, considering the strong correlation and continuity between intra-domain scheduling and inter-domain scheduling, we propose the SAC-GALB algorithm. Numerical results verify the effectiveness and superiority of the scheme.

articleTitle: A Hierarchical Reservation Adaptive Evolutionary Algorithm Based on NSGA-II for Multiobjective Optimization of Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In network scenarios where 5G and cloud computing are deeply applied, reasonable deployment of VNFs, rational routing and spectrum allocation in elastic optical networks are all conducive to optimizing the resource allocation of the entire network. The multi-objective optimization model obtains a set of service function chain deployment and link mapping strategies by considering multiple factors to provide a comprehensive solution. In this paper, a five-objective optimization model is established to minimize node resource consumption, link maximum frequency slot number, node load difference, unreliability of deployed nodes and mapped links, and service source-to-destination propagation delay. On this basis, a hierarchical reservation adaptive evolutionary algorithm based on the NSGA-II is proposed to solve the proposed optimization model. The algorithm adopts a combined method to jointly code the node selection scheme and the link mapping scheme, and integrates a hybrid initialization method to generate an initial population that consider both diversity and convergence. To improve the global optimization ability of the algorithm, we add a two-stage crossover mechanism, a dominated solutions hierarchical retention mechanism, and a last-ranking elimination mechanism when the solutions are not dominated by each other, as well as a neighborhood correction mechanism for illegitimate solutions and a two-stage flip-flop strategy for jumping out of the local optimum. The simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: High-precision Alignment System Based on Sub-pixel Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In the field of intelligent manufacturing and precision machining, realizing the precision positioning and alignment process of components is an essential step. High-precision automatic alignment system plays an important role in improving product production efficiency and machining accuracy, which is the key guarantee for efficiency and quality. With the development of micron-level and submicron-level processes in the fields of precision electronics industry and micro-nano manufacturing, the alignment accuracy of the alignment marks on the two masks has also put forward higher requirements. Therefore, how to realize the mask high-precision alignment becomes the key to accuracy. In order to meet the requirements of high accuracy and high real-time performance of the alignment system, this paper proposes an improved sub-pixel edge detection algorithm for Franklin moments based on analyzing the existing Franklin moment edge detection algorithm. And a new high-precision alignment system is proposed by combining it with the PowerLink protocol. Experiments show that compared with other alignment systems, the system proposed in this paper is easier to deploy and can meet the accuracy requirements.

articleTitle: A Domain Generalization Methodology for Side-channel Attack
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Side-channel attacks have been proven to be effective for retrieving secret keys by exploiting implementation vulnerabilities in encryption function. In recent years, deep learning techniques have been integrated into profiled side-channel attacks to achieve outstanding results. However, most state-of-the-art work only conducts attacks under ideal conditions where the profiling device (template device) and the target device are identical. The profiling traces are from the profiling device and the attack traces are from the target device. Unfortunately, constructing a template device is challenging and a flawed template device will lead to discrepancies between the profiling and the target devices. This inconsistent data distribution and discrepancies hamper the profiled SCA. To address these issues, we propose a domain generalization-based side-channel attack architecture called DGSCA. Especially, We simulate a scenario where the acquisition of target data is challenging and can’t be used for model training. Initially, we combine the Deep CORAL method with Mixup to deserve domain invariant representations across source domains. Subsequently, we integrate meta-learning into the DGSCA framework to enhance the model’s generalization ability, which is accomplished by randomly partitioning the source and target domains and leveraging the knowledge gained from the source domain to improve the attack result in the target domain. Moreover, we implement four different deep learning models (MLP, CNN, ResNet, DenseNet) and evaluate the DGSCA framework using the publicly available ASCAD dataset. The experimental results on the ASCAD desynchronous dataset show that our method successfully recovers the key within 1665 traces and demonstrate the scalability and generality of our proposed framework.

articleTitle: A DQN-Based Fair Coexistence Scheme for NR-U and WiGig in Unlicensed mmWave Bands
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: With the rapid development of mobile communication technology, millimeter wave (mmWave) bands have been exploited for data communication, making the new radio in unlicensed spectrum (NR-U) network attractive. However, it faces the challenge of friendly coexistence with the existing Wireless Gigabit (WiGig) network. And in the coexistence scenario with multi-user multiple-input multiple-output (MUMIMO), the conventional spectrum sharing schemes are not efficient and effective. To address these problems, we propose a Deep Q-learning (DQN) based fair coexistence scheme that aims to maximize the sum data rate of the NR-U network while satisfying the fairness requirement for its coexistence with WiGig. Specifically, we design the fairness constraint according to the Jain fairness index, and formulate the constrained Markov decision process (CMDP). Then, the Lagrangian duality method is used to transform the hard constraint into soft constraint. And based on the deep reinforcement learning (DRL) technique, the CMDP is integrated into an adaptive fair constraint DQN (AFC-DQN) algorithm to achieve the fair coexistence. Finally, simulation results show that the proposed scheme outperforms the conventional Listen-Before-Talk (LBT) mechanism in terms of data rate and fairness performance.

articleTitle: EM-CNN-BiLSTM: Causality extraction based on Electra and Dual-Stage Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Event causality extraction (ECE) is the task of extracting event-causal pairs and their structural event information from plain text. However, the accuracy of implicit causal relationship extraction in ECE is low, and how to fully mine the causal semantic relationship within sentences is still a problem in the case of limited samples. Therefore, this paper proposes a causality extraction model (EM-CNN-BiLSTM) based on Electra and dual network fusion. First, the input text sequence is converted into a word embedding vector to obtain the word vector representation of the text. Subsequently, the feature information is generated by a dual-network fusion model, which includes two TextCNN convolutional neural networks for capturing local features, and a bidirectional long-short-term memory network (BiLSTM) for capturing contextual information of sentences. Finally, the context vector is regularized with the dropout technique and mapped to the final classification result using a linear layer. In order to further improve the accuracy of causality extraction, a dual-stage attention mechanism based on features and timing (DAM, dual-stage attention mechanism) is introduced, which are channel attention mechanism and timing attention mechanism respectively, to enhance the model's understanding of important features and the ability to extract historical key information. Through a large number of experimental verifications on the public dataset SemEval-CE, the results show the effectiveness of the model in the task of causality extraction.

articleTitle: Stock Price Prediction Based on Non-Stationary Transformers Model
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In recent years, a growing number of investors and researchers have been applying deep learning techniques to stock price prediction in the stock market, yielding promising predictive outcomes. This study employs the newly introduced deep learning model, Non-Stationary Transformers, for stock price forecasting. This model extends the Transformer architecture by incorporating a Series Stationarization module and a De-stationary Attention module. This augmentation not only enhances the predictability of stock price time series data but also effectively harnesses the temporal modeling capabilities inherent in deep models. To demonstrate the effectiveness of the Non-Stationary Transformers model in stock price prediction, we conducted prediction experiments and backtesting experiments, comparing it with four other deep learning models. The prediction experiments revealed that the Non-Stationary Transformers model outperformed others, yielding the lowest Mean Squared Error (MSE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), and Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) values. Furthermore, the backtesting experiments also demonstrated that the Non-Stationary Transformers model achieved the highest Return Ratio, Sharpe Ratio, and an appropriate Max Drawdown. Both sets of experiments indicate that the Non-Stationary Transformers model provides reliable guidance for investors in making stock market investment decisions.

articleTitle: Joint User Selection and Power Allocation for Coexistence in Unlicensed mmWave Bands
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: To meet the spectrum demand for the rapid development of mobile communication technology, the use of the 60GHz unlicensed band is a promising solution, making the new radio in unlicensed spectrum (NR-U) and wireless gigabit (WiGig) attractive. However, achieving the friendly coexistence of networks belonging to different operators is a challenge. In addition, for these millimeter wave (mmWave) networks, it is also a challenge to realize spatial reuse while reducing conflicts. To address these problems, we first design a receiver assisted scheme for the multi-beam networks to access the channel, which can effectively detect transmission conflicts. Then, to further improve the network sum rate, a joint user selection and power allocation (JUSPA) algorithm is proposed. It can help the base station to make the optimal transmission decision and reduce the interference between different communication links. Both the optimal user selection and power allocation are obtained by the optimization method. And simulation results verify the effectiveness of the JUSPA scheme.

Author Keywords: joint user selection and power allocation

articleTitle: KG-ADS: A Log Anomaly Detection Assisted Decision-Making with Support of Knowledge Graph and Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: There are various methods for log anomaly detection, and different methods have different performances in accuracy, recall rate, and F1 score when they process the different logs. There is often a difficulty in decision-making for log anomaly detection. This paper proposes KG-Ads which is an assisted decision-making with the support of knowledge graph and reinforcement learning , which is designed to reduce the difficulty of applying log anomaly detection. With the support of knowledge graphs, KG-Ads holds a log anomaly detection knowledge which contain 22015 entities, and 11837 relationships, and 118 relationship models. KG-Ads builds an inference engine based on reinforcement learning, and produce recommended policy with the support of the log anomaly detection knowledge base. Our experiments show that KG-Ads is able to provide the suitable policies which are comparable to known policies in the existing work.

articleTitle: A RIS-Aided MIMO Secure Communication Scheme Based on Subarray Partition
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Subarray partition of reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) can significantly reduce the computational complexity of solving optimal reflection coefficients. However, there is no research about the RIS subarray partition of RIS-aided multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) communication for the eavesdropper scenario. In this paper, we intend to solve the optimization subarray partition problem for the eavesdropper scenario, design a RIS-aided MIMO secure communication scheme based on subarray partition (RSC-SP). We consider minimizing the number of subarrays while satisfying secrecy rate requirements. First, this problem is described as a nonconvex combinatorial optimization problem, then we solve it by combining alternating optimization and bisection. In this scheme, we derive the closed expressions of the optimal transmit covariance matrix and the optimal reflection coefficients of RIS. The alternating optimization algorithm is used to jointly optimize the transmit covariance matrix and the reflection coefficients of RIS, the bisection method is used to calculate the minimum number of subarrays. Simulation results show that compared with the traditional scheme without subarray partition, RSC-SP can significantly reduce the computational complexity while meeting secrecy rate requirements.

articleTitle: Rootkit Detection Mechanisms for Linux Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In order to enhance the detection of Rootkits present in the Linux system, this study conducted an in-depth analysis of existing Rootkit principles and proposed a precise Rootkit detection mechanism based on Kprobe technology. This mechanism utilizes instrumentation at relevant function execution points within the Linux kernel to obtain a reliable and accurate kernel-level view. Additionally, it combines audit tools to obtain a user-level view, allowing for the detection of hidden Rootkit presence through cross-view comparison. During the experimental phase, mainstream Rootkits were employed to test the effectiveness of this mechanism. The experimental results demonstrated outstanding detection capabilities of the proposed mechanism.

articleTitle: Research on real-time dispatching of urban rail transit based on blockchain
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: On the Metro lines, subway train scheduling varies with some trains experiencing delays and others operating on a regular schedule. The adjustment of timings between these two categories of trains is crucial. Different strategies are required for adjusting travel times and dwell times, making the subway system more complex than urban metro routes in such scenarios. In terms of train scheduling algorithms at stations to ensure reliability, this paper proposes a block-chain-based subway scheduling design based on foundational data including the initial operational schedules of subway trains, dwell times at various stations, and travel times between stations.

articleTitle: Reinforcement-Learning-Based Scheduling for Age of Information Optimization in MEC Multi-User Network
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In this paper, we consider an optimization problem in a mobile edge computing (MEC) multi-user network for collecting fresh information under bandwidth and energy constraints. We use the popular metric Age of Information (AoI) to measure the data freshness. To solve the age optimization problem, we first relax the bandwidth constraints, and then decouple the problem, where each sub-problem is formulated into a constrained Markov decision process (CMDP) problem. Due to the fast mobility of the users, the distribution of channel state information and size of raw data is difficult to obtain for the base station. To overcome the unknown channel statistics challenge, we introduce a Reinforcement-Learning-based Q-learning algorithm to learn the channel information, which helps to guide the optimal scheduling decision. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm can achieve the better AoI performance compared with other traditional algorithm while satisfying bandwidth and energy constraints.

articleTitle: Vulnerable Nodes Identification Algorithm Based on Virtual Loop Dependence in Power Communication Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: With the deepening of coupling between power communication network (PCN) and power system, the failure of PCN will seriously affect the safety and stability of the power system. This paper finds that PCNs have the high clustering coefficients characteristic. Based on this, the paper proposes the vulnerable nodes identification algorithm of PCNs based on virtual loop dependence (VLD), which considers information from three perspectives: the global location, the inter-node relative relationship and the neighborhood topology, to obtain the node vulnerability score. From the global perspective, VLD considers the node core position in the network and proposes the relative position centrality to weak the rich club. From the local perspective, VLD constructs virtual edge dependence and determines the node criticality by combining the influence of loop structure on dependence reduction. Finally, VLD ranks nodes by the vulnerability score. The paper simulates and analyzes six PCNs. By comparing with seven different algorithms, it is proved that the VLD algorithm can distinguish the similar nodes in a finer manner. Through the network efficiency loss and the network robustness decrease after attacking the critical nodes, the VLD algorithm in this paper is proven to be more accurate and more effective.

articleTitle: Joint Resource Allocation and Scheduling Optimization in Wireless Time-Sensitive Networks Based on IEEE 802.11
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Time-Sensitive Networking (TSN) is an emerging solution for deterministic transmission of time-sensitive services in wired/Ethernet and wireless networks and is considered to be the next generation of Ethernet. Due to the dynamic nature in its physical layer, wireless communications in general and wireless TSN (WTSN) in particular face more technical challenges than wired transmission. This paper proposes a wireless dynamic flow scheduling algorithm that is coined as PA-WTSN and deals with joint power and resource allocation based on OFDMA channel access. The algorithm is formulated as a mixed integer linear programming (MILP) problem with time sensitivity constraints and consideration of power allocation which is necessary for time-varying wireless channels. With the proposed algorithm, the end-to-end delay is optimized. and the effectiveness of the algorithm is validated by simulation.

articleTitle: A Sum-Difference Amplitude-comparison Direction-Finding Method Using 5G RSS
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In order to solve the problem of limited distance of traditional ratio amplitude direction finding, based on 5G-RSS, this paper adopts the idea of multi-information fusion passive direction finding, which is more effective than single-information passive direction finding, and designs a multi-information fusion radio direction finding system adapted to the communication signals of the 5G frequency band, Sum-Difference Amplitude-comparison Direction-Finding Method Using 5G RSS. Whilst the distance information obtained using RSS fuses with the angle information obtained by taking the monopulse amplitude comparison angle measurement algorithm to obtain the final direction-finding results via the 5G-RSS measurement module and the antenna array module. Through simulation, the effectiveness of this vectoring method in a 2-D surface array in a 5G environment is confirmed. Through using the range information provided by 5G-RSS, the final results indicate the method has superior differential beam performance and can cover a range of up to 60km with an accuracy of 0.01 radians. Compared to traditional direction-finding, the proposed 5G-RSS and sum-difference direction-finding method effectively extends the range of direction-finding and positioning while maintaining flexibility, providing a new idea for the traditional, distance limited, 5G radio positioning research.

articleTitle: Imitation Learning based Alternative Multi-Agent Proximal Policy Optimization for Well-Formed Swarm-Oriented Pursuit Avoidance
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Multi-Robot System (MRS) has garnered widespread research interest and fostered tremendous interesting applications, especially in cooperative control fields. Yet little light has been shed on the compound ability of formation, monitoring and defence in decentralized large-scale MRS for pursuit avoidance, which puts stringent requirements on the capability of coordination and adaptability. In this paper, we put forward a decentralized Imitation learning based Alternative Multi-Agent Proximal Policy Optimization (IA-MAPPO) algorithm to provide a flexible and communication-economic solution to execute the pursuit avoidance task in well-formed swarm. In particular, a policy-distillation based MAPPO executor is firstly devised to capably accomplish and swiftly switch between multiple formations in a centralized manner. Furthermore, we utilize imitation learning to decentralize the formation controller, so as to reduce the communication overheads and enhance the scalability. Afterwards, alternative training is leveraged to compensate the performance loss incurred by decentralization. The simulation results validate the effectiveness of IA-MAPPO and extensive ablation experiments further show the performance comparable to a centralized solution with significant decrease in communication overheads.

articleTitle: Personalized Federated Learning with Neighbor Aggregation for Traffic Flow Prediction
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: As an important part of Intelligent Transportation System (ITS), traffic flow prediction has attracted more and more attention from academia and industry. However, since traffic flow data are distributed among different organizations, traditional centralized learning methods are no longer applicable, thus federated learning has begun to play an important role in traffic flow prediction tasks. In this paper, we design an improved traffic flow prediction model based on federated learning. At the same time, we consider the interaction of topology and feature space between traffic data owned by different organizations, and propose a method named Federated Neighbor Aggregation (FedNe). The server update the model parameters with both the physical connectivity and similarity relationships between the organizations, and finally generate a personalized model for each organization. Experimental results on real-world dataset show that our proposed method has the lowest average MAE and average RMSE. Finally, based on our method, when new clients participate, they can also quickly obtain their personalized models.

articleTitle: Image Classification of Alzheimer’s Disease Based on ViT-Random Forest Model
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Alzheimer’s disease is a cognitive disorder that often occurs in the older. Detecting and treating Alzheimer's disease in its early stages can be effective in alleviating the symptoms. This paper proposes an innovative method, using the ViT-Random Forest model to classify Alzheimer’s different stages based on brain images. The ViT-Random Forest model has significant advantages, achieving a 90.3% accuracy and 95.8% recall rate on the test set. With higher accuracy, its training time is also reduced compared to traditional models. This work demonstrates the validity of the ViT-Random Forest model, emphasizing the importance of data preprocessing. It has been proven that using pre-trained ViT models of transfer learning as a feature extractor of unsupervised learning has a significant improvement in speed, and the differences between the source domain and target domain have not reduced the effectiveness. This matters in boosting the effectiveness and accuracy of early Alzheimer's disease screening.

articleTitle: Enhancing Distributed Graph Matching Algorithm with MPI RMA based Active Messages
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Traditionally, most parallel graph algorithms have been implemented based on the BSP paradigm and using MPI two-sided communication as the underlying communication method. However, for certain graph algorithms characterized by irregular communication patterns and complex operations on remote processes, the BSP model cannot effectively exploit the algorithm's inherent asynchrony. In contrast, the model based on active messages is better suited for implementing flexible, scalable, and highly concurrent graph algorithms. In this study, we optimize graph matching algorithm that are widely applied in fields such as sparse linear algebra, community detection, and graph partitioning using the active message paradigm. Additionally, we have developed the portable active message framework RMA-AM, built on MPI RMA operations. What sets our framework apart from other active message frameworks is that it is based on a process-based asynchronous progress model, addressing the multithread overhead issue typical of traditional thread-based approaches. The evaluation results on Tianhe-2 demonstrate that our proposed optimization achieves a speedup of up to 5.1x compared to traditional BSP-style implementation based on MPI two-sided communication, and a 3x speedup compared to traditional BSP-style implementation based on MPI one-sided communication.

articleTitle: Electricity Strategy Optimization for Industrial Users with Real-Time Price Estimation in the Electricity Market Transition
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Industrial users need to optimize their electricity consumption strategy under the dynamic real-time electricity prices in the electricity market transition. This paper presents a method that integrates real-time electricity price prediction and multi-objective optimization for this problem. The method employs a deep learning model based on TimesNet to forecast the future real-time electricity prices and then formulates a multi-objective optimization model that allocates the electricity consumption for various types of industrial loads in different time periods according to the predicted prices and users own load demand. The method applies AMOPSO-MD algorithm to solve the model and obtain a set of Pareto optimal solutions. The method is evaluated by simulations based on the real data of magnesium industry, and validates the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Distributed TSN Time Synchronization Algorithm with Increased Tolerance for Failure Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The integration of Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) and Time-Sensitive Networking (TSN) enables efficient and reliable real-time communication and control. Currently, one of the current research hotspots in the field of TSN is the improvement of reliability in the use of IEEE 802.1AS(IEEE Standard for Local and metropolitan area networks - Timing and Synchronization for Time-Sensitive Applications). On one hand, IEEE 802.1AS does not provide specific steps for constructing redundant clock trees, and on the other hand, it cannot detect error time values caused by the failure propagation of devices on the clock tree. To address these issues, this paper proposes a Distributed time synchronization strategy based on IEEE 802.1AS(DAS). DAS utilizes a broadcast-based message exchange, and each endpoint device calculates its own synchronized time using fault-tolerant time synchronization methods. Furthermore, the time information is no longer embedded in data packets, avoiding the impact of erroneous time values on the time synchronization of other devices. Extensive simulations and on-board verifications are conducted on the DAS algorithm in this paper. The results show that the DAS algorithm can tolerate more failure scenarios while maintaining similar time synchronization accuracy compared to IEEE 802.1AS. Although the DAS algorithm consumes more bandwidth, this overhead is acceptable in small-scale networks. As far as we know, our work is the first in the industry to simultaneously achieve compatibility with existing 802.1AS and distributed TSN time synchronization, and to physically implement it in switch.

articleTitle: Dual-Structure Regularized Sparse Bayesian Learning Channel Estimation for RIS Assisted Wireless Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) technology, as a revolutionary potential key technology for 6G, presents innovative avenues for wireless communication technology. Channel estimation stands as a fundamental and pivotal aspect of RIS assisted wireless communication systems, however, it becomes a complex challenge due to the integration of a large number of passive RIS elements. In this paper, we exploit the dual-structure (DS) sparsity of multi-user equipment (UE) cascade channels and propose a novel channel estimation algorithm based on hyperparameter regularized Sparse Bayesian Learning (HRSBL). We divide the cascade channel estimation problem into two stages. In the first stage, the position index of the dual-structure sparse channel matrix is estimated. In the second stage, we estimate the position index of the first stage is used as the channel prior information, and then HRSBL is applied to estimate the cascade channel matrix. Simulations substantiate the feasibility of this algorithm, showcasing its ability to significantly reduce pilot overhead.

articleTitle: An Effective and Head-Friendly Long-Tailed Object Detection Network with Improving Data Enhancement and Classifier
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Supervised learning methods achieve good results in large amounts of data and balanced data scenarios. However, the real world often has unbalanced data, such as long-tail distribution data sets, where the number of head categories is far exceeds the number of tail categories. Because the amount of tail data is small, using traditional supervised training methods will cause the model to be biased towards the head category. Therefore, when optimizing model performance, we often consider preventing bias from causing difficulty in improving model performance. A common approach is to balance the performance of the head and tail categories to achieve the purpose of improving the performance of the tail category and the overall performance of the model. Such approaches make a complex trade-off between the head and tail categories. Based on the above observations, we propose a head category-friendly long-tail object detection network (EHFL), including a data enhancement module (DEM) and a classifier enhancement module (CEM), and propose a decoupled performance adjustment strategy (DAS) for training, which can decouple the optimization of head category and tail category performance. In DEM, we propose using label information to generate training data to improve some categories’ performance. In CEM, we propose a classifer enhancement loss function to improve overall performance. Experimental results show that it reaches 26.48% on the LVIS-v0.5 data set, improving overall performance without reducing the performance of the head category, which is better than state-of-the-art methods.

articleTitle: Non-Contact Realtime Vital Signs Monitoring System Based on Millimeter Wave FMCW Radar
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Accurate measurement of respiration and heartbeat is crucial for assessing the normality of cardiopulmonary activity. This study proposes a novel real-time human vital signs detection method using a 77 GHz frequency-modulated continuous wave (FMCW) millimeter-wave radar. We measure the chest displacement caused by respiration and heart rate in the human body and transmit the collected measurement data to a PC via the UART data port. Subsequently, the data undergo preprocessing. We employ the vector averaging cancellation (VAC) method to remove static clutter and utilize linear interpolation to suppress potential pulse noise. Moreover, we extract the phase information from the signals. During the frequency estimation of the heartbeat signal, we analyze the signal energy to address motion artifacts and mitigate the interference caused by body movement on heart rate estimation. To reduce estimation errors in heart rate, we selectively filter out the respiratory second harmonic component when appropriate, avoiding the strong influence of respiratory signals and their harmonics on heart rate estimation. The determined respiration and heart rate values are then displayed in real-time on the PC. Experimental results demonstrate that this real-time vital sign detection system maintains high detection accuracy while ensuring real-time capability.

articleTitle: Incorporating Speaker’s Speech Rate Features for Improved Voice Cloning
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: We investigate a neural network-based text-to-speech (TTS) synthesis system that aims to simulate the Mandarin voice of different speakers using short voice samples. Our system introduces new attempts in two key parts.: (1)Unlike prior studies, we not only capture the unique voice characteristics of each speaker but also integrate a speaker feature extraction model to improve our model’s effectiveness. Importantly, we utilize a duration model for accurately capturing the speech rate and rhythm of each individual, thus allowing our synthesized speech to demonstrate enhanced realism and credibility.(2) Based on the Tacotron model, we combine additional properties such as "speech rate" and "D-vector" to generate mel spectrograms from a given text, thereby enhancing the ability to clone through mechanisms such as location-sensitive attention. This ensures the quality and authenticity of the synthesized speech. Experiments have shown that this innovative approach uses less data to train and has better sound quality than previous models, and has a certain degree of reproduction in speech speed.

articleTitle: Two-Subnet Scheme Based on Conditional GAN for Channel Agnostic End to End Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: This paper proposes a two-subnet scheme based on conditional generative adversarial nets (CGAN) for channel agnostic end to end communication to improve the bit-error rate (BER) performance with lower complexity. Specifically, a two-subnet scheme for joint optimization of transceiver is first introduced. The entire end to end communication system is implemented by neural networks, and the receiver is composed of two subnets: the equalization subnet R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Equ</inf> and the decoding subnet R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Dec</inf>. Then, a two-stage training strategy is proposed. In training stage I, the transmitter T is directly concatenated to the subnet R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Dec</inf> to address the challenge of updating transmitter parameters through unknown channels. In training stage II, the generator from the subnet R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Equ</inf> which adopts CGAN is deployed to accomplish the estimation and equalization. Simulation results demonstrate that the two-stage training strategy can effectively recover long transmission sequences, and the BER performance precedes both the traditional method based on expert knowledge and the state-of-the-art end-to-end method. Furthermore, the proposed method greatly reduces the retraining complexity since merely the subnet R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Equ</inf> need retrain when the channel scenarios change. It should be noted that the proposed method can be easily applied to any OFDM systems or other practical channels. This paper also develops the parameters updating mechanism.

articleTitle: Efficient Authorship Attribution Method Using Ensemble Models Built by Knowledge Distillation
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Authorship attribution is a task to identify the author of given documents. It is often treated as a classification task that predicts the author of a written text among given candidates. From practical application perspectives, such as forensic science, the interpretation of results is essential, and the ability to perform authorship attribution with many sentences at high speed will become increasingly important for developing authorship attribution methods. Recently, transformer-based large-scale language models have been developed in natural language processing, and high accuracy has been achieved in various fields. The attention mechanism implemented in the encoder part of the transformer is called self-attention, which calculates the degree of attention given to each word in a sentence. However, in classification problems such as author attribution, the only evidence used as a basis for judgment is the attention distribution, which is a single dimension of the matrix calculated by self-attention and is computationally inefficient. In addition, since this attention distribution is obtained for the number of attentions in the model, its contribution to estimation results and utilization is difficult to examine. In this study, we propose an authorship attribution method that ensembles compact models that substitute each attention of a fine-tuned transformer made by knowledge distillation. We also examine the contribution of each attention to the estimation results based on the accuracy of each ensemble model. In authorship attribution experiments using the works of modern Japanese authors, the ensemble of distillation models achieved results comparable to those of bidirectional encoder representations from transformers. Furthermore, if the process can be ideally parallelized, the computational time required for inference by the proposed method can be significantly reduced.

articleTitle: DualStreamAttentionNet: A Multimodal Approach for Audio and Text sentiment analysis with Self and Cross Modal Attention Mechanisms
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Sentiment analysis is a crucial task in natural language processing. While unimodal sentiment analysis relies on one modality, multimodal sentiment analysis combines features from various modalities to improve accuracy. However, many current models emphasize complex fusion techniques and neglect the importance of enhancing modality feature extraction. They also often overlook the interaction between modalities. In response, we introduce the DualStreamAttentionNet(DSAN), an innovative model tailored for joint text and audio sentiment analysis. Our architecture employs a Transformer encoder for robust textual feature extraction and processes audio using 1D convolutions followed by a bidirectional LSTM for enhanced audio feature representation. Crucially, by leveraging self and cross-attention mechanisms, our model not only amplifies the intrinsic features of each modality but also effectively captures the interrelated dynamics between text and audio. This dual-focus approach leads to a synergistic fusion of features, resulting in heightened emotion classification accuracy.

articleTitle: Research on SFSDP Optimization Based on Gradient Methods
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Multi-agent systems can be applied in many fields and have good prospects for development. It is particularly necessary to obtain the location information of a single agent in the system. In this paper, a sparse version of full semidefinite programming(SFSDP) is used to solve the multi-agent system localization problem. The results can be applied in networks of both robotic vehicles and unmanned aerial vehicles with located sensors. In this paper, a model of multi-agent system localization problem was built and converted into a convex optimization problem by SFSDP relaxation. To address the poor performance of SFSDP optimization based on the gradient method in some situations, this paper creatively adopts Adagrad to optimize the SFSDP and verifies the superiority of Adagrad in optimizing the SFSDP through experiments.

articleTitle: Air-Ground Cooperative Asynchronous Online Federated Learning With Misaligned Over-The-Air Computation
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In practice, air-ground cooperative federated learning (FL) assisted by unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) faces challenges due to lagging UAVs and the necessity of learning features from real-time data. Moreover, frequent communication and computation become performance bottlenecks for air-ground cooperative FL, especially when a large number of UAVs share the same wireless medium. Therefore, an Air-Ground Cooperative Asynchronous Online Federated Learning framework with Over-the-Air Computation (OAC-AOFL) is proposed. The OAC scheme enables UAVs to perform computations simultaneously with data transmission over a multiple-access channel. Therefore, the communication and computation delays are reduced. Additionally, a matched filter is employed to develop an aligned-sample estimator, minimizing the impact of misaligned OAC. Simulation results reveal that the proposed OAC-AOFL accelerates global model convergence speed compared to AOFL with conventional orthogonal frequency-division multiple access. Moreover, excessive noise power or degree of time misalignment can significantly impact the performance of OAC-AOFL.

articleTitle: An Enhanced Instance Segmentation Network for Surface Defect Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Surface defect detection is a crucial aspect of industrial production processes, requiring both high detection accuracy and speed. Numerous research studies have successfully applied computer vision methods to surface defect detection tasks. However, these methods still face challenges when applied in industrial production scenarios. We propose a novel high-speed surface defect instance segmentation network. To overcome the issue of low contrast between defects and the background, global context attention modules are introduced into the backbone network, enhancing the model’s feature extraction capability. The BiFPN network is utilized as the Neck network to improve feature fusion within the model. Furthermore, a lightweight cross-layer connection module is proposed to fully integrate low-level positional information with high-level semantic information, thereby enhancing defect edge detection accuracy. We collect a representative dataset for surface defects on electrical contact workpieces (EC). Experimental results on the KolektorSDD2, MT, and EC datasets demonstrate that our proposed method achieves both fast detection speed and high detection accuracy.

articleTitle: Interface Design for Analog Front-End Chips in Battery Management Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: This paper presents a design of the communication interface circuit following the I2C and SPI protocol for the analog front-end (AFE) chip within a battery management system(BMS). The AFE interface type can be configured upon AFE powers on and during the normal operation following the host command. Some considerations to reduce transaction are given during the address spacing building. In this work, different commands are categorized, introducing the concept of direct and indirect commands to optimize address space usage. To enhance efficiency and reduce unnecessary data transfers, a block data transfer communication method is defined.The proposed design undergoes initial validation through RTL simulation and is subsequently fabricated using the SMIC 0.18um BCD process. Post-fabrication chip-level testing demonstrates the proper functionality of the AFE communication interface, confirming stable data transmission.

articleTitle: Continual Learning with Ranking Self-Correction in Event Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Event detection is challenging in real-world scenarios due to the continuous occurrence of new events while old events still persist, which can lead to catastrophic forgetting of the old events. Due to the inherent advantages of incremental learning in preventing catastrophic forgetting, application of incremental learning in event detection is getting more and more attention from research communities. However, there are still some problems need to be solved in the method of incremental learning and its application in event detection. Existing research has mainly focused on designing models to retain event features from previous models, without considering the mistakes made in the previously event predicted models. In this work, we propose a method called Ranking Self-Correction (RSC) that employ a self-correction approach, we introduce a new loss function to ensure that the predictions of the new model have smaller errors compared to the previous model, preventing the predictions from shifting towards a worse direction. The experimental results demonstrate that our proposed method effectively addresses the incremental event detection problem and achieves consistent and significant performance on the MAVEN and ACE dataset.

articleTitle: Research on the Reliability of 5G-R Railway Base Station Networking Based on Monte Carlo Simluation
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The reliability of 5G-R private network is an important guarantee for 5G railway communication. Aiming at the base station networking system with CU/DU separation, the Monte Carlo simulation method is used to establish a more complete base station equipment management and fault switching logic, and simulate the base station fault scenarios. The base station reliability curve is simulated, the weak links of the base station system are analyzed, and the feasibility of the model and analysis method are verified, which lays a good foundation for the subsequent problem research.

articleTitle: Physical Layer Authentication for Two-User Two-Way Large-Scale Antennas Relay Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Relay communication is ubiquitous in various wireless communication networks, and physical layer security has grown to be an important issue for relay systems. This paper proposed an additively uniquely decomposable constellation pair (AUDCP) based physical layer authentication (PLA) scheme for two-user two-way relay systems. In the proposed scheme, tags generated by hash function are embedded into the messages at the two single-antenna users and a noncoherent detector is employed at the relay with large-scale antennas to execute signal detection in the multiple access phase, where the AUDCP design is used to guarantee the signal distinguishable. PLA is carried out at the relay to authenticate the identities of the users before the forwarding of received signals. Then, precoding is operated at the relay for the broadcasting phase with the estimated channel state information after a regenerated tag being embedded into the broadcasting signals. Finally, PLA is also implemented at the two users after the signal detection. Simulation results show that the proposed scheme achieves high reliability for secure relay communications.

articleTitle: Ship target detection method for SAR image based on image block
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In order to solve the problems of large amount of SAR image, large differences in target resolution, non-uniform sea clutter, and difficulty in real-time detection in orbit, an Algorithm for ship detection in spaceborne SAR image based on image segmentation is proposed. Firstly, the image is processed into blocks according to the azimuth and distance directions, secondly, the target detection method based on Weibull statistical model is used to detect ship targets on each block, and finally the connected domain labeling method is used to realize the target clustering. The algorithm effectively solves the problem of target segmentation, improves the detection efficiency and precision, and reduces the false alarm rate. The test is carried out on the hardware platform of multi-core DSP-TMS320C6678 + XilinxV7XC7VX690T. The test results show that the detection effect and efficiency are improved.

articleTitle: Research and Optimization of Electrode-Assisted Human Key Point Detection Algorithm Based on Channel Attention and Adaptive Feature Fusion
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In carotid endarterectomy surgery, it is crucial for the surgeon to accurately locate the stenosis. Due to the medical application of this method and the actual research cost, Electrode, which is commonly used in medical fields, was chosen as the detection target in this study. To address the above issues, this paper proposes an Electrode-assisted human key point detection algorithm based on channel attention and adaptive feature fusion, and conducts experiments using a self-labeled dataset. To improve the detection accuracy in complex scenes and complete a large amount of computation in a short time, a series of techniques were employed, including using a deeper convolutional neural network, a larger receptive field, and more feature layers to enhance detection accuracy, fusing convolutional layers, using FPN and other acceleration techniques to improve detection speed. The channel attention mechanism can adaptively learn the importance of each channel, thereby capturing key information in the image better and improving the model's generalization performance. The adaptive feature fusion can adaptively learn the weight of each feature map, thereby better fusing feature information from different levels and further improving the model's generalization performance. The experiment shows that the average accuracy of this method on the dataset is 89%.

articleTitle: QoE Assessment of Single-User Operation and Dual-User Operation in Remote Robot Systems with Force Feedback
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: This paper makes a subjective comparison between single-user operation and dual-user operation for cooperative work in remote robot systems with force feedback by QoE (Quality of Experience) assessment. A single user operates a remote robot by using a haptic interface device in the single-user operation, and two users operate the remote robot by using two haptic interface devices in the dual-user operation.
