In our assessment, each subject answers which of the operations is better than the other. Assessment results illustrate that the dual-user operation outperforms the single-user operation. Also, as the network delay increases, the dual-user operation is more desirable.

articleTitle: Estimation Method of Ship Propeller Parameters Based on Deep Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In this paper, the deep convolution neural network is used to estimate the propeller parameters of ship. By using its ability to extract features form high-dimensional complex data, the accurate mapping from ship radiated noise to propeller parameters is realized. Firstly, the ship radiated noise is demodulated to generate DEMON spectrum. And through time accumulation and normalization processing, normalized DEMON spectrum samples conforming to deep learning are obtained. Then, a deep convolutional neural network model adapted to the usage scenario is constructed. In view of the large difference between the time and frequency dimension scales of the normalized DEMON spectrum graph, the different strides is adopted in some convolutional cores to reduce the influence of the asymmetry of the time and frequency dimension scales. In order to estimate the fundamental frequency and blade frequency of propeller simultaneously, two output layers are constructed on the top layer of the model to represent the estimation results of fundamental frequency and blade frequency respectively. On this basis, large-scale highly complex simulation DEMON spectrum samples are used to train and verify the performance of the deep convolutional neural network model. The results show that the model training process has good convergence. The accuracy of fundamental frequency estimation and blade number estimation is up to 92.9% and 95.6% under the condition of low signal-to-noise ratio, which verified the effectiveness of the deep convolutional neural network model to estimate propeller parameters.

articleTitle: Sci-CoT: Leveraging Large Language Models for Enhanced Knowledge Distillation in Small Models for Scientific QA
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown outstanding performance across wide range of downstream tasks. This competency is attributed to their substantial parameter size and pre-training on extensive corpus. Moreover, LLMs have exhibited enhanced reasoning capabilities in tackling complex reasoning tasks, owing to the utilization of a method named "Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting". This method is designed to generate intermediate reasoning steps that guide the inference of the final answer. However, it is essential to highlight that these advanced reasoning abilities appear to emerge in models with a minimum of 10 billion parameters, thereby limiting its efficacy in situations where computational resources are constrained. In this paper, we investigate the possibility of transferring the reasoning capabilities of LLMs to smaller models via knowledge distillation. Specifically, we propose Sci-CoT, a two-stage framework that separates the processes of generating rationales and inferring answers. This method enables a more efficient use of rationales during the answer inference stage, leading to improved performance on scientific question-answering tasks. Utilizing Sci-CoT, our 80-million parameter model is able to exceed the performance of BLOOM-176B in the ARC-Easy dataset under the few shot setting.

articleTitle: FMCW Radar Fall Detection Based on Parallel Multi-scale Feature Extraction
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Existing fall detection systems are prone to insufficiency of feature extraction, over-fitting and error propagation caused by small datasets, as well as the low recognition rate, this paper proposes a RNCK-SENet model for fall detection. Firstly, an imbalanced human motion echo signal is obtained using FMCW radar, which is then utilized to construct a set of micro-Doppler feature maps. Next, preliminary feature extraction is performed using a transfer learning-based ResNet18 model, In addition, the features are filtered and optimized through the SE module to fully extract comprehensive behavioral features. To capture information from multiple scales and enhance feature extraction, a parallel multi-scale feature extraction module is embedded in the network. Finally, the fused features are fed into a fully connected layer for classification. Comparative results with classical networks demonstrate that our fall detection algorithm achieves higher average accuracy, recall, and F1 score, reaches 98.43%, 99.33%, and 99.12% respectively. The F1 score is improved by 2% to 10%.

articleTitle: Enhancing Community Deception based on Graph Autoencoder and Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Detecting communities plays a crucial role in social network analysis, offering valuable insights into network structures and relationships. However, there is a pressing concern regarding the potential exposure of sensitive or personal information about individuals when analyzing these communities. To tackle these privacy challenges, we present a novel community deception approach which could hide community information for individuals by perturbing network structures. In particular, we first conduct sampling to obtain subnetworks from the original network. Subnetwork sampling allows us to work with large networks. Then, we propose pairwise constraints into subgraph autoencoders to perturb the connections in the original network. Finally, we employ a genetic algorithm to seamlessly combine the perturbed subnetworks and construct a complete ruined network, which could ensure that sensitive information remains concealed within the network. Extensive experiments on several real-world datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach.

articleTitle: Adversarial Profiled Side-Channel Attack with Unsupervised Domain Adaptation
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Deep learning-based methods have been proven to be very successful when applied to profiled side-channel attacks (SCA). In profiled SCA, the attacker gains knowledge about the target device by accessing a profiling device before the attack. However, most of the work does not consider the problem that it is difficult to obtain profiling traces that is fully consistent with the attack traces because the target device often employs more advanced masking countermeasures. Even if a small discrepancy between profiling traces and attack traces (regarded as domain discrepancy) may cause the attack failure. To address the problem of domain discrepancy, we propose a side-channel attack method based on the domain adversarial self-attention mechanism (DASA-SCA). Specifically, the method feeds the feature extractor through the bounded loss of the domain classifier when building the model in order to learn a hidden representation that is not only discriminative but also domain invariant. To enhance this domain-invariant representation, we introduce self-attention mechanism in the feature extractor to give higher weights to the significant parts of the leakage in order to improve the feature extraction. We implement three different deep learning models including CNN, ResNet, and LSTM in the DASA-SCA approach for both electromagnetic(EM) side-channel and power side-channel to demonstrate the scalability and generality of the framework. Finally, we validate the effectiveness of the DASA-SCA approach using the ASCAD dataset and DPA dataset. The experimental results demonstrate that our method can significantly reduce the impact of domain discrepancy caused by different countermeasures and enhance the side-channel attack capability.

articleTitle: Differential Privacy Hierarchical Federated Learning Method based on Privacy Budget Allocation
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Federated learning can effectively protect users’ personal data from being obtained by attackers, and differential privacy can enhance the privacy of federated learning and solve the privacy leakage problem caused by model training parameters. Because of the rapid increase in the number of terminals, hierarchical federated learning framework has a wide application prospect because of its advantages such as high scalability. Most of the existing researches on the combination of federated learning and differential privacy are based on the terminal-server framework, while the relevant researches based on hierarchical federated learning framework are lacking. In this paper, we propose a differential privacy hierarchical federated learning method based on privacy budget allocation, which can effectively resist member inference attacks by adding quantitative noise to model parameter update when the model parameter update is uploaded. In order to achieve the balance between data availability and privacy protection, an accurate privacy budget allocation strategy is designed to ensure the efficiency of federated learning and the availability of the model. We verify the effectiveness of the proposed method on the MNIST dataset, and the experimental results show that the accuracy of the global model can still be maintained at a high level under the premise of protecting data security.

articleTitle: Hermes: An Efficient Building Block for RDMA Incast in Datacenters
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In Remote Direct Memory Access (RDMA) data center networks, incast has a serious impact on non-incast flows due to its many-to-one and synchronous characteristics. With the increasing link rate, the response speed of RDMA Congestion Control (CC) alone fails to effectively cope with incast. However, existing RDMA incast solutions have limitations. They are unable to control the incast in time and require extensive device modifications. We propose Hermes, an efficient incast control scheme based on Top-of-Rack (ToR) switches. Hermes achieves accurate incast identification with the shortest control loop through the traffic monitor and uses the Virtual Output Queue (VOQ) to converge quickly to the proper rate of incast traffic. The core idea of Hermes is to minimize the accumulation of incast traffic on core switches and improve the performance of non-incast flows. Hermes only modifies ToR switches and is compatible with existing RDMA CCs. We evaluate Hermes through our Testbed and NS3 simulations. The results show that Hermes can reduce the average and 99th Flow Completion Time (FCT) slowdown of incast victim flows by up to 20% and 55% respectively, compared with the state-of-the-art solution.

articleTitle: Learning to Reason: Event Argument Extraction with Multi-Step Reasoning
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Event argument extraction (EAE) identifies the arguments and their roles from a piece of text under a given event. Existing methods for EAE mostly rely on generation models and use various techniques to provide additional information to the model, such as designing prompts or modifying the model structure. However, these methods do not adequately harness the reasoning capabilities of large language models (LLMs), which have demonstrated their ability to perform well on complex tasks by generating natural language explanations. We propose a novel EAE method that uses LLMs as reasoning teachers and guides the model to extract the correct arguments by imposing syntactic and argument role type constraints in the reasoning process. We also apply the Chain-of-Thought technique, which produces a sequence of intermediate steps that guild the reasoning process towards the final answer, to enhance the reasoning skills of both small models like T5 and large models like GPT3.5. We perform experiments on four distinct datasets and achieve new SOTA results, outperforming the previous methods by an average of 1.2%. Our results validate the effectiveness and efficiency of employing reasoning steps for EAE.

articleTitle: An iGOMP Channel Estimation for V2V Channels under the scenarios of Scattering Environments
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: an improved generalized orthogonal matching pursuit (iGOMP) channel estimation scheme for V2V channel model in urban scattering environments is proposed in this paper. The iGOMP can split the channel estimation problem into a sparse signal recovery issue, which replaces the classical inner product criterion with the Dice atom matching criterion, and integrates with the atomic weak progressive selection method to avoid that the inner product criterion cannot select the optimal atom from the redundant dictionary. Then, to achieve the optimal channel estimation, we use the feedback results to iterate. Finally, numerical simulations demonstrate the effectiveness of the iGOMP in comparison with other conventional channel estimation schemes. Besides, both the complexity and running time of each algorithm are carried out to compare the performance of the proposed algorithm with those of the existing state-of-the-art methods for V2V channels.

articleTitle: Multicast SFC Mapping Algorithm Based on Comprehensive Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In this paper, we study the multicast service function chain (SFC) mapping problem in software-defined networking and network function virtualization environments. In order to jointly optimize node computation, storage and bandwidth resource consumption, we propose a multicast SFC mapping heuristic algorithm based on comprehensive evaluation. The algorithm builds a multicast tree covering all destination nodes while deploying virtual network functions (VNFs). It first conducts a comprehensive evaluation of several best candidates at the current tree building and the impact of these candidates on the subsequent tree building. Then it selects the candidate paths to be added to the tree that can save the overhead of the multicast tree and contribute to the reduction of the number of VNFs to be deployed, optimizing simultaneously the multicast tree's overhead and the number of VNF placements in the tree building process and further reducing the consumption of transmission, computation and storage resources. The experimental simulation results show that the proposed algorithm outperforms the MC-MSFT in terms of node computation, storage and bandwidth resource consumption as well as blocking ratio.

Author Keywords: minimum path cost multicast tree algorithm

articleTitle: A Transformer-Based Multi-Feature Extraction Neural Network for Bluetooth Devices Identification
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Radio frequency fingerprint identification(RFFI) is a novel method for device authentication that ensures the security of the Internet of Things(IoT). Feature extraction is the most essential step in this technique, however, most existing deep learning(DL)-based methods leverage convolutional neural networks(CNNs) and recurrent neural network(RNNs) to extract single local features from signals, but multi-scale, global features can significantly enhance RFFI’s accuracy. To address these issues, this paper proposes a transformer-based multi-feature extraction neural network(TMFENN) for RFFI. We utilize a transformer structure to extract multi-scale features embedded in signals with different sampling rates, and then perform feature fusion based on an attention mechanism. In addition, we employ a classification module based on ResNet blocks to accomplish the device classification task. To evaluate the performance of the proposed RFFI method, we conduct extensive experiments with 33 kinds of bluetooth signals from different mobilephones. At SNR = 20dB, the classification accuracy reaches a high of 92.6%. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed TMFENN outperforms existing DL-based methods in terms of both accuracy and robustness.

articleTitle: Research on Artificial Intelligence Empowered Network Security
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: As the world becomes increasingly interconnected, new AI technologies bring new opportunities while also giving rise to new network security risks, while network security is critical to national and social security, enterprise as well as personal information security. This article mainly introduces the empowerment of AI in network security, the development trend of its application in the field of network security, the challenges faced, and suggestions, providing beneficial exploration for effectively applying artificial intelligence technology to computer network security protection.

articleTitle: A Scalable Small Array Design Method for Generating Multi-mode OAM Waves
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The key to orbital angular momentum (OAM) communication lies in the multiplexing of multi-mode OAM vortex waves, which can be generated by multiple concentric uniform circular array (UCA). In this paper, a design method for small and scalable array for generating multi-mode vortex waves is proposed, and this array has regularity. The design concept is that the distance between adjacent UCAs is equal, the distance between adjacent elements in each UCA is equal, and the distance between adjacent elements in all UCAs is equal. The proposed array designed method has advantages such as regularity, scalability, and smaller volume. Compared with traditional concentric ring array antenna, simulation results show that the vortex waves generated by the designed array have higher mode isolation. The proposed array design method is beneficial for reducing mutual coupling between antenna elements and reducing the size of antenna array. Therefore, OAM beams with higher quality and ability to reuse more modes can be generated, which is of great significance for achieving multi-mode OAM multiplexing communication.

articleTitle: OWFQ: Reducing Packet Drops for Approximate Weighted Fair Queueing with Calendar Queues
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Weighted fair queueing (WFQ) is a router mechanism that can achieve customized bandwidth allocation and flow isolation in data centers as well as other high-speed networks today. However, it’s hard to faithfully implement the original WFQ algorithm in high-speed networks due to the high complexity such as the need for sorting packets at line rate. Therefore, many approximate WFQ packet schedulers have been proposed as a substitute, such as PCQ, a packet scheduler that uses calendar queues. Unfortunately, although PCQ successfully achieved fairness among flows without such complex hardware requirements, it introduced a new problem that the packet drop rate is significantly increased when compared with ideal WFQ algorithm as a result of its implementation mechanism and approximation cost. As we all know, packet drop is a common but important problem. High drop rate not only affects bandwidth utilization but also has a negative effect on the QoS (quality of service) of latency-sensitive services. In this paper, we design a new approximate WFQ scheduling algorithm with calendar queues named opportunistic weighted fair queueing (OWFQ). OWFQ is designed to reduce packet drops caused by the approximation cost of calendar queues. We conduct simulations on an incast network with one switch to measure drop rates of different algorithms. The results show that OWFQ significantly decreases the drop rate when compared with PCQ and thus improves bandwidth utilization.

articleTitle: MiTM Attack Detection Scheme Using Monitoring Information in V2X Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communication technique is required for driving autonomous vehicles. It calculates the optimal driving route using collected real-time traffic information. Therefore, the integrity of messages transmitted via V2X communication must be guaranteed and they must be correctly transmitted to the driving vehicle. However, messages transmitted through V2X communication can be modified or dropped by an attacker attempting a man-in-the-middle attack. As intelligent transport systems develop, various traffic situations need to be addressed. However, in certain situations, attack detection is impossible using the existing schemes. The proposed scheme detects attacks by utilizing road condition monitoring information in various traffic situations.

articleTitle: Prediction of Regional Carbon Emissions Based on ARIMA Model and Kaya Model
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Research on regional carbon neutrality targets and path planning is the foundation for achieving China’s carbon neutrality goals and promoting sustainable development. By studying and analyzing the carbon emissions, economic structure, energy consumption, and other factors of specific regions or areas, a carbon reduction path and action plan suitable for the region can be formulated to guide the region in adjusting its energy structure, improving energy utilization efficiency, and developing low-carbon industries. This paper uses statistical methods combined with data science to conduct time series analysis and regression analysis based on the characteristics of the data provided in order to establish a predictive model for regional carbon emissions, economic, population, and energy consumption. The Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average Model (ARIMA) time series model is used to predict the trend of population, economy, energy consumption, and a multiple regression model between energy consumption, population, and GDP is established based on the Kaya model.

articleTitle: Efficient Programming of Re-configurable Radio Frequency (RF) Transmitter
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: For re-configurable RF transmitter, an important challenge is to find an optimal configuration for a specific communication standard. The particle swarm optimization(PSO) algorithm with a cross-variance operation is used in this paper to program the re-configurable RF transmitter, which can find the optimal configuration efficiently. The simulation results show that the designed RF transmitter meets the specified performance criteria, including dynamic range and linearity. Our numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed methodology is more efficient (i.e., with low computational cost) than other traditional algorithms.

articleTitle: Optimization Transmission Schedule based on Information Value in Remote State Estimation
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In this paper, the issue of designing transmission schedule for remote state estimation system for multiple dynamical processes is investigated. As the limited capacity of wireless channel, it is no possible that all observation information can be transmitted at any time. Furthermore, the information value of each observation information can be realized at the estimator is different. For this consideration, the problem of sensor selection, aiming to maximize the system performance is studied. We first formulate this problem as an integer programming problem to derive the optimal transmission strategy, and the penalty function method is utilized to reduce such problem as unconstrained one. Then, the ant colony optimization policy is utilized to optimize the transmission schedule. Lastly, numerical results are given to validate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: QCon: A Q-Learning Based Congestion Control Scheme in Named Data Networking
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In Named Data Networking (NDN), congestion control is essential for ensuring efficiency of data delivery. The present TCP/IP based end-to-end congestion control algorithms are inapplicable in NDN due to its multi-source and multipath transmission characteristics. Hop-by-hop congestion control is a distinctive feature in NDN that utilizes intermediate routers to control the congestion. However, the current congestion control schemes utilized in NDN are not up to the mark in controlling the congestion because of the varying network conditions of NDN. To overcome the limitations present in the current congestion control schemes, this paper proposes a novel Q-learning based hop-by-hop congestion control scheme named QCon. The proposed scheme utilizes congestion information (i.e., queue occupancy) from upstream nodes as a new field value in Data packet. The receiving router update the Q-values based on local congestion information and information received from upstream router and selects the path with the best Q-value for forwarding the Interest packets. The simulation results show that the proposed scheme outperform the similar hop-by-hop congestion control schemes in terms of packet loss ratio and throughput when encountered with congestion.

articleTitle: NOMA-Assisted Relay Access Scheme for Flying Ad Hoc Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Flying Ad Hoc networks (FANETs) have been widely used in military and civil applications due to their rapid deployment and flexibility. FANET is characterised by dynamic topology and limited energy of Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) nodes, existing topology-based routing protocols are not suitable for FANET. Location-based GPSR protocol is widely adopted due to its scalability. But with the increase in the number of UAV nodes, how to increase the node throughput over the limited spectrum becomes a constraint for FANET routing protocols. In this paper, based on GPSR protocol, NOMA technique is used to improve the spectrum efficiency. In addition, this paper gives the power control scheme for each UAV node in NOMA grouping and derives the outage probability under this scheme. Simulation results show that the power control scheme proposed in this paper can greatly improve the average throughput of the nodes, and the simulation NOMA outage probability matches well with the theoretical outage probability.

articleTitle: 3GPP Evaluation on UE with 8 Receiving Antennas in 5G NR Release 18 Standardization
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The evolution from 4G LTE to 5G NR has increased the requirement for downlink data rate and data transmission reliability. Massive MIMO, as an advanced antenna technique, has been extensively deployed in 5G systems. 8Rx UE performance has never been verified for its practical network structure and typical network parameter configurations. In this paper, an evaluation of the UR 8Rx performance verification for 5G NR in terms of system modeling, antenna correlation modeling, and key algorithms is provided based on the 3GPP Release 18 new work item. The evaluation covers multi-stream transmission, CQI selection, and link adaptation. Link-level simulation results show that compared with the traditional UEs with 2/4Rx, UEs with 8Rx can provide better performance with muti-stream transmission and link adaption.

articleTitle: Compliance monitoring of protective clothing removal in medical scenarios
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In recent years, the field of epidemic protection has taken center stage, with a laser focus on deploying deep learning algorithms in daily life, especially in medicine and transportation. The intricate process of doffing protective gear and completing personal disinfection in medical settings directly impacts staff safety. However, the current standardized decontamination protocol relies on manual inspection, an onerous and error-prone approach, with substantial gaps remaining in related algorithms and concrete implementations. To bridge this void, we propose a holistic suite of intelligent protective clothing monitoring algorithms powered by object detection. Our cascading detection paradigm melds accuracy and speed. To address the challenges of limited precision and vulnerability in small target detection by existing algorithms, we propose the incorporation of a multidimensional feature fusion module, exploiting more extensive and comprehensive feature data. Additionally, we integrate a dynamic library to further improve the algorithm’s processing speed and better fulfill real-time demands. Extensive experiments reveal that our protective clothing detection algorithm attains exceptional accuracy and exceptionally fast performance. In particular, the multidimensional feature fusion module significantly enhances detection accuracy and robustness. Overall, our innovative techniques yield concrete results, advancing the state of automated epidemic protection.

articleTitle: Formal Verification of Taylor’s Theorem in Coq
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: We have constructed a formalized system of unary differential calculus using the Coq tool. In this system, we formally defined the fundamental concepts of sequences, limits, functions, and derivatives in differential calculus. Furthermore, we carried out formal verification of various properties and theorems related to function limits, Local Preserving of Sign, Intermediate Value theorem, Uniform Continuity theorem, and the four Arithmetic Operations of Derivatives. Based on these efforts, we successfully completed the formal proof of Taylor’s theorem. The system’s code can be rigorously executed and validated on a computer, ensuring the entire proof process is rigorous and reliable. This work shows great potential in advancing the formalization of mathematics in the future, assisting educators in their teaching efforts, guiding learners in their studies, and making a positive contribution to the field of education and teaching.

articleTitle: A Revised Entropy Based Algorithm to Solve Wordle
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The previous entropy based algorithm for Wordle has a weak performance when encountering words with a common suffix. In order to solve this issue, we establish a revised entropy based system, adding a revised term to the entropy formula to amend the influence of suffix on the expected pattern distribution. We also consider the influence of KL divergence on the probability that a common suffix may result in a poor performance. The results show a 1.5% overall improvement with average attempts decreasing from 3.87 to 3.81. We also test our system's sensitivity on starting words and "salet" turns out to be the best starting word that suits our revised system.

articleTitle: An Intelligent Routing Approach for SDN Based on Improved DuelingDQN Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Existing intelligent routing methods make routing decisions based on limited link information in data center networks with surging traffic, making it difficult to adapt to complex network environments and dynamic traffic loads that cause congestion and low bandwidth utilization. In order to improve the traffic transmission efficiency and network reliability, this paper proposes a smart routing algorithm (DRL-PD, Deep Reinforcement Learning-Prioritization and Dijkstra) based on improved DuelingDQN. The algorithm combines the Software Defined Networking (SDN) controller to monitor the network link information and maps it into the state space of the intelligences for training decisions, designs the intelligent routing model as a multidimensional reward weight, proposes a Dijkstra a priori exploration strategy based on Epsilon’s greed to intelligently adjust the routing and forwarding strategy, thus adapting to the changes in the network traffic, alleviating link congestion, and improving the traffic transmission efficiency and performance of the network. The experimental results show that DRL-PD has the effectiveness and stability of fast convergence on training compared to Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) and Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) algorithms. In terms of routing effectiveness, DRL-PD has a good performance in improving network throughput and reducing data packet loss under guaranteed transmission tasks compared to Deep Reinforcement Learning-Traffic Engineering (DRL-TE) method, state-action-reward-state-action (SARSA) and Dijkstra routing algorithm.

articleTitle: Protecting Location Semantics under Local Differential Privacy
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: With the widespread proliferation of mobile devices, location-based services (LBS) are gaining increasing popularity due to the emergency of convenient context-aware services. The collection and analysis of locations in LBS potentially lead to privacy risks due to the nature of locations. Several existing works try to protect location privacy under local differential privacy (LDP), which is a state-of-the-art privacy preservation model. However, these works still pose a risk to user privacy because untrusted data collectors can exploit location semantics to infer the user’s true location. In this paper, we propose a novel approach LSLDP to protect location semantics under LDP. In LSLDP, we first propose a novel LDP method SRLS that carefully combines physical distance and semantic distance during the perturbation process. Additionally, we design a location release method based on the Expectation Maximization (EM) reconstruction method to rectify estimation errors stemming from SRLS. Comprehensive experiments on real-world datasets substantiate the effectiveness of LSLDP.

articleTitle: Realization of supermarket product image recognition based on automatic machine learning
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In recent years, with the rapid development of machine learning, it has achieved great success in the field of image recognition. However, it requires a lot of knowledge and human resources to achieve superior learning performance, bringing about all aspects of machine learning that cannot be separated from human participation. In order to make machine learning techniques easier to apply and reduce the need for human experts, Automatic Machine Learning (AutoML) has become a hot topic in industry and academia. In this paper, we contribute to the research of supermarket goods recognition by applying AutoML to supermarket goods recognition. We first survey the literature on image recognition and AutoML to get an appreciation of their current status. Next, we introduce two main methods we use in this paper: image augmentation and AutoML. Furthermore, we apply the model and get an acceptable evaluation with mAP(0.933), accuracy(0.888), and recall rate(0.851).

articleTitle: Recognition and Segmentation of Heat Treatment Processes Based on PLR
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In industrial processing, heat treatment encompasses various techniques such as annealing, tempering, quenching, tempering, surface hardening, and more. These diverse processes impart different characteristics to metallic materials, catering to the specific requirements of subsequent production stages. As each technique corresponds to a distinct temperature range, temperature serves as a pivotal process parameter, exerting a decisive influence on the quality of manufacturing equipment. This study focuses on the analysis of temperature time series data in the context of heat treatment. We propose an PLR algorithm based on key Point and Bottom-Up merging (KP-BU PLR) to partition different process stages and extract corresponding features. Simultaneously, we address the issue of anomalous fluctuations in temperature time series data encountered in practical production processes. To tackle this challenge, we introduce a sliding window-based approach for anomaly detection and handling, enhancing the information density of production data, while ensuring the stability of the KP-BU algorithm. Finally, the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed methods are validated through experimental verification using real production data.

articleTitle: STRSNet: A Spatial Transformer-based Remote-sensing Segmentation Network
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Multi-scale feature extraction is commonly adopted in high-resolution remote-sensing semantic segmentation tasks, in which images are reshaped into multiple sizes to generate features from different levels. However, larger size images contain less detailed information and smaller images lose more contextual information, and both of them restrict the performance of remote-sensing semantic segmentation neural networks. In this paper, a Spatial Transformer-based Network for Remote-sensing Segmentation(STRSNet) is proposed to deal with this problem. Local images of smaller sizes are cut from the center of larger images, and both of them are input to STRSNet separately. Local features from cropped local images and contextual features from larger images are extracted respectively in STRSNet to learn both detailed and contextual information and capture more long range dependencies, and a Spatial Enhancement and Perception Transformer(SEPT) is used for feature fusion. SEPT contains a Polar Coordinates Spatial Enhancement module(PCSE) and a Spatial Multi-layer Perceptron module(SMLP) to build fine-grained local spatial information. Experimental results on Land-cover Dataset with Gaofen-2 satellite(GID) have shown that the proposed STRSNet has outperformed the compared methods.

articleTitle: A novel annular through-silicon-vias in 3D-ICs
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Based on through-silicon-vias technology, a novel annular through-silicon-vias (TSVs) structure has been proposed which is improved on traditional circular structure. The accurate wideband equivalent circuit is derived based on lumped parameters. The results of the equivalent-circuit model match well with the result of the HFSS simulations. The results show that the proposed new structure not only saves the footprint of the through-holes, but also greatly improves the performance of the through-holes.

articleTitle: Personalized Federated Distillation Method Based on Game Theory
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In the era of data-driven artificial intelligence, the emergence of federated learning has promoted the open sharing of data. In order to overcome the limitations of data and model isomorphism in federated learning and enhance privacy protection during the federated learning process, this paper proposes the ESAFD (encode-shuffle-analyze-federated-distribution) model to shuffle and protect private data; At the same time, personalized aggregation coefficients are calculated using game theory during aggregation analysis, and knowledge distillation is used to transfer the client’s predictive knowledge to the local model for training, achieving federated transfer learning of heterogeneous models. The effectiveness of the proposed FedPD algorithm was verified using the MNIST dataset, and experiments have shown that this scheme can effectively improve the performance of the model in federated learning.

articleTitle: LightRPC: An Efficient and Simple RDMA-based RPC Framework
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: RDMA has been widely used in modern data centers because it can provide low-latency and high-bandwidth network communication for distributed applications. However, how to build an efficient RDMA-based RPC framework is still challenging. We observe that existing work may have the following problems: First, the lack of a serialization module makes the RPC framework difficult to use, and cannot further be optimized by overlapping serialization and network communication. Second, CPU resources are ignored to scale out instead of focusing on QP and memory resources, which may result in the RPC framework not being scalable. In this paper, we propose LightRPC, which provides users with easy-to-use and portable interfaces via a new resource abstraction and achieves efficient performance through co-design of serialization and communication, usage of pre-registered memory, and adaptive polling mode. Compared to bRPC’s IPoIB and RDMA modes, LightRPC improves throughput by about 2.5x and 1.5x, respectively, and has lower median and tail latency.

articleTitle: A Joint Algorithm Based on Multi-Objective Optimal Power Allocation and Partial-Fixed Interference Alignment
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: This paper proposes a joint algorithm based on multi-objective optimization of power allocation and partial-fixed interference alignment in order to address the issues of inadequate selection of optimization objectives and slow convergence of interference alignment algorithm in the power allocation strategy. To begin with, three optimization goals throughput, interference leakage, and system power consumption are chosen to create a power allocation model, and then the transmitter pre-coding matrix is adjusted based on the channel state data, so that the receiver matrix does not need to be repeatedly computed to finish the interference alignment. The findings of the experiment demonstrate that the suggested algorithm offers considerable benefits in terms of system throughput, energy efficiency, transmission dependability, and lessening interference leakage.

articleTitle: A Semi-blind Source Separation Approach for simultaneous Acoustic Echo Cancellation and Speech Dereverberation
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: This paper presents a new algorithm based on independent vector analysis in a unified semi-blind source separation framework for acoustic echo cancellation (AEC) and speech dereverberation (DR). Due to time independence assumptions of speech signals, a special propagation process and a source model that is a Gaussian distribution with time-varying variance are combined to extract a clean signal in the short-time Fourier transform domain. Also, the proposed algorithm applies an online auxiliary-function-based independent vector analysis (AuxIVA) to avoid the problem of poor stability and slow convergence. Experimental results show the improvement of echo cancellation and speech dereverberation compared with the conventional AEC and the cascade algorithm of AEC and DR based on AuxIVA.

articleTitle: On the information transmission delay and algorithms of strong product digraphs
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The distance of digraphs is one of the most basic structural parameters in graph theory, and it plays an important role in analyzing the effectiveness of interconnection networks. In particular, it provides a basis for measuring the transmission delay of networks. When the topological structure of an interconnection network is represented by a digraph, the average distance of the directed graph is a good measure of the communication performance of the network. In this paper, we mainly investigate the distance and average distance of strong product digraphs, and using a new way to give a formula for the distance of strong product digraphs, and an algorithm for solving the average distance of strong product digraphs.

articleTitle: Reliability-Based HARQ: Performance Analysis and Segmented Optimization
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Reliability-Based hybrid automatic repeat request (RB-HARQ) scheme can reduce the amount of retransmission bits by retransmitting the most unreliable bits. In this work, we provide an approximate method for calculating the BER of retransmission frame of RB-HARQ scheme. Further, in order to lower the feedback overhead, we propose Segmented Reliability-Based HARQ (SRB-HARQ), choosing the most unreliable bit in every segment to retransmit, and the performance analysis is also given for SRB-HARQ. Both the theoretical analysis and simulation results can prove that the SRB-HARQ can reduce the feedback overhead and provide similar frame error rate (FER) of RB-HARQ at the same time.

articleTitle: Performance analysis of Mixed RF/FSO DF relay based on Low Density Parity Check (LDPC) codes using deep learning techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: This Cooperative optical communication allows a free-space optical network to coordinate antenna distribution and achieve dramatic performance gains similar to those of conventional MIMO systems. It enables significant improvements in terms of network capacity and coverage. Cooperative Free Space Optics (FSO) communication is one of the most promising technologies for the next generation of wireless optical communication networks. FSO systems are particularly attractive for problem last mile access by bridging fiber optic-based backbone connectivity and RF access networks. To address this practical deployment scenario, there has been increasing attention on so-called hybrid RF-FSO (dual-hop) systems where RF transmission is used at one hop followed by FSO transmission at the other. . In this article, we study the performance of hybrid RF/FSO cooperative systems based on error-correcting codes, particularly LDPC codes using an LDPC decoder based on deep learning.The use of mixed RF/FSO cooperative systems improves the reliability and transmission of the network. The results demonstrate improved performance of the LDPC code-based RF/FSO DF cooperative relay system using a deep learning-based LDPC decoder compared to LDPC code-based RF/FSO systems without the use of the deep learning, but also to the DF systems proposed in the existing literature.

articleTitle: Flexible Iterative Synthesis of Equiripple Filtering Functions
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: This paper presents an iterative synthesis method for equiripple filtering functions with great flexibility. It is not only suitable for the synthesis of single-band filtering functions but also can synthesize equiripple dual-band filters with fully prescribed performance. The proposed method can be used to synthesize symmetric or asymmetric responses, and the traditional generalized Chebyshev equiripple filter function can be seen as a case of the proposed method. Two substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) filters that one is bandpass filter and the other is dual-band are synthesized and designed to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: An Effective Task Migration Scheme Based on Intelligent Prediction in Mobile Edge Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: With the rapid growth of data from the Internet of Things (IoT), traditional centralized cloud computing is becoming overwhelmed and inefficient. Mobile edge computing offers a solution to address the limitations of centralized cloud computing, such as network latency, data security, and traffic congestion. Additionally, task migration among edge service nodes (ESNs) can enhance energy efficiency and optimize resource usage in mobile edge networks (MENs). However, excessive task migration may negatively impact the quality of service. In this paper, we propose an intelligent prediction-based energy-efficient (IPEE) task migration scheme that utilizes learning and prediction techniques to anticipate traffic load fluctuations in MENs. Compared to traditional greedy-based schemes, our IPEE scheme significantly reduces unnecessary migrations while improving energy efficiency. Simulation results demonstrate a reduction in migrations by over 30%.

articleTitle: XR perceived power saving and capacity enhancement technology
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Extended reality (XR) refers to all kinds of reality technologies, such as virtual reality (VR), augmented reality (AR), and mixed reality (MR). For XR services, a group of packets is used to carry the payload of a PDU set. Therefore, new PDU set parameters are introduced to support the XR traffic. In addition, due to the XR traffic periodicity being non-integer, the DRX cycle with rational number is introduced to reduce the power consumption. Furthermore, since there may exist multiple XR traffic and XR traffic may have pseudo periodicity, the enhanced CG mechanism is introduced to improve the system capacity. Finally, the numerical results show that multiple CG occasions in one CG configuration can improve the system capacity significantly.

articleTitle: Radar Waveform Recognition Based on Time and Phase Features Convolutional Network
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Low probability of intercept (LPI) radars, distinguished by their superior anti-interception performance, are extensively used. LPI Radar Waveform Recognition (RWR) is vital for electronic support systems. However, the contemporary deep learning (DL) based RWR is afflicted with high computational complexity and expansive network parameters. To meet the demands for precise and swift recognition of LPI radar waveforms, this paper introduces a low-complexity, lightweight model for RWR. This proposed method deviates from traditional approaches that use time-frequency transformation, instead utilizing a convolutional neural network to directly extract phase and short-time features from the raw signal. Thirteen distinct LPI RWR experiments validate the effectiveness of our proposed method, achieving over 90% accuracy even at an SNR of -4dB, with minimal cost. Our approach requires only 12% of the parameters and 0.14% of the computational resources compared to the Wigner-Ville distribution plus DL method, while still achieving higher accuracy. Additionally, our model achieves comparable accuracy to complex-valued neural networks while utilizing only half the parameters and one-sixth of the computational load. It has also demonstrated a significant speed advantage in real-world hardware tests.

articleTitle: Super-Resolution SAR Image Reconstruction via Deep Unfolding Network and Modified VGG Network
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) as an advanced remote imaging system is affected by its inherent speckle noise, atmospheric disturbances and motion blurring factors. In this paper, the problem to improve the resolution of SAR is considered in a practical scenario, and we present a super-resolution (SR) reconstruction method based on deep unfolding network and a modified very deep convolutional (VGG) network. Specifically, the degradation process of the SAR image is first predefined to decompose it into a data subproblem and a prior subproblem. Then, two subproblems are solved by neural modules, resulting in an end-to-end trainable and iterative network. A modified VGG network is used for multiplicative to additive noise fitting as a trained model. During the experiments of real SAR images, our method performs clearer visual effects than other super-resolution reconstruction and achieves better performance on peak signal-to-noise ratio.

articleTitle: Analysis of Training Methods for Deep Learning-based CSI Feedback
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The accuracy and overhead of Channel State Information(CSI) feedback are important for massive MIMO systems. As the scale of antennas increases, the contradiction between CSI accuracy and feedback overhead will become more severer. This paper first studies three training mechanisms for the popular transformer-based CSI feedback algorithm. Then, the algorithm is compared with the Type II codebook in 3GPP Release 16 in terms of both the Squared Generalized Cosine Similarity(SGCS) and User Perceived Throughput(UPT) under three training methods. Furthermore, we simulate its performance under various channel environments to verify its generalization capability, and analyze the complexity and feasibility of different training methods. The results show that with the same feedback overhead, the transformer-based CSI feedback can obtain about 6.5% SGCS gain and up to 15% UPT gain than the Release 16 Type II codebook. By choosing a reasonable training method, transformer-based CSI feedback can achieve good generalization with low training complexity.

articleTitle: Application and Development of 5G Technology in Smart Logistics Industry
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The rapid growth of logistics demand and the continuous emergence of new technologies and new management force traditional logistics enterprises to carry out transformation and upgrading, and the in-depth integration of the logistics industry with a new generation of information technology, such as 5G, artificial intelligence and cloud computing, can realize the transformation and upgrading of the logistics industry, reduce the cost of application of logistics enterprises and improve the operational efficiency of logistics enterprises. This article mainly summarizes the overview of smart logistics, the opportunities and challenges of logistics industry transformation, the application of 5G technology in the smart logistics industry, and the innovation of the smart logistics development models in the context of 5G, aiming to provide a reference for the development of the smart logistics system.

articleTitle: An Optimization Mechanism of Routing Protocol for Integrated CISR Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Due to the dynamic topology structure, high-speed mobility, and limited energy resources of Integrated Communication, Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance (CISR) Networks, we propose an Optimized Fish-eye Adaptive On-demand Distance Vector (FEAODV) routing protocol. Adaptive beam antenna and fish-eye technology are added to the traditional on-demand routing protocol, reducing the update frequency of remote node information, optimizing traffic control in the network. Due to signal interference, network congestion, dynamic topology, and long distances between UAVs, we also propose a cross-layer routing diagnostic policy determine the effectiveness of the route simultaneously with traffic transmission to verify the validity of the route. Simulation results show that the FEAODV protocol has significant advantages in reducing delay and routing overhead, improving group delivery rate of Integrated CISR Networks.

articleTitle: State-of-Health Estimation for Lithium-ion Batteries based on BiLSTM-WGAN
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: As an important parameter in the Electric Vehicle Battery Management System (BMS), the accuracy of State of Health (SOH) of Lithium-ion Batteries (LIBs) is crucial for promoting efficient battery utilization and ensuring human safety. However, due to factors such as complex experimental conditions and data security concerns, obtaining a sufficient quantity of high-quality battery data is exceedingly challenging, resulting in low accuracy in SOH estimation. To address this issue, a model based on BiLSTM-WGAN is proposed. This model is capable of capturing the temporal characteristics of dynamic battery cycling data, generating data under given conditions, thereby enhancing the accuracy of SOH estimation. Firstly, in order to capture the temporal characteristics of dynamic battery cycling data, a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network is used to establish the foundational model for the Generative Adversarial Network (GAN). Secondly, the loss functions of the generator and discriminator are improved using Wasserstein distance and Gradient Penalty (GP). Finally, the generated data and real data are mixed and fed into the SOH estimator constructed by BiLSTM. Experimental results demonstrate that this model can learn the probability distribution of real data, generate battery data under given conditions, and, after training on mixed datasets, achieve higher accuracy in SOH estimation compared to other methods.

articleTitle: Maximizing Coverage for Indoor NLoS mmWave Links by Deployment of Reflectors
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The usage of spectrum in the millimeter wave (mmWave) bands can significantly increase communication capacity. However, the high propagation loss and high sensitivity to obstacles of mmWave communication make it extremely dependent on Line-of-Sight (LoS) conditions. One of the efficient methods to improve the transmission condition is to deploy passive reflectors strategically. In this paper, we study an indoor coverage enhancement scenario with a passive reflector. We consider an indoor L-shaped corridor scenario, where the LoS link is blocked. To achieve the maximum coverage, we propose the Maximum Coverage using Reflectors (MCR) algorithm to find the optimal deployment position of the reflector, and we leverage Ray-Tracing (RT) software Wireless Insite to simulate the indoor experimental environment. Analytical and simulation results show that the optimal deployment location is within a range, and that the coverage trend with reflector size is independent of the transmit power, which are counter-intuitive findings.

articleTitle: Robustness Improvement of JTIDS Waveform in Saturated Layered Networks Using Spectrum Reshaping
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The Joint Tactical Information Distribution System (JTIDS), which serves as the communications carrier for Link 16, provides services for joint operations. With the increasing number of systems dependent on JTIDS terminals, the cascading network mode operating in a saturated state leads to frequent inter-network adjacent frequency interference. In this paper,we analysed the performance of Minimum Shift Keying (MSK) modulation and Gaussian Minimum Shift Keying (GMSK) modulation for JTIDS under different channel conditions, as well as the issue of mutual interference when multiple networks transmit data simultaneously in a time slot in a layered network operating in a saturated state. At the same time, a simulation platform is built for the JTIDS physical layer model with coding, spreading, hopping, and modulation capabilities, as well as channel models with Gaussian white noise, Rayleigh fading, and Rician fading. Simulations show that JTIDS robustness better with GMSK modulation than with MSK modulation under different channel modes. However, the performance of JTIDS is severely degraded in the presence of adjacent band interference.

articleTitle: FF-BCSD: A Binary code similarity detection method based on feature fusion
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: With the explosive growth of Internet of Things (IoT) devices, software engineers often reuse third-party code. If the security vulnerability is in the reused code, all downstream IoT components reusing this code will introduce the same vulnerability. To address this problem, we propose a binary code similarity detection method based on feature fusion. We construct features for instruction sequences and control flow graphs (CFGs) using deep learning models. These two features are fused to form the deep feature representation of a function as similarity measurement. Compared to Gemini and VulSeeker, our method has better results in accuracy, precision, recall, and F1. Besides, the experiment results show that deep feature representations perform better than the single feature in different scenarios.

articleTitle: Exploring the Dilemmas Faced by Depressed Patients in China Based on Deep Learning Methods
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Depression is a major global public health problem, with high prevalence, recurrence, and mortality rates, and is a significant factor contributing to the global disease burden. Depression has caused great harm to the health of patients. The purpose of the paper is to identify the problems faced by patients with depression, understand their needs, and provide evidence for medical institutions and society to better serve and help patients with depression. We collected posts and comments from the help-seeking module in an online depression community. The topics and emotions of text content were got by the BERTopic and BERT, respectively. The word co-occurrence network under each topic was constructed to analyze the dilemma faced by users. We divided user needs into 7 categories: doctor, medication, symptom, study, family, emotion, and work. In the help-seeking module, users receive not only information but also emotional support. Keywords under each topic and the word co-occurrence networks indicate that users have a lot of problems in the treatment of depression; they not only need the help of experienced patients but also need explanations and suggestions from doctors. There are a large number of adolescent patients in this community. How to help adolescent patients get effective and timely treatment and overcome study difficulties is a problem that these patients are concerned about, and it also needs to be solved by relevant sectors of society.

articleTitle: An Improved Syndrome Bit Flipping Decoder with Narrowed Flipping Set for LDPC Codes
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In this paper, we propose an improved Syndrome Bit Flipping (SBF) decoding algorithm that utilizes narrowed flipping set. The narrowed flipping set is prone to contain all error bit positions with high probability. To construct the narrowed flipping set, part of its elements are selected according to channel information, and the rest are constructed by random selections. The narrowed flipping set mitigates possible error propagation by avoiding some non-error bits being unnessary flipped, thereby further improving the decoding performance of the original SBF algorithm. The simulation results show that the proposed algorithm can achieve about 1.2 dB bit error rate gain compared with the original SBF algorithm, with a modest increase in computational complexity.

articleTitle: Fast Time-Varying Wireless Channel Prediction Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: This paper presents a channel prediction method based on deep temporal convolutional neural networks to accurately obtain channel information between different time slots. This method uses causal convolution and dilated convolution to capture the temporal correlations of historical Channel State Information (CSI) for predicting future CSI. The proposed method is evaluated using both original channel matrix coefficients generated by the simulation platform and measured Channel Quality Indicator (CQI) data as the CSI datasets, demonstrating its performance in both scenarios. Simulation results show that the proposed method outperforms the non-prediction and mainstream prediction methods, exhibiting superior prediction performance and adaptability to real-world environments.

articleTitle: Transmission Performance Analysis of Space Optical Communication Based on PPM in Atmospheric Channel
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The transmission performance of space optical communication based on pulse position modulation (PPM) in atmospheric channel is studied. We utilize the quantitative mathematical analysis to derive the bit error probability of PPM in atmospheric turbulence channel. The performance variations with different modulation order and turbulence intensity are quantitatively analyzed. Besides, on the basis of turbulence effect, we consider the phenomenon of pulse broadening induced by the scattering effect and further analyze the transmission performance. The bit error probability of PPM with higher modulation order will be subjected to the greater impact in the presence of the scattering effect.

articleTitle: Connected Components Labeling Algorithms: A Review
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Connected Components Labeling (CCL) is a technique to detect different objects in an image by assigning each object a unique label. CCL has been widely used in many applications. For example, in Computer-Aided Diagnosis (CADx), CCL is a vital preprocessing step in detecting pulmonary nodules in lung computed tomography (CT) images, and discovering masses in mammographic images. Over the past decades, a number of CCL algorithms have been proposed in literature. In this paper, these CCL algorithms are classified into contour tracing CCL algorithms and raster scan CCL algorithms according to their scanning order. This paper serves as a survey to review the major CCL algorithms in each category and explore the future direction in this research field.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Delay Imbalance in Redundant RRU Connections in 5G-R Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: To ensure the operational safety of high-speed trains, 5G-railway(5G-R) demands higher reliability compared to the public 5G network. It necessitates the adoption of Cross Connection Redundancy (CCR) technology, utilizing Remote Radio Units (RRUs). This study focuses on the analysis of delay imbalance issues introduced by CCR technology in the 5G-R system. This paper begins by introducing the system model of RRU redundancy and conducting an analysis of delay-related parameters. Subsequently, theoretical analysis and mathematical modeling explore the impact mechanism of these delay-related parameters on coverage performance. Finally, the theoretical analysis results are validated through simulation experiments, comparing the extent of the impact of delay variation on coverage performance. The experimental findings indicate that significant delay variations, when combined with RRU’s CCR technology, lead to a degradation in the coverage performance of the railway 5G-R communication system.

articleTitle: mFall: A Scenarios-Based Research on Human Fall Detection Leveraging Millimeter-Wave Sensing
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The issue of falls among the elderly is widely recognized globally, as falls often imply serious health risks. With the rapid development of technology, millimeter-wave (mmWave) sensing, due to its non-contact, continuous monitoring capabilities and higher safety and resolution, shows great potential in fall detection applications. However, current research still shows significant deficiencies in distinguishing between falls and non-falls in special scenarios and complex environments. Our research focuses on these deficiencies, collecting authentic human point cloud data. This includes basic daily activities as well as other common indoor movements that could be confused with falls. Then, we also gather point cloud data for irregular human activities introduced by complex scenarios. We use a sliding time window and convert the point cloud sequences into feature maps, which are then fed into the Deep Residual Network (ResNet). This process handles the spatio-temporal information contained in the point cloud data, ultimately yielding binary classification results. The system we develop shows efficiency in distinguishing between fall events and non-fall events, significantly improving the accuracy and reliability of fall detection, thereby offering a safe and accurate health monitoring solution for independently living seniors.

articleTitle: EEHF: Learning Event Argument Extraction from Hybrid Feedback
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The event argument extraction (EAE) task is aim to extract a structured event record from an event text. Most existing approaches need learn from well-labeled training set. Due to the expensive and time-consuming manual annotation cost, insufficient training data seriously hinders the EAE model from achieving better performance. In this paper, we propose Event argument Extraction with Hybrid Feedback (EEHF), which can use reinforcement learning to learn EAE task on unsupervised corpus. The hybrid feedback containing correctness feedback, reasonableness feedback and validity feedback to reward the model in various dimensions. The experiments show EEHF achieves new state-of-the-art on three benchmarks with a significant margin in the EAE task. Hybrid feedback can effectively align language models to EAE tasks.

articleTitle: Fine-Grained Task Offloading for UAV-Assisted Mobile Edge Computing
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: To solve the challenge of task offloading decisions and adaptive link selection of air-to-ground channels for UAV-assisted mobile edge computing, a fine-grained task offloading method is proposed. Firstly, an air-to-ground communication channel model is designed considering the probability of line-of-sight (LOS) and non-line-of-sight (NLOS) links in different signal propagation environments. On this basis, the task offloading optimization objective is defined to minimize the weighted value of delay energy consumption, and the impact of different weighted parameters on the task offloading algorithm is considered. Finally, a dynamic task offloading approach based on the depth deterministic strategy gradient algorithm is presented, and an efficient offloading scheme is obtained through adaptive learning of dynamic air-to-ground networks. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed approach effectively mitigates system energy consumption and reduces computational latency within UAV-assisted mobile edge computing systems, ensure system efficiency, stability and reliability, and better meet the service requirements of mobile edge users compared to other benchmark algorithms.

articleTitle: Grey Wolf Optimizer for enhancing local search based on population
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: To improve the convergence rate and avoid early maturity when using Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO) to solve the Traveling Salesman Problem (TSP), a Grey Wolf Optimizer for enhancing local search based on population (GWO-LSP) has been proposed.The grey wolf is divided into populations, and the GWO is iterated within the population and cross-genetically inherited between the populations to avoid falling into local optimum solutions,which improves the quality of the algorithm to solve the TSP problem. Meanwhile, the position update step of the grey wolf optimizer is optimized and improved, so that the iteration within populations and cross genetics between populations can be processed in parallel and the iteration speed is improved. By conducting on the TSPLib dataset experiments, the results show that the improved algorithm has the advantages of high solution quality and fast solution speed.

articleTitle: Resource Management Technology in Smart Grids enabled by Regional Energy Internet
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: There are numerous distributed new energy and diversified loads in the regional energy Internet. New business demands such as virtual power plant group dispatching and control, demand side response, and energy big data centers are constantly emerging, putting higher requirements on the reliability, security, and processing capacity of communication networks. As the core of the regional energy Internet, the power grid’s advanced communication and computing resources management is an effective way to meet the needs of the new business. In order to meet the differentiated requirements of services and security isolation, the network slicing technology is applied to the power grid. In this paper, we proposed a computing and bandwidth resource management scheme in smart grids enabled by regional energy Internet to reduce energy consumption and network delay. We modeled the joint allocation of bandwidth and computing resources of network slicing as a convex optimization problem, aiming to minimize the weighted sum of system delay consumption and computational energy consumption. The Lagrange multiplier iterative optimization method is used to solve the optimal allocation scheme of computing resources and bandwidth resources. The simulation results show that the proposed solution can meet the differentiated delay requirements of the service and effectively reduce the delay consumption and energy consumption of the system.

articleTitle: Airport video aircraft tracking and data fusion method at remote tower
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: To solve the problem that airport video data is single, low monitoring accuracy and flight information discrete at remote tower, airport video aircraft tracking and data fusion method at remote tower is proposed. Firstly, the global positioning coordinates and its corresponding images are collected in the camera's field of view. Then the relationship matrix between the GPS (Global Positioning System) coordinate system and image coordinate system is obtained by image homography model. Moreover, the pixel coordinates of the aircraft ADS-B (Automatic Dependent Surveillance – Broadcast) data is calculated by the combining the homography matrix and the aircraft GPS coordinates extracted from the civil aviation data; the aircraft positioning in video is obtained by detection and tracking algorithm. Finally, the relevant information is displayed in video by matching the aircraft trajectory and the ADS-B data trajectory. Experiments in typical airport show the proposed method can not only accurately detect the aircraft position, but also accurately display the corresponding flight information in video.

articleTitle: Algorithm Improvement and Modeling Analysis for SPMA
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The Statistical Priority-Based Multiple Access (SPMA) protocol is an access control protocol proposed to ensure the transmission quality of high-priority services in multi-priority service scenarios. In this paper, a double collision avoidance SPMA (DCA-SPMA) protocol is proposed. Two strategies, adaptive backoff mechanism and circular channel allocation, are used to reduce the probability of system collision. In addition, we have analyzed the state model of the nodes by establishing a two-dimensional Markov model. We focus on solving the average packet success rate and throughput. Finally, we analyze the impact of system parameters on the performance of the protocol. A comparison with CSMA/CA is also made. The simulation results prove the effectiveness of our proposed protocol.

articleTitle: Identifying Unconvincing User on Social Media with Limited Features
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Unconvincing users on social media are responsible for many malicious online activities. Therefore, developing classifiers to identify them is crucial. Due to the trade-off between the crawling costs of features and sample size, it remains challenging to distinguish unconvincing users from normal human users using limited features with low API call cost. To address the challenge, we present a case study where we develop machine learning-based classifiers with limited features to specifically identify a predefined category of unconvincing users: fake Twitter followers. Four models, namely Random Forest (RF), XGBoost, LightGBM, and Support Vector Machine (SVM) are employed and trained using a tabular dataset consisting of only 19 low-cost features. Experimental results show that the LightGBM classifier achieves the highest accuracy at 98.7%. Furthermore, feature importance analysis is carried out on LightGBM, and both SHAP analysis and Information Gain (IG) results indicate that the ratio between friends and followers is the most important feature.

articleTitle: Multi-modal Recommendation based on Knowledge Graph
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In recommendation tasks, data sparsity is a key problem that restricts the improvement of recommendation performance. Researchers usually use supplementary information, such as item attributes and user profiles, to alleviate the sparsity. In this paper, we consider both multi-modal features and knowledge graph as the supplementary information. The multimodal features can provide richer item properties from multiple perspectives, and from the knowledge graph, we can find latent connections between users and items. To fully utilize and combine these two kinds of supplementary information, we propose an end-to-end framework called MRKG. MRKG can adequately fuse the features of image and text modalities to capture users’ multi-modal preferences for items. And then the preferences are propagated and aggregated across the knowledge graph to obtain higher-order user representations for recommendation. We evaluate our method on MovieLens dataset. Experiments show that our model achieves the best performance compared to other recommendation models on both AUC and ACC metrics. In addition, we explore the influence of different multi-modal fusion methods though ablation study.

articleTitle: SDN-based Connectivity Restoration for Partitioned Flying Ad hoc Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
