abstract: Due to possible failure of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), a connected flying ad hoc network (FANET) may be divided into multiple sub-networks. In this case, the FANET connectivity should be restored in a short time and at a low cost. In this paper, we investigate the FANET connectivity restoration when a FANET is split. Firstly, in order to restore the FANET connectivity in a centralized manner, we propose a software-defined networking (SDN)-based FANET architecture. The process of FANET connectivity restoration is designed based on this architecture. Secondly, we propose a UAV scheduling algorithm based on greedy idea to calculate the position to which each mission UAV needs to move, so that the FANET connectivity can be restored through mission UAV movement. This algorithm should be invoked by the SDN controller. Numerical results show that our approach can restore the FANET connectivity with a lower total movement distance and a lower maximum movement distance than three other baselines.

articleTitle: Payload-based 5G Attack Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Due to the versatility and flexibility of 5G technology, its global adoption is increasing rapidly. The enhanced configurability of 5G-Core network makes it susceptible to attacks due to potential errors in complex configurations. As the web-based technologies and protocols used in the 5G Core architecture are widely adopted, additional efforts are essential to maintain the security of the 5G system. Therefore, 5G attack detection has received keen interest from research community. Machine learning based solutions provide an effective way of determining a potential threat and can function as a part of a versatile defense. In this paper, we proposed an ensemble approach for attack detection using Random Forest, Logistic Regression and Convolutional Neural Networks and performed evaluation using the 5GAD dataset. We evaluated the performance of each individual model component and compared them against the final ensemble approach. We further investigated the benefit of embedding layer on our proposed CNN architecture within the ensemble. We evaluated the performance of our methodology and achieved around 99% accuracy for the proposed method.

articleTitle: Channel state information feedback and reconstruction algorithm for massive MIMO based on joint attention mechanism neural networks
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: This paper studies the feedback and reconstruction of Channel State Information (CSI) in the downlink of FDD mode of massive multiple input multiple output (MIMO) system. Aiming at the problems such as high computational complexity and strict requirement on channel sparsity of traditional CSI feedback algorithms based on compressed sensing, and the problem that existing CSI feedback algorithms based on deep learning are insufficient in performance. A massive MIMO channel state information feedback and reconstruction algorithm based on joint attention mechanism neural network is proposed. And it includes a new CA-CsiNet neural network model based on auto-encoder neural network architecture. The attention mechanism algorithm is introduced into the encoder network to improve the feature extraction ability of the neural network effectively. Experimental results show that the proposed algorithm has better performance than traditional CSI feedback and reconstruction algorithms and existing deep learning algorithms.

articleTitle: A Style-Based Model for MRI to CT Image Translation
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The unsupervised generation of high-quality CT images remains an important and challenging problem. To obtain high-quality CT images, CT scans need to be performed on patients, which may result in radiation exposure and affect human health. In order to prioritize the health of patients, we attempt to estimate one modality of images from another modality, such as estimating CT images from MRI images. Therefore, we propose a novel framework for generating high-resolution CT images. Unlike previous encoder-based methods that can only predict latent codes from real images, our method maps the given medical images to the $\mathcal{W} + $ space and adjusts the generation details of medical images by modifying the variables in the $\mathcal{W} + $ space to ensure the generation of realistic high-resolution medical images. We generate a series of style vectors and then input them into a pre-trained StyleGAN to form an extended $\mathcal{W} + $ space. We assume that the latent vectors can be decomposed into content information and style information. To transform the images of MRI data into CT data, we combine the style information from the MRI images with the style information randomly sampled from the style space of the CT images, and finally generate realistic CT images by combining the content information from the CT images. We demonstrate a method for generating high-resolution medical images by manipulating latent style variables, which effectively yields a CT-like image without exposing the patient to radiation.

articleTitle: A Satellite-Terrestrial Integrated Network Architecture Based on Stateless Core Network
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Comprehensive coverage is a natural advantage of satellites, and loading the functions of base station on satellites can expand the service range of Satellite-Terrestrial Integrated Network(STIN), providing users with extensive and efficient access services. However, the management and control capabilities of satellite networks are inadequate, and this aspect has not been well investigated. The signalling from the control plane needs to be routed over the backhaul links to the Terrestrial Core Network(TCN) for processing which increases the service latency. In this paper, we propose a novel integrated core network architecture where satellites simultaneously have access and control capabilities by provisioning next-generation NodeB(gNB) and some core network functions. Considering the constrained satellite resources, we design a lightweight Stateless Satellite Core Network (SSCN) to enhance the flexibility and stability of the satellite network control. Meanwhile, based on SSCN, we redesign the registration, session establishment, and handover procedures to support mobility management and further reduce service latency. Simulation results show that the proposed integrated core network architecture improves the stability of mobility management and optimizes the network latency compared to the Non-Terrestrial Network(NTN) architecture in that satellites act as radio access networks only.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Approach for Event Extraction in Safety Production
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Event extraction aims to identify events of interest from unstructured text and represent them in a structured format. However, due to the diversity and complexity of events, the current accuracy of event extraction remains low, particularly for sentences containing multiple events. Furthermore, existing event extraction studies have primarily focused on domains such as news, finance, and biomedicine, with limited application in the field of safety production. To address these challenges, this paper divides the event extraction task into two phases tailored to the characteristics of the safety production domain: event triple extraction and event classification. This approach achieves the extraction of essential event information and the categorization of event types through a phase-based extraction method. By extracting event triples based on dependent syntactic analysis and semantic role annotation, we can successfully match 84.64% of events according to the template and structure the event representations. Subsequently, the event classification task is performed on the event triples using the ELECTRA_TextRCNN model. In comparison to the TextRCNN model, our proposed ELECTRA_TextRCNN model demonstrates a 9% improvement in accuracy and a 7% increase in F1 value. Ultimately, we have significantly enhanced the accuracy of event extraction in the safety domain through a two-stage approach.

articleTitle: Research on robot indoor automatic navigation algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: This paper first analyzes and compares the Dijkstra algorithm and the A* algorithm based on graph theory under the global path planning, and the comparison results show that the A* algorithm is more efficient than the Dijkstra algorithm. This paper uses the bidirectional path search strategy, evaluation function optimization and Open set optimization to improve the A* algorithm, and compares the traditional A* algorithm and the optimized A* algorithm by using MATLAB, and draws the conclusion that the improved A* algorithm has higher efficiency but more memory consumption.

articleTitle: Channel Modeling and Performance Analysis of RIS-Assisted MIMO Communications in High-Speed Rail Tunnels
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: As a typical application scenario of the fifth-generation(5G) mobile communication system, the high-speed mobile scenario attracts much attention and the tunnel is a typical application scenario for high-speed rail communication. As one of the key beyond 5G(B5G) technologies with the greatest development, Reconfigurable Intelligence Surface(RIS) has the advantages of low complexity, low cost, and easy deployment, providing new opportunities for the development of communications in 5G smart high-speed rail tunnel scenarios. The traditional high-speed rail communication in the tunnel is covered by leaky coaxial cables. The spectrum efficiency of the communication system covered by leaky coaxial cables is limited by deployment and is difficult to significantly improve. Based on the fixed scatterer distribution characteristics in the tunnel and considering the angular relationship between the transmitter, the reflecting surface, and the receiver, the deployment position and quantity of RIS are designed. The paper considers deploying RIS at the top inside the tunnel, thereby establishing a single-bounced channel model for RIS-assisted wireless communication. The model considers the direct path from the transmitter to the receiver and the assisted path provided by the RIS, supporting the deployment of multiple RIS relays. Under this model, the paper carries out a simulation evaluation for RIS-assisted MIMO communication. The simulation results show that the introduction of RIS can effectively expand coverage and demonstrate that the large size and appropriate location of the RIS can significantly improve the channel capacity.

articleTitle: Time-domain Turbo Equalization for DVB-RCS2 Satellite Return Link in NTN-TDL Channel
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: This article models the satellite broadband channel of the second generation return channel satellite for digital video broadcasting (DVB-RCS2) using the Non Terrestrial Network Tapped Delay Line (NTN-TDL) model of the 3rd Generation Partnership Project (3GPP) and modifies the DVB-RCS2 satellite return link. A suitable time-domain turbo equalization structure is presented, and two equalization methods based on minimum mean-square error (MMSE) and maximum-likelihood sequence estimation (MLSE) principles are deduced. Then, to realize the soft output of the MLSE-based turbo equalization, a non-binary soft output Viterbi algorithm (SOVA) suitable for high-order modulation schemes of DVB-RCS2 is given. The simulation results show that for DVB-RCS2 satellite return link in NTN-TDL channel, the MLSE-based turbo equalization has a lower burst error rate, and its performance approximates to the performance in the additional white gaussian noise (AWGN) channel when the code rate is low. When the reference waveforms with higher code rate and shorter burst length, and the performance gap between the MLSE-based turbo equalization and the MMSE-based method is larger.

articleTitle: Heterogeneous Laplace Distribution Noise Background Modeling for Sperm Detection in Microscopic Images
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Semen quality assessment is a very important tool for the timely detection and treatment of infertility disorders. Many artificial intelligence methods for sperm image analysis have emerged in recent years. Sperm detection in sperm microscopy is the first step in semen quality assessment. However, the acquisition of sperm electron microscopy images can produce a variety of different background lighting situations. The performance of established methods is susceptible to changes in background illumination. Therefore, a sperm detection method with heterogeneous Laplacian distribution noise background modeling (HLDNBM) is proposed. In this paper the method uses background illumination surface fitting to eliminate the effect of illumination in a single sperm image, and realizes the segmentation of sperm head and sperm tail with different grayscale by upper and lower segmentation threshold surfaces to achieve complete sperm image segmentation and multi-target detection in a single image. This method effectively avoids the degradation of target detection performance caused by sudden changes in illumination in other background modeling methods. Moreover, this method shows strong adaptability for images with different lighting backgrounds, and is friendly to small datasets as well. The experimental results show that the accuracy and sensitivity of the algorithm for sperm detection in images with different grayscale characteristics are very promising, with high universality and robustness.

articleTitle: Design of Underwater Coaxial Cable Communication System Based on ARM Cortex-M3
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: This article designs and implements an underwater coaxial cable communication system based on ARM Cortex-M3. This article introduces for overall system design, system hardware design, coaxial cable transmission line model research, and system software design. After multiple tests, the communication system is stable and has a low packet loss rate, which has reference significance for data transmission of baseband coaxial cables.

articleTitle: An Efficient Puncturing Scheme for Polar Codes Based on Fixed Information Set
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: For traditional polar codes, the code length is limited to a power of two, due to the use of the 2×2 kernel matrix. To obtain flexible code lengths, puncturing is widely considered for polar codes. In this paper, we propose an efficient puncturing scheme based on fixed information set (FIS) of the mother code. First, we estimate the qualities of bit channels using the Gaussian approximation after puncturing. In addition, the search scope of punctured bits in the codeword is significantly reduced to the number of frozen bits. Furthermore, a computationally efficient method for selecting the most promising puncturing pattern is employed. Moreover, a low-complexity recursive method is leveraged to construct the puncturing pattern. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed puncturing scheme outperforms the state-of-the-art FIS-based puncturing schemes remarkably in terms of error-correction performance.

articleTitle: Index-Based Mode Adjustment for Energy Saving of Service Vehicles and Robots in Vehicular Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Vehicular networks with service robots and vehicles have been widely studied in the past few years, and a large number of these vehicles and robots may appear in people's lives, such as in science and technology park, university town, restaurant, and public transportation hub. Energy-saving in vehicular networks becomes a key issue in these scenarios for ensuring the endurance time of vehicles and robots, so it is useful to dynamically adjust their working modes based on the pedestrian flow density around them. In this paper, we predict the peaks and troughs of the pedestrian flow based on four technical indexes, and adjust between active and ordinary modes for the vehicles and robots to save their energy while still guaranteeing their services. Simulation results show that the used technical indexes can predict the peaks and troughs of a pedestrian flow, hence the proposal effectively reduces the energy consumption of the vehicular networks.

articleTitle: Real-Time Automatic Modulation Recognition Based on FPGA
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: This paper presents a real-time automatic modulation recognition scheme that can implement deep learning algorithm on Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) to meet the performance and power requirements of real-time signal processing in edge computing scenarios. The proposed convolution neural network (CNN), using very few parameters and multiplications/additions, can recognize the modulation types of the wireless signals with high accuracy according to the In-phase and Quadrature component. Then the CNN model is compressed by Int8 quantization and deployed on FPGA fabric for real-time and low-power embedded computing, while maintaining recognition accuracy close to the software performance. The measurement results show that the performance in terms of latency and energy consumption greatly improved compared with other embedded platforms. When compared to other FPGA implementation, the proposed scheme achieves the same performance with fewer hardware resources.

articleTitle: Multi-Relational Knowledge Enhanced Contrastive Learning for Event Extraction
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Event extraction (EE) is a fundamental task under the field of natural language processing. Most of the existing EE methods perform supervised fine-tuning, training downstream with the help of the ability to pre-train language models (PLMs), limited labeled data is difficult to satisfy the training needs of PLMs and faces problems such as limited generalization. Contrastive learning, as a self-supervised training paradigm, improves the representational power of PLMs by acquiring a wider range of knowledge from large-scale unlabeled corpora than is implied by the data labels. However, existing contrastive learning methods mainly focus on the sentence-level, while the development at the token-level represented by EE tasks is still in its early stages, resulting in noisy representations of tokens and a lack of detailed use of event knowledge, which makes the performance bottleneck of the PLMs after contrastive learning when fine-tuning downstream EE tasks. To this end, we propose MRKE-CLEE, a multi-relational knowledge enhanced contrastive learning for event extraction. MRKE-CLEE first accomplishes the coreference resolution and AMR parsing as supported tasks to obtain multiple event-relationship knowledge pseudo-labels from a large-scale unlabeled corpus through the auxiliary model, then uses in-sentence knowledge guided contrast to filter noisy contrastive pairs to make the resulting token representations more distinct, and using event type knowledge guided contrast to aggregate token representations with the same event type. With the combination of multi-relational event knowledge, using contrastive learning to improve the performance of event detection (ED) and event argument extraction (EAE). Experiments demonstrate that our MRKE-CLEE achieves a new state-of-the-art performance on the ACE2005 and MAVEN datasets and introduces new attempts to use token-level contrastive learning in EE tasks.

articleTitle: Resource Trading Incentive Mechanism Based on Stackelberg Game and Auction Theory in Computing Power Network
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Computing power network (CPN) is a new architecture proposed in recent years. It has integrated multidimensional resources, such as computing, network and storage resources in cloud, edge and end to realize more flexible resource allocation and task scheduling. Consumers in CPN want to purchase some resources to meet their service demands and gain some profits, while operators would like to obtain payments by selling their idle resources to others. However, consumers usually prefer to purchase resources from large and public cloud operators in reality, while small and private operators who lack the recognition struggle to obtain the opportunity to join in the sales. Therefore, both parties may lack the passion and enthusiasm to participate in CPN transaction and there is a great need for a resource trading incentive mechanism. In this paper, we propose a three-tier joint optimization framework to increase their motivations and establish a centralized computing service platform (CSP). We use the Stackelberg game to describe the resource-purchasing process of computing service demanders (CSDs) and use the auction theory to describe the task-scheduling process of computing service operators (CSOs). In this way, both parties can gain their profits so that they will have a greater willingness to participate in the transaction. The simulation results demonstrate the feasibility and superiority of our scheme.

articleTitle: Scalable Transmission of Convolutional Neural Network Weights in the Frequency Domain
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Considering the big size of a typical convolutional neural network (CNN) model, it is difficult to transmit all the CNN weights within a limited latency. In this paper, a scalable transmission scheme for CNN weights is proposed. Firstly, all weights are transformed to the frequency domain. Then the frequency coefficients are divided into segments of different priorities. Finally, the segments are transmitted sequentially with a priority-based method. To further reduce the cost of transmission, the coefficients of different segments are quantized with a priority related bit-width. The simulation results show that the frequency segment of the highest priority can perform inference task independently and the performance of inference task can be improved when more segments of lower priorities are transmitted.

articleTitle: X-Band 25 W High PAE Power Amplifier MMIC with Second Harmonic Suppression for Radar Network Application
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: This letter introduces a high-power-added efficiency (PAE) and high second harmonic suppression (SHS) power amplifier monolithic microwave integrated circuit (MMIC) designed for operation in the frequency range from 8.5 GHz to 10.5 GHz. The design is based on a 0.25 µm gallium nitride (GaN) high electron mobility transistor (HEMT) process. To achieve high power gain, a three-stage amplifier structure is employed. Additionally, a SHS topology is incorporated in the output matching network to enhance harmonic suppression while maintaining high efficiency. The measurement results showed that the output power is around 45 dBm, the PAE ranges from 41.0% to 51.7%, the SHS exceeds 54 dBc from 8.5 GHz to 10.5 GHz. Furthermore, the size of the PA is 3.5 × 3.2 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Compared to other reported MMICs with similar size, this design exhibits significantly higher PAE and higher SHS.

articleTitle: Low Cost Massive Array with Ultra-wideband and High Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: A novel low cost massive array is described for ultra wideband RF and microwave communication applications. The usual Marchand balun is replaced with the tapered slotline balun and a lumped matching network is employed to obtain high impedance transformation efficiency operating from 222MHz to 2000MHz. The average total radiation efficiency is above 80% throughout the whole a 9:1 bandwidth. The design is based on FR4 ordinary materials, which can reduce the fabrication cost of a wideband phased array especially in the ultrashort wave band. The balanced tapered-slot dipole uses a top coupling design to facilitate the modularization and connection between subarrays. The array can scan to ±60° in both E plane and H plane and the spacing between elements is 77mm, which is greater than λ/2 of the highest frequency. A closed finite array prototype of 8×9 dual polarized elements is proposed to weaken the cutoff influence of edge ports and has been verified by the full wave simulation. An amplitude-phase optimization algorithm is applied to achieve the desired results for the finite array. The instantaneous full frequency results of active VSWRs and realized gain patterns show that the proposed method can further improve the whole aperture performance.

articleTitle: Efficient Neighbor Discovery for Wide-Range FANET with Non-Uniform Directional Beams
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Directional antennas are increasingly used to meet the demand for anti-interference ability and high transmission rates in Flying Ad-hoc Network (FANET). However, it may experience poor efficiency in network connections for highly dynamic FANET scenarios. This work focuses on the neighbor discovery scheme in the initial establishment of wide-range FANET (wFANET) using directional antennas, which has been overlooked in previous studies. Considering the limitation of flight altitude, a non-uniform beam pattern is designed in order to minimize the beam positions while satisfying the communication requirements. Based on such beam arrangement, the optimized transmitting probability is calculated for a 2-way handshake process to maximize the likelihood of successful neighbor discovery. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed scheme has advantages in improving neighbor discovery efficiency compared to the scheme under uniform beam design.

articleTitle: Transmission Line Insulator Defect Detection Based on Enhanced YOLOv5n
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: To meet the inspection requirements for insulators on power transmission lines, this article proposes an improved algorithm based on YOLOv5n. First, the FasterNet Block is employed to replace the Bottleneck in the C3 module of YOLOv5n, reducing redundant computations and memory accesses. Then, the Dyhead (Dynamic Head) module is introduced to integrate scale-aware, spatial-aware, and task-aware attention mechanisms simultaneously, enhancing the detection capability of insulator defects in complex environments. Finally, the Normalized Wasserstein Distance (NWD) is introduced into the loss function calculation to mitigate the sensitivity of IoU-based metrics to small target position deviations, thus improving the detection capability for small-sized insulator defects. Experimental results show that compared to the original YOLOv5n, the insulator defect Average Precision (AP) improved by 1.9%, mAP improved by 1.8%, and parameters and FLOPs were reduced by 8.5% and 4.9%, respectively. Compared to YOLOv7-tiny, the insulator defect AP increased by 1.7%, while parameters and FLOPs were only 26.7% and 29.5% of YOLOv7-tiny. The proposed algorithm allows for more accurate detection of insulator defects with lower model complexity.

articleTitle: Time Series Forecast of Air Travel Demands with Considering the Influences of New Routes
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In this paper, A hybrid SARIMA-RF model is proposed to the practical problem of the air travel demand forecast, considering the scenario of carrying out new route. The Seasonal Auto Regressive Integrated Moving Average (SARIMA) model is generated to deal with the air travel demand, while the Random Forecast (RF) is generated as the demand stimulus model to deal with those markets with the influences of new routes, which the SARIMA can not give a good forecast result. The experiment with actual airline market data is carried out to validate the performance of the proposed model, and the results show that the SARIMA-RF model has a better performance with smaller forecast error than the original SARIMA time series forecast model in the markets with the new routes.

articleTitle: A Virtual Network Topology Spoofing Defense Method Based On DCGAN
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Aiming at network scanning and sniffing attacks, this paper designs an active defense mechanism based on virtual network topology, which generates a large number of random and independent fake networks through generative adversarial networks, and uses the traffic traction capability of software-defined networks to trick attackers into accessing preset defense hosts, making it impossible to detect the real internal network topology, and it is difficult to collect the element information required for attacks, such as key link sets and sensitive server collections. Experiments show that compared with the relevant defense mechanism, the proposed method has obvious advantages in protecting the server response experiment and file transfer rate.

articleTitle: AoI-Aware Resource Allocation in MIMO Video Transmission Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In video-assisted scenarios such as live events, remote surgery, autonomous driving and so on, age of information (AoI) can be used as a quality of service (QoS) metric for evaluating video transmission quality in conjunction with effective capacity (EC) due to its unique property of portraying the freshness of information. In this paper, we propose a Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) downlink video transmission system and apply the AoI model of the idealized service process to the video transmission system to obtain an upper bound on the peak AoI violation probability. Considering the limited resource and the information freshness requirements of video users simultaneously, we formulate the total effective capacity maximization problem. By decomposing the original problem into two resource allocation subproblems, an iterative resource allocation algorithm is proposed to find the optimal solution. The simulation results show that the proposed algorithm has good convergence performance and can obtain the corresponding optimal EC values for different numbers of users. Meanwhile, the optimal EC value in the proposed algorithm is greater than that in the two baselines.

articleTitle: Enhance Engineering Pedagogy in Programming Course via Knowledge Graph-Based Recommender System
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Purpose: There is a lack of suitable recommendation systems to assist engineering teaching. The existing traditional engineering pedagogies lack learning interests for postgraduate students. The knowledge graph-based recommender system aims to enhance postgraduate students’ programming skills, with a focus on programming courses. Design/methodology/approach: The case study will be used as a major research method, and the two case studies will be taken in both two teaching styles of the universities (Zhejiang University and the University of Nottingham Ningbo China), followed by the interviews. Quantitative and qualitative research methods will be combined in this study. Research limitations/implications: The case studies were only focused on two teaching styles universities, which is not comprehensive enough. The subject was limited to postgraduate students. Originality/value: The study collected and analyzed the data from two teaching styles of universities’ perspectives. It explored the challenges of Engineering education and tried to seek potential enhancement.

articleTitle: BBPM: A Study of Information Pre-retrieval Models Based on Medical BERT Model
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: This study focuses on the preprocessing of medical paper retrieval, aiming to address the challenge of extracting information from lengthy medical texts. This process is crucial in facilitating effective medical research. We propose BioBERT Preprocessing Model (BBPM). By employing the cutting-edge medical BERT model, we predict the subject words of the paper’s abstract. Subsequently, based on these subject words, we calculate secondary similarity using the corresponding medical model. Finally, we incorporate the most strongly associated words to augment the associative vocabulary of the article, thereby enhancing its effectiveness in subsequent text retrieval. Experimental results show that BioBERT shows superior performance in predicting subject words in long medical texts, with a basic text similarity of about 90%. The primary contribution of this paper lies in the integration of the latest BioBERT model for preprocessing the abstracts of medical papers. This yields additional subject terms necessary for retrieval. These terms are then integrated with the title keywords into the final retrieval system, leading to more efficient retrieval outcomes. This approach promises to provide fresh insights into medical information retrieval.

articleTitle: Optimal Refinery Crude Oil Scheduling Based on Proximal Policy Optimization
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Currently, most refinery crude oil scheduling studies adopt static scheduling schemes based on mathematical programming, which cannot adjust and optimize according to environmental change in real-time. This paper establishes a dynamic real-time scheduling decision model subject to refinery production constraints and designs the corresponding agent interaction environment. The proximal policy optimization (PPO) algorithm in deep reinforcement learning solves the model. The performance of the strategies learned in each production link is evaluated and analyzed through experiments, and the adaptability of the model is evaluated under the uncertain condition of the arrival time of the tanker. The results demonstrate that this model can obtain scheduling results compatible with business evaluation, thus effectively reducing the influence of random events on the overall decision and improving the performance and stability of crude oil scheduling.

articleTitle: Secret Carriers Intelligent Management and Controlling System Based on RFID
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: With the automation of national command, office information, and application networking, the secret carrier is an important means of storing and exchanging secret information, which greatly enhances the overall efficiency of the work of the military, but also gives national defense and military secret security major security risks. Facing the practical needs of the use and management of secret carriers, comprehensively using technologies such as RFID, artificial intelligence, and context awareness, through the purchase of RFID readers, exciters, custom RFID electronic tags, and management of servers and terminals to build hardware systems, comprehensive application of secret carrier intelligent control model, through programming tools, SDK development kit of the RFID reader and database implement the software system, including basic information maintenance, confidential carrier management, access registration management, online monitoring management, anti-lost alarm management, system maintenance, reader configuration and in-place query. The system can solve the problem of management and control of secret carriers from manual operation to automatic detection, precise monitoring, and intelligent decision-making, has significant military and economic benefits with technology to resolve security risks.

articleTitle: Probability Shaping for High-Order Systems with DSC-LDPC Codes
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The research on joint source-channel coding (JSCC) systems primarily employs low-order BPSK modulation. However, such low spectral efficiency modulation schemes cannot meet the demands of future high-speed communication. In real-world scenarios, source probabilities are often unequal. Therefore, introducing high-order modulation with a probability shaping model, combined with dual spatially coupled low-density parity-check (DSC-LDPC) codes, can better exploit system performance and further increase throughput.Utilizing the remaining source redundancy to achieve amplitude shaping gains, a novel approach called joint source-channel coded modulation (JSCCM) is proposed, serving as a solution based on probabilistic amplitude shaping (PAS). This paper suggests the combination of quadrature amplitude modulation (QAM) modulation with a DSC-LDPC-JSCC system and examines whether probability shaping techniques can further enhance the system.

articleTitle: Intelligent Decision Algorithm for Downlink Anti-Jamming of Measurement and Control System Based on DDPG
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Aiming at the problem that the downlink of the aerospace measurement and control system has weak anti-dynamic interference performance in the dynamic interference environment, this paper proposes an anti-interference intelligent decision-making algorithm based on Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG), and applies it to the system, which increases the anti-dynamic interference performance of the system. In this paper, the downlink structure of the measurement and control system is given, and an intelligent decision-making algorithm based on DDPG and the performance evaluation function are designed. The simulation results show that compared with the decision-making algorithm based on rule inference and neural network, the bit error rate (BER) of the proposed algorithm can be reduced by an order of magnitude in the face of dynamic interference, which can significantly increase the transmission performance of the measurement and control system.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of CNC Programming Technology Based on Process Fusion
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Aiming at the problems of machining redundancy and rough process intersection caused by the existing single-process machining CNC programming method, a CNC programming technology based on process fusion is proposed after analyzing the polygon clipping algorithm for machining path optimization. Firstly, the geometric characteristics of the process are analyzed, and the actual machining problem is transformed into a polygon clipping problem, thus establishing a mathematical model to solve it. Secondly, a new data structure and polygon clipping algorithm are designed to speed up problem solving. Finally, the process sequence is fused to generate a more efficient and reliable process execution flow. Through simulation experiments, the CNC programming technology based on process fusion is compared with the traditional CNC programming technology, and has significant advantages in improving machining efficiency and quality.

articleTitle: Enhancing Economic Security in Blockchain-Based Spectrum Trading: A Stablecoin Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In the research of the spectrum blockchain, more attention is often paid to how the blockchain architecture can achieve efficient spectrum access, neglecting the implementation details of "currency for spectrum trading". However, a robust security mechanism is crucial for the spectrum allocation system, and the potential economic risks brought by digital currency must be carefully considered. This article presents a comprehensive approach to address these concerns. Firstly, we propose a multi-entity spectrum trading system based on blockchain and mobile edge computing (MEC). Secondly, we introduce a stable spectrum currency called SCoin, which incorporates a "dual-token" function achieved through coupling the consensus mechanism with the spectrum market cycles. SCoin serves a dual purpose within the spectrum market as a stable transaction currency and an economic incentive. In addition, we introduce a set of stakes specifically designed for DPoS-based wireless blockchains. Considering the interference factor in stake assessment facilitates a direct evaluation of node effectiveness in the system. The simulation results show that our SCoin design can well maintain the stability of the SCoin’s price. In summary, SCoin provides a clear strategy that utilizes digital cryptocurrency to facilitate blockchain-based spectrum trading while enhancing economic security.

articleTitle: Modelling of Received Power Measurement Based on Reference Signal in 5G-700M Band
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The 700MHz band is the golden band among wireless frequencies, and with the 700MHz band being divided under the 5G communication system, it effectively solves the problem of weak 5G signal coverage capability, and at the same time provides new ideas for solving the problems of difficult network coverage in remote mountainous areas and emergency protection. In this paper, the Reference Signal Receiving Power (RSRP) is used as an example, and the 700MHz band parameters are paired and simulated by MATLAB software. Based on the free space loss, a 700MHz band path loss calculation method based on RSRP and path loss is proposed according to the idea of average power method. The correctness of the measurement model is verified by comparing the SS-RSRP values in the real environment and the values simulated by the loss model.

articleTitle: A Dual Channel MAC Protocol with IRS Relay Selection Mechanism for Terahertz Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The demand for high-speed data transmission in 6G networks has triggered the urgent need for research on terahertz (THz) communication frequency bands. However, the THz directional transmission and rapid attenuation in the air pose a challenge to the design of Medium Access Control (MAC) protocols. In this paper, a novel Terahertz Dual Channel MAC Protocol based on IRS Relay Selection (RS-MAC) is proposed, which leverages GHz frequency band for control signaling and employs THz beams for data transmission. Firstly, we introduce a Joint Judging Line-of-Sight (LoS) Algorithm Based on Location and Angle Information (LA-LoS) to determine whether LoS exist between the transmitter and receiver. Moreover, we capitalize on the unique reflection characteristics of Intelligent Reflection Surface (IRS) technology to introduce IRS relay paths at the MAC layer, reducing relay delay and enhancing data transmission efficiency. In the end, numerical simulations were conducted to analyze the performance improvements. The results indicate that, compared with some existing MAC relay protocols, the proposed protocol exhibits a substantial reduction in THz transmission delay and an improvement in achievable throughput.

articleTitle: Enhancing Architectural Information Extraction Using DHAM-based Segmentation Network
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In response to the challenges faced in acquiring datasets for building defect segmentation algorithms, and the narrow, elongated nature of defect areas that can contain a variety of composite defects, rendering existing segmentation networks ineffective, an attention-mechanism-based human feedback reinforcement learning algorithm for building defect segmentation has been proposed. The design of the reward network is first carried out, and the information extraction ability of the reward network is enhanced by introducing a deep mixed multi-scale attention mechanism, thus reducing the number of iterations. Subsequently, by improving the deep deterministic policy gradient, human feedback is integrated into the reinforcement learning framework for the overall algorithm design. Experimental results demonstrate that, compared with existing supervised segmentation networks, the proposed algorithm reduces the per-pixel cross-entropy loss by 3.52%, and compared with unsupervised segmentation networks, it reduces this loss by 7.43%. In addition, the algorithm exhibits superior results in terms of recall, precision, and other metrics.

articleTitle: The Prediction Method of Airport Emergency Rescue Materials Based on Historical Data
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Based on the analysis of the technical research status of emergency rescue material allocation in civil transportation airports and the current situation of emergency rescue material allocation in domestic civil airports, this article studies the applicability of commonly used methods for predicting the number of emergency rescue materials. Given the complexity of emergency rescue materials in civil transportation airports and the scarcity of historical data samples, the grey system theory is utilized as the basic technology to provide a synchronous prediction workflow and model for various emergency rescue materials. Finally, this article validates the proposed method using real data on the allocation and consumption of emergency rescue materials at a large civil airport in China.

articleTitle: Short-term wind power forecast based on Long Short Term Memory
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: As the impact of climate change on the environment increases, the demand for new energy sources is growing. In the development of renewable energy, wind power generation is an important technology that can use wind energy to generate electricity. However, due to its unstable nature, the forecasting of wind power generation has become one of the most important problems in wind farm management. In this paper, historical wind power data is selected as input to establish a wind power prediction model based on Long Short Term Memory (LSTM). By training LSTM model, the prediction of wind power in next 12 hours is realized. Result shows that the model has certain feasibility and accuracy, can accurately predict the future short-term wind power generation, and has a wide range of application value.

articleTitle: Design of low power LSTM neural network accelerator based on FPGA
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The continuous progress of artificial intelligence has led to the great success of LSTM neural networks in various fields, and with the changing application scenarios, the design of hardware gas pedals for LSTM neural networks has become a hot topic of discussion today. Compared with CPUs, GPUs, and ASICs, FPGAs have the unique advantages of low resource consumption, low power consumption, high energy efficiency, and high flexibility in accelerating deep learning, making them the preferred platform for hardware implementation of neural networks. Improving LSTM accuracy comes at the cost of a larger network model, and a larger model represents a more significant power consumption. How to guarantee the operation of neural network gas pedals under resource constraints has become a considerable research hotspot. This paper proposes a low-power FPGA-based LSTM neural network gas pedal through parameter quantization, weight pruning combination, and other methods; after the training of the MINST dataset, this hardware gas pedal can realize the inference process of the neural network while having 80% accuracy, the web-based on Xilinx Virtex VC-707 FPGA board to complete the design and testing. Experimental results show that the proposed method consumes only 0.986W, 2-40 times less power than similar designs.

articleTitle: Generalized Huygens–Fresnel Principle
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In classical electrodynamics, the famous Huygens– Fresnel principle is usually expressed in terms of some convolution integral formulations (CIFs). The conventional CIFs are generalized in this paper. The generalized CIFs are applicable to the simply connected dielectric scatterer, multiply connected dielectric scatterer, multi-body dielectric scattering system, and conductor-dielectric composite scattering system. In the various scatterers and scattering systems, the dielectric part can be either homogeneous isotropic or inhomogeneous anisotropic. For the various scatterers and scattering systems, the generalized CIFs can formulate the external scattered field, internal scattered field, internal incident field, and internal total field of the scatterers and scattering systems.

articleTitle: Terahertz-Empowered Communications and Sensing in 6G Systems: Opportunities and Challenges
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The current focus of academia and the telecommunications industry has been shifted to the development of the six-generation (6G) cellular technology, also formally referred to as IMT-2030. Unprecedented applications that 6G aims to accommodate demand extreme communications performance and, in addition, disruptive capabilities such as network sensing. Recently, there has been a surge of interest in terahertz (THz) frequencies as it offers not only massive spectral resources for communication but also distinct advantages in sensing, positioning, and imaging. The aim of this paper is to provide a brief outlook on opportunities opened by this under-exploited band and challenges that must be addressed to materialize the potential of THz-based communications and sensing in 6G systems.

articleTitle: Far-Field to Near-Field Transformations for Antenna, Free-Space Waveguide, and Scatterer
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The energy-viewpoint-based methods for calculating the energy-decoupled modes (DMs) of antenna, free-space waveguide, and scatterer are simply reviewed. Some far-field to near-field transformation methods for antenna, free-space waveguide, and scatterer are proposed by using the DM-based modal expansions. The DM-expansion-based far-field to near-field transformation methods have the following two main advantages over the conventional multipole-expansion-based far-field to near-field transformation method: 1) the former can calculate the fields inside the circumscribing spheres of antenna and scatterer, but the latter cannot; 2) the former does not have any restriction on the shape of the input port of free-space waveguide, but the latter is only applicable to the free-space waveguide whose input port is a spherical surface.

articleTitle: Low-Rank Approximation in Kernel Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The kernel matrix plays a pivotal role in kernel learning and spatial statistics. This paper contends that under a broad range of conditions, the kernel matrix becomes ill-conditioned as the matrix dimension significantly increases. This ill-condition can lead to computational breakdowns in some algorithms and substantial output variation in response to minor alterations of input variables. Low-rank approximation emerges as a potent solution to mitigate this ill-condition problem. Through a comprehensive numerical study, we contrast various low-rank approximations, offering insightful guidance on the selection of a suitable low-rank approximation for practical application.

articleTitle: Screen Recognition: Creating Accessibility Metadata for Mobile Applications using View Type Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Many accessibility features available on mobile platforms require applications (apps) to provide complete and accurate metadata describing user interface (UI) components. Unfortunately, many apps do not provide sufficient metadata for accessibility features to work as expected. In this paper, we utilize the relevant data information that can be obtained from the terminal to detect the type of each View in the display interface, and we can also perform finer division based on this information. In order to achieve this method, we collected the feature information of View under multiple scenarios in the normal use of the three mainstream and representative apps, including Today's Headlines, Tiktok and WeChat, and manually calibrated the type of View to establish a database containing more than 40000 pieces of data. By utilizing the layout features, structural features, and attribute features of View to learn and predict the type of View, a detection system has been implemented that can accurately predict the type of unknown View. This system can accurately predict the type of an unknown View, with a prediction accuracy of over 95% for known apps and relatively accurate predictions for unknown apps.

articleTitle: Energy Transport Theorem (ETT)-Based Decoupling Mode Theory (DMT) for Microstrip Transmission Lines and Power Dividers
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: An energy-viewpoint-based electromagnetic modal analysis method—decoupling mode theory (DMT)—is proposed for microstrip transmission lines. The DMT is established using energy transport theorem (ETT) framework. The ETT-based DMT (ETT-DMT) can use diagonalizing input power operator (IPO) method to construct a set of energy-decoupled fundamental working modes [simply called energy-decoupled modes (DMs)] for an objective microstrip transmission line. The DMs can effectively reveal the inherent energy transmission character of the objective microstrip transmission line, and any two different DMs do not have net energy exchange in an integral period. Besides microstrip transmission lines, the ETT-DMT is also applicable to microstrip power dividers. By some proper generalizations, the ETT-DMT can also be applied to SMA-microstrip-SMA transmission-line and power-divider systems.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Modal Analysis for the Wireless Channel between a Pair of Transmitter and Receiver
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The transport process of the energy flowing in the wireless channel between a pair of transmitter and receiver is studied. The energy transport process is quantitatively governed by so-called energy transport theorem (ETT). In the ETT, there exists a source term—input power operator (IPO)—used to sustain the steady energy transport process. By diagonalizing the IPO, a set of fundamental modes propagating in the wireless channel are obtained, and the fundamental modes are energy-decoupled, so the fundamental modes are simply called energy-decoupled modes (DMs). This ETT-based diagonalizing IPO scheme provides an effective modal analysis method to the transmitter-channel-receiver structure. To avoid the risk that the core physical principle is covered by some complicated mathematical formulations, this paper restricts the transmitter to a relatively simple aperture-fed microstrip patch antenna, and restricts the receiver to a relatively simple aperture-loaded dielectric resonator antenna. In fact, the modal analysis method proposed in this paper can be easily extended to some more complicated transmitter-channel-receiver structures, such as metasurface-channel-metasurface structure.

articleTitle: A comparative study of two different optimization methods applied to the static job scheduling problem in grid computing
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In the telecommunications sector where real-time data processing and low latency are essential, grid computing promotes faster response times and reduced network congestion. Grid Computing has since become a very powerful and indispensable tool for telecommunications operators because it allows companies to optimize their operations, improve the performance of their network and provide better services to their customers. One of the distributed computing systems used in telecommunications is the User-PC (UPC) system. The User-PC Computing (UPC) system provides a cost-effective distributed computing platform by utilizing the unused resources of personal computers (PCs). Effective job allocation methods are essential for optimizing system performance. In this study, we introduce a comparative analysis of the static job scheduling problem in the UPC system, focusing on the performance comparison between our proposed hybrid approach, which combines a greedy algorithm and a algorithm genetics, and the approach based on Randomized Multi-Start Local Search. Our hybrid algorithm is composed of two steps. In the first step, a Greedy Algorithm is used to create an initial population of candidate solutions by assigning jobs to available workers based on CPU core utilization. In the second step, a Genetic Algorithm is used to optimize job-worker assignments through selection, crossover and mutation operations. To evaluate the performance of our approach, extensive experiments were conducted with up to 27 jobs and 6 worker PCs. The results show that our hybrid approach achieved a shorter makespan compared to the approach based on Randomized Multi-Start Local Search. Specifically, our algorithm outperformed the multi-start random local search-based method by more than 31% in terms of makespan reduction. The experimental results highlight the effectiveness of our hybrid approach to improve job scheduling performance in the UPC system.

articleTitle: Knowledge Distillation Based Lightweight Deep Neural Network for Automatic Modulation Classification
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Deep learning is widely used in the field of automatic modulation classification. Although the present state-of-art deep learning models for Automatic Modulation Classification (AMC) have high accuracy, their computational complexities are large, which is not friendly for practical considerations. To address this issue, a novel lightweight student network named GSCNET is proposed, based on the Ghost module and depthwise separable convolution. Furthermore, three different loss functions—cross-entropy loss, Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence loss, and soft label-based cross-entropy loss are used to supervise the training of GSCNET. Specifically, the cross-entropy loss is used to minimize the distance between predictions and true label. Regarding the last two losses, they are employed to minimize the discrepancy between predictions made by a student model and those from a teacher model (where the teacher model has better classification performance than GSCNET), which are derived from the methodology of knowledge distillation. As a result, the proposed algorithm can benefit from the knowledge of a teacher model, which is more discriminative than relying solely on the cross-entropy loss. Finally, the proposed GSCNET exhibits high classification performance with low computational complexity.

articleTitle: Enhanced Automatic modulation classification Using Leveraging Semi-Supervised Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Automatic modulation classification (AMC) is essential for identifying the modulation scheme of received signals, a key step bridging signal reception and demodulation. This process traditionally relies on prior signal information. Deep learning’s role in AMC has been notable, though its efficacy hinges on the volume of labeled data. Addressing the scarcity of labeled samples, our research introduces a semi-supervised AMC approach using consistency regularization and pseudo-labeling. This method harnesses unlabeled data’s distributional information to mitigate the shortfall of labeled data. We designed a dual-component objective function: one segment calculates loss from labeled data training, while the other assesses regularized loss from augmented unlabeled data. These combined losses concurrently refine the model parameters. Comparative tests reveal our method’s superiority over established algorithms like decision trees, support vector machines, pi-models, and virtual adversarial training, demonstrating enhanced performance in AMC.

articleTitle: PRIS: Online Routing and Scheduling Making CQF Flexible in Dynamic Time-Sensitive Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The growing number of IoT devices has brought about a large number of time-sensitive applications, and time-sensitive networks (TSN) are widely regarded as promoting paradigm for enabling the deterministic transmission. However, most of the existing research is based on the static network where the flow information is known a priori, and the transmission scheduling scheme is synthesized offline. This makes their design mechanism unsuitable for industrial automation scenarios with equipment changes and flow changes. Meanwhile, joint routing and scheduling faces the problem of large search space and high algorithm complexity, which poses a challenge to how to solve the problem within the acceptable time range of dynamic scenarios.We present PRIS, an algorithm that combines pre-routing and online incremental scheduling. Considering the periodicity of time-sensitive flow, the pre-routing algorithm uses weight factors including scheduling compatibility and load balancing as routing indicators. The online incremental scheduling based on Cyclic-Queuing and Forwarding(CQF), which was proposed by IEEE 802.1 to achieve bounded delay transmission. Based on CQF, our PRIS is designed to be flexible and with high schedulability, low execution time. Simulation results show PRIS has a high scheduling success rate of 92.7% at 150 new flows in feasible sub-second execution time.

articleTitle: Research on Computation Offloading Method of Digital Twin Assisted Internet of Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The rapid development of information has brought about the explosive growth of the amount of data computation, and the intelligent vehicle terminal is inevitably affected, and its local computing resources are difficult to cope with the complex computing needs. In the face of such a dilemma, computation unloading is undoubtedly an effective means to alleviate the shortage of vehicle computing resources. However, most computing tasks in vehicle networking scenarios have the characteristics of high delay sensitivity, so the delay requirements will be relatively higher. How to shorten the delay under the highly dynamic vehicle is an urgent problem to be solved. In this paper, digital twin technology is used to obtain network dynamics and business requirements, build a vehicle-connected architecture based on digital twin, measure task design priorities, model the computational offloading problem in dynamic environment as a Markov decision process, generate real-time resource allocation strategies, thereby reducing latency and maximizing task utility. In the unloading part, an unloading algorithm based on dual deep Q network is proposed to minimize the task processing delay.

articleTitle: Adaptive Sending Rate Regulation for RTC Video Telephony over Low-earth-orbit Satellite Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Low-earth-orbit (LEO) satellite networks have recently gained significant development due to large bandwidth, low latency, and wide coverage. Meanwhile, the satellite networks have sparked new vertical applications such as real time communication (RTC) video telephony. However, our investigation reveals that RTC services suffer from poor quality of experience (QoE) over satellite networks with a stalling rate of 30.5%. Surprisingly, the underlying cause lies in the lack of adaptability of RTC protocols to the satellite networks. Specifically, the RTC mechanism fails to differentiate between satellite link handoff events and actual network transmission congestion, leading it to employ an overly aggressive congestion avoidance strategy that reduces sending rates indiscriminately. In this paper, we propose an adaptive RTC sending rate regulation mechanism for satellite networks, called satAdaptor. This mechanism accurately identifies the factors of QoE decline. For the link handover, it predicts a reasonable sending rate using GRU methods; whereas for network congestion situations, it adopts a lower sending rate to present overload on satellite networks. Through simulation evaluations, we demonstrate significant QoE improvements for RTC video telephony. For instance, the sending rate can recovery within 2 seconds, which benefits from the handover prediction accuracy up to 92.46%.

articleTitle: Joint Energy Efficient Beamforming and Antenna Selection in Extremely Large-Scale MIMO Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The paper investigates a downlink extremely large-scale multiple-input multiple-output (XL-MIMO) system, where a base station (BS) equipped with a massive number of antennas serves multiple users located in different visibility regions of the BS. A main challenge of such system is the rapid increase of power consumption due to the large number of antennas, which does not align with the green communication requirements. To address this issue, the paper proposes a joint transmit beamforming and antenna selection design to maximize the energy efficiency of the system, subject to the maximum transmit power constraint at the BS, signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) constraints at the users, and binary constraints for antenna selection. The optimization problem is a fractional mixed-integer programming, which is high non-convexity and hard to handle. We propose an efficient algorithm based alternative optimization. In particular, by utilizing our proposed algorithm, the antenna with low transmit contribution are tend to closed to save energy. Finally, the numerical results is provided to validate the benefits of the proposed algorithm in addressing the energy efficiency challenges in downlink XL-MIMO systems with non-stationarity channel.

articleTitle: Joint AP clustering and beamforming in IRS-aided User-Centric Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: User-centric network is regarded as a promising technology for future mobile networks to achieve high quality-of-service (QoS) requirements. However, with the massive deployment of access points (APs), power consumption and interference management have become challenging tasks. To address the problem, we explore an intelligent reflecting surface (IRS) aided downlink user-centric network, utilizing IRSs to reduce power consumption and improve system performance. Considering user mobility and the effect of IRSs on the channel, we formulate a time-varying sum rate maximization problem and propose an effective alternating optimization algorithm that jointly optimizes the passive beamforming at IRSs, active beamforming at APs, and AP clustering. As for the proposed algorithm, AP clustering is solved using the discrete particle swarm optimization and beamforming is optimized based on the fractional programming method. Our simulation results show that the proposed algorithm can achieve significant sum rate improvement compared with baseline algorithms.

articleTitle: Automatic detection and classification algorithm of thyroid nodules in CT images based on YOLOv5s
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Thyroid nodular lesions are one of the most common diseases in the population. As the number of patients increases, it is clinically important to provide physicians with an accurate early aid to determine the benignity and malignancy of thyroid nodules in order to avoid unnecessary surgery and reduce patient burden. In this paper, we propose an improved Yolov5s-based target detection algorithm for benign and malignant thyroid nodules for thyroid nodule classification and identification. Replacing the backbone network of Yolov5s with ResNet18 to reduce the complexity of the model and the number of parameters; introducing the CBAM attention mechanism into the Yolov5s algorithm to improve the ability to extract features; Modify the spatial pyramid pooling module SPP to SimSPPF to improve the training speed of the algorithm; replace GIoU Loss with CIoU-Focal Loss as the loss function of the algorithm to improve the localization accuracy while increasing the regression rate of the bounding box. The experimental results show that the improved Yolov5s achieved an average accuracy of 92.9%, which is 2.9 percentage points higher than the average accuracy of the original algorithm, and can effectively improve the accuracy and efficiency of nodule detection.

articleTitle: Jammer-assisted Joint Power Allocation and Beamforming for Covert Wireless Transmission in ISAC Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The integration of radar sensing and communication is a promising technology and provides enhancement of spectrum resource utilization. Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) systems are emerging to improve communication quality and sensing efficiency. To ensure information security for ISAC systems, a jammer assisted covert wireless transmission technology is introduced into the ISAC system and joint power allocation and beamforming scheme is proposed. The sensing and communication performances are analyzed and the detection probability of Willie is calculated. The problem of maximizing covert rate by optimizing the beamformer vectors and power allocation is established and solved through semi-definite relaxation (SDR). Our work reveals the tradeoff between sensing performance and communication performance, and the influence of jamming power budget to wireless transmission rate. The numerical results highlight the benefits of jammer assisted covert wireless transmission in ISAC systems.

articleTitle: PPO Based Computation Offloading and Resource Allocation Algorithm in Smart Grids
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In smart grids, data communication and computation are required between electric vehicles (EVs) and charging stations (CSs) to realize charging management. In this paper, we investigate the joint optimization of computation offloading and resource allocation in edge computing (EC)-based smart grids to address the massive energy consumption caused by charging management. Firstly, a collaborative task offloading, computation resource allocation, and spectrum and power allocation problem is formulated to minimize the energy consumption in the EC-based system, by considering time-varying conditions as well as a delay constraint. Then, this NP-hard long-term optimization problem is defined as a Markov decision process, and a proximal policy optimization (PPO)-based algorithm is proposed to avoid the curse of dimensionality. Simulation results show that the PPO-based algorithm can effectively reduce the average energy consumption by 20.3% and 25.6% compared with two benchmark algorithms. Moreover, as the number of CSs increases, the advantage of the PPO-based algorithm is more obvious.

articleTitle: A Malicious Domain Detection Method of Cryptomining Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: With the skyrocketing prices and soaring trading volumes of Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies, the harms caused by malicious cryptomining activities are also increasing. Hackers are increasingly utilizing malicious software to conduct network attacks for cryptocurrency mining, posing threats not only to user privacy but also leading to the consumption of computing resources and increased electricity costs. Despite these challenges, existing detection methods, such as using blacklists to protect users’ browser antivirus programs, only offer partial solutions to this problem, as attackers can easily bypass their detection by frequently changing their domain names using domain generation algorithms. To address these issues, this paper employs deep learning technology and designs a method for detecting malicious cryptomining domains. This method combines blacklist detection with Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and is capable of identifying malicious domains from a large number of domain samples. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method produces excellent classification and detection outcomes.

articleTitle: Simulation Research of Intelligent Operation and Maintenance Information System of Rail Transit Based on Digital Twin
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: This paper describes an implementation method of intelligent operation and maintenance system of rail transit based on Digital Twin (DT), which is used to simultaneously display, analyze and judge the data status of monitoring equipment of rail transit station in different life cycles. First of all, this paper introduces the method of constructing the basic model and behavior model of metro station DT based on big data technology. Secondly, the multistate analysis method is used to study the status of DT of subway station monitoring equipment in different life cycles. Finally, different functional requirements of station operation and maintenance in training, exercise and operation scenarios are realized through the combination of multiple state modes. This study provides a new direction for DT landing.

articleTitle: A Novel Time Slot Structure for the High-speed Digital Maritime Communication Network
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: As a result of the rapid development of maritime economic activities, the scale of maritime network nodes is increasing and the amount of transmitted data is also skyrocketing, that put forward higher requirements on maritime communication performance. The traditional narrowband communication technologies including AIS, ASM and VDES, face the challenges of limited bandwidth and tight time slot load, in the scenarios of the large-scale network node access and high-speed communication. To overcome the above problems, a novel time slot structure for the high-speed digital maritime communication network was proposed in this paper. The proposed time slot structure is not only compatible with the existing AIS, ASM and VDES systems, but also suitable for communication scenarios requiring more network node access and higher transmission rate. The simulation results indicate that, under the conditions of 4500 slots per minute and 64QAM modulation method, the new time slot structure compared to the terrestrial VDES system, increases the scale of network nodes by nearly twice and the communication rate by more than four times.

articleTitle: Optimization of Image Transmission in UAV-Enabled Semantic Communication Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) are widely used in emergency communication systems. However, the lack of adequate communication power and bandwidth in UAV-enabled communication networks hinders transmitting large files like images and videos. The semantic communication is introduced to tackle this challenge by transmitting the semantic features instead of raw data. In this paper, we propose a UAV semantic communication architecture by jointly optimizing the UAV flight trajectories, semantic information selection, and resource allocation. Accordingly, an optimization problem is formulated to maximize the total similarity score of semantic information, and then, a soft actor-critic based entropy-maximization (SAC-EM) algorithm is proposed. Simulations demonstrate that the proposed algorithm increases the total semantic similarity score by 54.2% and improves convergence speed by 80% compared to traditional reinforcement learning algorithms.

articleTitle: Lattice-Based DAA Cross-Domain Authentication Protocol for Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The rapid development of quantum computing challenges the security of classical cryptographic regimes, and Direct Anonymous Attestation (DAA), a protocol built on RSA or ECC, widely used in the Internet of Things, cannot achieve post-quantum security. This has given rise to a variety of lattice-based direct anonymous protocols (LDAA). This paper proposes a cross-domain lattice-based DAA to address the need for cross-domain authentication in the IoT. The CD-LDAA protocol is based on the traditional DAA cross-domain protocol and introduces trusted third-party institutions and designs lattice-based TA-Join, Issuer<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">B</inf>-Join, and CD-Sign/Verify protocols. Secondly, the security of CD-LDAA is demonstrated based on a generic composable security framework with improved CD-LDAA ideal functions. Finally, the execution time of the CD-LDAA protocol and the size of the generated visa certificate and cross-domain certificate are tested through simulation experiments. The results show that the scheme proposed in this paper is higher than the traditional ECC or RSA-based DAA cross-domain protocols in terms of computation and storage consumption, but the post-quantum security strength is higher.

articleTitle: Entity Alignment Study Based on Hybrid Similarity Calculation
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The task of entity alignment is to determine whether two or more entities are pointing to the same object in the real world.
