This study can provide certain theoretical and practical references for the improvement of information technology in universities.

articleTitle: EKR: An Efficient K-anycast Routing in UAV Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: K-anycast refers to a communication model where a message is transmitted from a source to k destinations. Compared to multicast and unicast, k-anycast offers significant advantages in terms of load balancing, redundancy, and improved reliability. As far as we know, there is currently no research on k-anycast for UAV networks. We propose an Efficient K-anycast Routing scheme called EKR. The high dynamism of UAV networks poses a challenge in formalizing and addressing the k-anycast problem. Therefore, this paper utilizes predetermined trajectory information to construct Encounter Record Tree (ER-Tree), which converts dynamically changing network topologies into a static graph. Based on ER-Tree, we formalize the k-anycast problem in UAV networks and transform it into a Group Steiner Tree problem, which is known to be NP-hard. Then an efficient search algorithm is proposed to solve it and find the transmission path. To evaluate the performance of EKR, we performed simulations with the One simulator. The results demonstrate that EKR outperforms existing protocols in terms of delivery rate, end-to-end delay, and network overhead.

articleTitle: Throughput Improvement for Buffer-Aided UAV Relaying Communications With Jamming
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Due to the high mobility of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and the broadcast nature of wireless communication channels, UAV systems are more vulnerable to malicious jamming attacks. This paper investigates a UAV assisted relaying communication system where a buffer-aided UAV acts as an aerial mobile relay to aid the information transmission between ground terminal nodes in the presence of malicious jamming. For the maximum end-to-end throughput, this paper formulates the optimization problem of joint communication scheduling, transmit power allocation and UAV trajectory planning under the buffer constraints. However, the non-convexity of the optimization problem will lead it to be intractable to obtain an optimal solution at an acceptable complexity, hence an efficient iterative algorithm is proposed to achieve an approximate suboptimal solution of the original problem. Numerical results not only demonstrate the convergence of the proposed iterative algorithm, but also indicate that the proposed joint design can considerably enhance the system throughput.

articleTitle: CeDA-BatOp 2.0: Enhanced Framework for Base Station Parameter Optimization and Automation with Joint Optimization, Controlled Drift Analysis and Pseudo-Labeling
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In the ever-evolving landscape of cellular networks, the pursuit of optimal network performance remains a constant endeavor. This paper introduces CeDA-BatOp 2.0, an enhanced framework designed to address the complexities of network optimization. Building upon the foundations of its predecessor CeDA-BatOp version 1.0, this upgraded version presents a Multi-task learning (MTL) approach that leverages joint training of a base station parameter predictor and clustering. By intertwining these tasks, CeDA-BatOp 2.0 demonstrates its ability to provide a holistic and efficient solution for network optimization. Furthermore, this framework introduces an innovative analysis of controlled data drift using Gaussian Mixture Models. The controlled drift analysis allows the framework to adapt to real-world data variations effectively, enhancing network performance and reliability. It also incorporates a pseudo-labeling strategy using Multi-View Co-Training, streamlining the retraining process. This feature is crucial in scenarios where manual labeling is impractical, making the system adaptive and efficient in responding to changing network conditions. Through the simulated data, the paper demonstrates the framework’s efficacy, achieving significant improvements in network optimization. CeDA-BatOp 2.0 is a step forward in addressing the complexities of cellular network optimization. By combining MTL, drift analysis, and pseudo-labeling, it provides a comprehensive solution that adapts to the dynamic nature of cellular networks, ultimately enhancing network performance and the user experience.

articleTitle: A multipath-assisted localization algorithm under 5G-based opensource testbed
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Indoor localization services are playing an important role in a variety of emerging industries. Traditional positioning methods suffer from insufficient accuracy or high deployment costs in indoor environments, and with the rapid development of cellular mobile communication systems, positioning under cellular networks has been more widely used due to its low cost and easy deployment. In the indoor environment, the number of available base stations is limited, and positioning by direct radius information provided by only one base station suffers from insufficient accuracy. In this paper, we designed a method for indoor localization based on cellular networks, which considering the localization information carried by the multi-path, to verify the performance of this algorithm in practical scene. We implement this algorithm in a 5G-based testbed based on software-defined radio (SDR) technologies. The results show that our algorithm can meet the requirements of indoor cases defined in 3GPP 38.855.

articleTitle: Timing and carrier Synchronization for DVB-RCS2
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The second generation digital television broadcasting interactive satellite system (DVB-RCS2) is widely used in Internet access and other services. In actual scenarios, DVB-RCS2 must address the synchronization issue at the receiver. In this paper, we analyze the performance of timing synchronization under four-times oversampling and sixteen-times oversampling. According to the three frame structures designed by DVB-RCS2, we give a carrier synchronization scheme based on FFT. The scheme we proposed operates effectively in both data-aided (DA) and none-data-aided (NDA) manner. In addition, considering the complexity and performance, we propose a fine frequency offset estimation scheme based on phase difference under low FFT points. Simulation results show that the proposed synchronization algorithm suits all frame structures in the standard. The synchronization algorithm works well at low signal to noise radio (SNR).

articleTitle: Stereo Image Dense Matching Based on SGM Constrained by Feature Matching
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Dense image matching plays a important role in stereo vision and remote sensing. Semi-global matching (SGM) is a widely used dense image matching framwork, which uses dynamic programming calculation strategy to optimize the global energy function. SGM has the problem of wrong disparity accumulation along the path. To solve the problem, this paper proposes a new dense image matching method based on feature matching and SGM. First, the feature matching is used to extract the reliable reference points. And then, reference points are used as additional constraints in matching cost aggregation to cut off the wrong disparity delivering along the path. In order to evaluate our method, qualitative and quantitative experiments are carried out on three stereo image pairs. The experimental results show that our method can achieve high matching accuracy by effectively reducing the error propagation.

articleTitle: Prohibited Items Detection in X-ray Images Based on Task Decoupling YOLOv5
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: X-ray security inspection is a critical security measure in airports, train stations and other areas with dense populations. However, due to the intricate nature of X-ray imaging and the intense occlusion between objects, the result of general object detection algorithms is not satisfactory. By exploiting the efficient YOLOv5 algorithm, we propose an Attention Task Decoupling Head (ATDH)to decouple the features used for classification and regression tasks. ATDH consists of a channel attention adjustment module (CAAM) and a spatial attention adjustment module (SAAM). These two lightweight modules make task-specific adjustments to the input features of YOLOv5’s shared prediction heads from channel dimensions and spatial dimensions, respectively. The unreasonable situation of using the same feature to predict classification tasks and regression tasks with different information preferences is avoided. In addition, we also have implemented SimOTA dynamic sample assignment approach to flexibly adapt to the requirements of different training stages and different object instances for dividing positive and negative samples. Experiments on datasets including OPIXray, SIXray, CLCXray, and HIXray show that our approach has a significant performance improvement over the YOLOv5 benchmark.

articleTitle: CNN-Transformer Architecture Solution for Compound Facial Expression Recognition
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: True emotions can be indicated by the human facial expression of emotions. Facial expression recognition has vast applications in healthcare, security, artificial intelligence, e-learning, sports, agriculture and various other fields. Although significant research has been conducted on basic emotions, there is currently a surge of interest in recognizing compound facial expressions of emotions in the field of image processing. In this paper, we present a method that employs the vision transformer (ViT) and utilizes the DenseNet-121 as a backbone for recognizing compound facial expressions of emotions on the CFEE and RAFDB datasets. The proposed method has outperformed and improved the recognition accuracy of compound emotions compared to the state-of-the-art (SOTA) models. The obtained results demonstrate the accuracy rates of 66.4% for the CFEE dataset and 72.05% for the RAFDB dataset. The recognition accuracy was enhanced by around 9.05% on the CFEE dataset and approximately 3.62% on the RAFDB dataset in comparison to the current state of the art (SOTA), thanks to the proposed methodology. This approach tackles the current task and paves the way for future investigations in detecting complex emotions using ViT models.

articleTitle: Research on Time Synchronization Algorithm Based on Co-band Signal
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In recent years, the Internet of Things (IoT) has imposed increasingly stringent requirements on time synchronization technology. While striving for continuous improvement in time synchronization accuracy, there is a simultaneous needed to minimize communication costs, leading to the emergence of various time synchronization protocols. TC-OFDM Co-band signal system has been used in IoT for years. In this paper, we propose a two-way mechanism and an Accumulation Timing Measure (ATM) algorithm based on the TC-OFDM Co-band signal system to reduce clock drift and costs of communication. The ATM aggregates N round-trip time (RTT) measurement results to derive a concise set of Accumulated Time measurement parameters, specifically estimating logical clock drift and logical clock offset, which facilitate complete information exchange for clock difference settlement. Through extensive simulations, we have observed that the ATM algorithm achieves nanosecond-level accuracy. Furthermore, we have found that the accuracy of ATM remains within 0.05 of the TPSN while substantially reducing communication costs with an increase in the number of communication cycles.

articleTitle: Design of Substrate Integrated waveguide 8×8 Slot Array antenna at Ku band
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In order to solve the problems of low radiation power of microstrip antenna and difficult integration of metal waveguide, substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) structure with the advantages of both microstrip and waveguide has attracted wide attention. Based on HFSS, an 8-element constant amplitude in-phase standing wave linear array operating at Ku-band with the center frequency of 18GHz is designed by using the side-feed mode. Then the 8×8 slot array antenna is designed by the wide side longitudinal slit of the SIW. The simulation results show that the gain of the array is 20.9dBi, the return loss is very small, the VSWR is less than 2 in 17.09~18.19GHz and 19.66~22 GHZ bands, and the relative bandwidth is about 59%.-10dB bandwidth is 17.18GHz-18.14GHz(16.6%). The resonant frequency of the input reflection coefficient is 18GHz, which is less than -20dB, and the antenna efficiency is high. The simulation results are good, which verifies the feasibility of the design. The designed antenna has high gain, strong directionality, easy integration and good impedance matching, which has a broad application prospect in microwave and millimeter wave systems.

articleTitle: Edge Detection in Dark Industrial Environments
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: To solve the problem that current edge detectors cannot accurately detect the edges of artifacts under low-light conditions, we propose an edge detection network-EDD that adapts to scale changes and low-light environments. First, we utilize a feature pyramid to divide the features of the input image into 4 stages of different resolutions. Second, we introduce a scale enhancement module to obtain feature information at different scales. In addition, in order to solve the challenge of inconspicuous edge details in low-light environments, we design a high frequency enhancement module. We conduct experimental verification on the BSDS500 dataset and our own artifact dataset MPBD, and the results show that EDD has a significant edge detection effect in low-light environments. Compared with other methods, EDD can capture the edge of the workpiece more accurately, and provides an effective solution to the edge detection problem in dark conditions.

articleTitle: Analysis and Intelligent Integration of Mapping Elements for Remote Sensing Monitoring of the Contaminated Sites
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Using global spatial autocorrelation index and local spatial autocorrelation index, based on the vector data of contaminated sites in Zhejiang province, the overall spatial distribution and local clustering distribution of contaminated sites in the research area were analyzed in this paper. According to the vector data of contaminated sites and remote sensing data, the intelligent mapping feature integration method was constructed, such as designing map template, positioning map data frame and associated mapping auxiliary elements of contaminated sites in the research area. The results showed that: (1) the possibility of spatial clustering of contaminated sites in the research area is greater than 90%, with 34 statistically significant hotspots, 4 statistically significant high-high clustering areas, and 1 statistically significant high-low clustering area. (2) the intelligent mapping integration can complete the work of 3 days’ manual mapping within 8 minutes, which improved the mapping efficiency and accuracy significantly.

articleTitle: UAV-vision based Oilfield Anomaly Detection via Optimized LBAM-YOLO
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Anomaly detection remains a great challenge for Oilfields. Oil leaks and intruding of unknown vehicles often propose severe safety issue for oil-field. At present, the using of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) is crucial in promptly identifying and addressing these anomalies, ensuring the safe operation of oilfields. However, detecting ground-level oilfield anomalies from a high-altitude is challenging due to the complexity and diversity of oil leakage features. Therefore, this study proposes an improved attention mechanism based target detection model termed LBAM-YOLO. The enhanced algorithmic model mainly incorporates the CBAM (Convolutional Block Attention Module) attention mechanism augmented with label information. Ablation experiments were conducted to evaluate the performance of our proposal. It demonstrates that compared to prevalent models, our method achieves more satisfactory performance in terms of recall and F1 score while maintaining high precision. Our model also exhibits more comprehensive ability to detect oilfield anomalies.

articleTitle: SRv6 Strategy Based on Network State and Behavior Prediction in 5G Network
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: With extremely low delay and extremely high data transmission speed, 5G network has been widely used at present, and it is of great significance to realize innovation and development in many fields of society. 5G puts forward strict requirements for the bandwidth, delay, slicing and time synchronization accuracy of the bearer network. Aiming at the problem of local optimization of existing information center network (ICN) routing, this article introduces Segment Routing based on IPv6 data plane (SRv6) and proposes SRv6 strategy based on network state and behavior prediction. Through the source routing mechanism of SRv6, the routing table is sent to the source node at one time to avoid intermediate routing and make the network obtain better performance. The simulation results show that paper algorithm can reduce packet loss, delay and system overhead compared with the shortest path algorithm and random path algorithm when the number of requests in the network is increasing. SRv6 can simplify the network and carry out super-large-scale deployment, and will gradually become the network evolution direction in the era of 5G and cloud.

articleTitle: The Performance of Cooperative-NOMA in Cognitive Hybrid Satellite Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Integrating cognitive radio (CR) technology into satellite communication represents an effective approach to enhance the throughput of satellite systems. However, the use of orthogonal multiple access (OMA) in traditional satellite-based CR systems has posed limitations on satellite system development. This paper focuses on power-domain non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA for simplicity), which has the potential to increase the number of access users and improve user communication capacity within the cognitive network. The integration of NOMA into CR networks holds immense potential for improving spectral efficiency and accommodating a larger user base. Notably, NOMA leverages successive interference cancellation (SIC) to decode information from the far user (FU) by the near user (NU), enabling the NU to potentially relay data and assist the FU. To fully harness this characteristic, we propose the utilization of cooperative NOMA (C-NOMA) to enhance system performance while ensuring the quality of service (QoS) for the FU. In evaluating the performance of the proposed system, we conduct an analysis of the outage probability and bit error rate (BER). This analysis provides valuable insights into the effectiveness of integrating CR and C-NOMA to enhance the reliability and quality of satellite communication.

articleTitle: Node centrality algorithm based on Fluid Bernoulli Static Pressure
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Node importance measurement is of great significance for studying the robustness and vulnerability of power communication network. The structure of large-scale real power communication networks tends to change over time and has limitations in obtaining global network information for assessing the importance of nodes. A node importance assessment algorithm Similar Fluid Bernoulli Static Pressure (SBSP) is proposed by quantifying the current intensity generated by the external sources of the local network topology. Aiming at the neighborhood connection information in two hops of the central node and the characteristics of the neighboring nodes, the algorithm combines the generalized resistance distance and Fluid Bernoulli equation to characterize the structure importance of the central node in the network. Based on six classical IEEE power grid topologies, the network is gradually attacked in order of node importance. By comparing the experimental results of the maximum connectivity subgraph, network efficiency and node importance differentiation, it is proved that the proposed algorithm is superior to the four traditional algorithms and three abstract algorithms based on physical model proposed in recent years.

articleTitle: Channel Measurement and Characteristics Analysis for Metal Pipeline Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Metal pipelines are thought to provide efficient solutions for the conditions in which high-speed maglev trains operate. A key component of the maglev system’s foundation is wireless communication. Due to the confined space, metal walls and the use of leaky coaxial cables (LCXs), the wireless channel characteristics are quite unique within the pipelines. This paper presents the first channel measurement within the metal pipeline containing LCXs at 2.16 GHz. Based on the measurement results, we analyze the channel characteristics, including path loss, shadow fading, root mean square (RMS) delay spread and build a tapped delay line (TDL) model. The analysis reveals that the use of LCXs and metal materials creates additional strong power paths and a wider delay spread compared to other scenarios. For the subsequent deployment of communication systems for metal pipeline scenarios, the conclusions of this paper are an invaluable resource.

articleTitle: TD3PG-Based Network Revenue in SDSAGIN
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: A space-air-ground integrated network (SAGIN) is considered a highly promising solution to meet the demand for ubiquitous connectivity and quality of service (QoS). However, it is challenging to orchestrate heterogeneous resources in large-scale and dynamic networks to guarantee QoS and service provider revenues. Firstly, a SAGIN architecture based on network function virtualization (NFV) and software-defined networking (SDN) is proposed in this article. Virtual network function (VNF) embedding and wireless resource management are taken into account. And the revenue and cost for the network are jointly constructed as an objective function. Then, a twin delayed deep deterministic policy gradient (TD3PG) algorithm based on deep reinforcement learning (DRL) is developed to optimize the objective function to maximize the net network revenue. Finally, the simulation results demonstrate the convergence and superiority for the algorithm.

Author Keywords: twin delayed deep deterministic policy gradient

articleTitle: Formal Proof of Contract Theorem in First-Order Logic in Coq
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: This paper uses the theorem proving tool Coq to complete the formal description and proof of the contract theorem in the field of first-order logic. The contract theorem elaborates the link between variable assignments and the outcomes of term assignments, or the computed result of a formula’s satisfaction relationship. We also provide comprehensive explanations of fundamental concepts in first-order logic, encompassing variables, formulas, and satisfiable relations. The successful verification of the Contract Theorem serves as a vital step towards substantiating the validity of first-order logic formulas and culminating in the creation of a comprehensive logical framework. Through this proof, we emphasize Coq’s remarkable capabilities in automated induction, as well as its interactive and intelligent nature in facilitating machine-based mathematical theorem proofs.

articleTitle: Optimizing Pre-trained Language Models for Efficient Vulnerability Detection in Code Snippets
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The early detection of vulnerable software code snippets is crucial for enhancing security and mitigating potential exploit risks. In machine learning (ML) and natural language processing (NLP), large-scale pre-trained language models (PLMs) offer considerable potential for tackling this challenge. However, fine-tuning these models can frequently result in overfitting, particularly when working with smaller or dissimilar datasets. This study introduces an innovative strategy to optimize pre-trained language models from Hugging Face—a platform acclaimed for its broad user base and research support—for efficient vulnerability identification in code snippets. We fine-tune high-performing models such as BERT, RoBERTa, and DistilBERT, selected for their superior natural language processing capabilities and aptitude for syntactic and semantic analyses essential for code scrutiny. Utilizing the CodeXGLUE Defect-detection dataset, featuring labeled C programming language code snippets, we aim to mitigate overfitting issues while enhancing vulnerability detection accuracy and efficiency. Our research focuses on classifying code snippets into vulnerable and non-vulnerable categories, equipping developers with valuable insights to address security risks proactively. A rigorous evaluation reveals that our machine learning methodology outperforms existing approaches regarding precision, recall, and overall effectiveness. Our research underscores the potential of utilizing pre-trained language models for advanced software security enhancement and novel language analysis tasks.

articleTitle: Research on Optimization Strategy of Distributed Data Center and Energy Integration System
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: As a key infrastructure supporting the development of the digital economy, data centers have attracted attention due to their increasing energy consumption and operational costs. This article proposes a distributed data center and energy integration system that includes a data subsystem, an energy subsystem, and a data-energy integrated management and scheduling platform. It constructs an integrated operational dispatching model and proposes an optimization strategy based on data flow-energy flow collaborative scheduling. Taking the comprehensive energy cost including electricity cost and carbon trading cost as the optimization objective, a particle swarm optimization algorithm is used to find the optimal solution. Experimental results demonstrate that the operational optimization strategy proposed in this article can effectively reduce the overall energy consumption and operational costs of the system while ensuring system reliability.

articleTitle: Multi-Dimensional Resource Allocation Strategy for LEO Multi-Satellite Beam Hopping Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Recently, the low earth orbit (LEO) satellite communication network has received much attention as an important part of the Space-Air-Ground Integrated Network (SAGIN). However, the resources on satellites are limited, which requires efficient resource allocation strategy to meet user demands. Moreover, the limited spectrum resources mean many satellites share the same frequency resources. Thus, effective interference avoidance measures will further improve the quality of satellite system services. To realize efficient resource management in the LEO multi-satellite beam hopping network, this paper proposes a multi-dimensional resource collaborative allocation strategy, which is implemented in three steps. Firstly, the beam hopping pattern is designed based on the principle of interference avoidance. Secondly, bandwidth resources are allocated by the matching theory. Finally, the non-convex problem is transformed into a convex optimization problem to realize power resource allocation. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed strategy can effectively avoid interference and minimize the total transmission delay.

articleTitle: An Improved Path Planning Algorithm for USV Based on Voxel Extension
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a corridor generation algorithm based on voxel extension to obtain a safe path for unmanned surface vehicle (USV). Firstly, a dual-drive model is applied to model the USV, and then we design a path planning framework for the front-end and back-end parts. The front-end structure is responsible for finding a series of asymptotically optimal path points and generating safe corridors connected by a series of convex polygons based on these path points. The back-end part takes the safety corridor as a partial constraint and applies numerical optimization methods to generate a smooth trajectory. Finally, we validate and compare the proposed method with the baseline in a simulation environment.

articleTitle: Trusted Assurance for Transactions on Big Data Clouds: An Improved Blockchain-Based Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: This paper aims to explore methods and techniques for achieving verifiability in cloud computing environments. Methodologically, by utilizing game theory as the theoretical foundation and employing blockchain and smart contracts as core technologies, we introduce various cooperative mechanisms, including prisoner's contracts, collusion contracts, and traitor contracts, to construct a trustworthy computational framework. In terms of improvements, we innovatively incorporate local blockchains, state channel technology, zero-knowledge proof technology, multi-signature technology, and dynamic reward and punishment mechanisms to additional optimize existing methods. However, the proposed technologies in this paper still require further research and practical validation to assess their actual applicability. Going forward, it is important to enhance blockchain storage and synchronization mechanisms, as well as promote their implementation in broader domains.

articleTitle: Outage Analysis for Leader-Follower Cooperative Flying Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Directional communication is a crucial technology for reliable and high-speed communication in unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) formation networks. Based on the idea of integrating communication and control, this paper investigates the leader-follower UAV formation network and proposes a outage probability analysis method for the leader-follower UAV formation network. One UAV in the network acts as the leader UAV and guides the entire network, while the follower UAVs exchange their position information to ensure the stability of the formation flight. In this paper, the outage probability of a follower UAV falling outside the coverage of the leader UAV's transmitting beam is analysed taking into account the effect of inter-UAV communication noise, an approximate expression is derived and the upper and lower bounds of the derived results are analysed. The simulation results show that the outage probability introduced in this paper is related to the distance between the leader UAV and the follower UAV, the noise variance and the beam angle of the leader UAV emission, and finally the upper and lower bound analysis is verified by simulation.

articleTitle: Security Assessment Algorithms for Transmission and Services in SDN-Based Mobile Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In response to the challenge of comprehensively security assessment and analysis in existing mobile networks from both upper-layer services and network transmission levels, A SDN-based security assessment model for transmission and service security in mobile networks (SAMTS) is proposed. This model introduces security assessment algorithms, in which static configuration information and dynamic abnormal information are considered comprehensively to judge the trend and the risk degree of attack when evaluating the security of network nodes. Meanwhile, the node importance of service orientation and transmission is integrated for security evaluation. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by simulation and comparison experiments, demonstrating its higher evaluation accuracy compared with similar algorithms.

articleTitle: Photovoltaic Prediction Algorithm Based on Hybrid Artificial Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: With the development of science and technology, the proportion of photovoltaic power generation has increased significantly. The nonlinearity and instability of photovoltaic power generation make it difficult to integrate into the power grid on a large scale. Accurate photovoltaic power generation pre-can make photovoltaic(PV) power generation stably integrated into the grid system. This paper proposes a new Random Forest-Convolutional Neural Network-Long Short Term Memory (RF-CNN-LSTM) hybrid model. This model combines the advantages of CNN model which can effectively extract features and LSTM model which can deal with time series problems well. It makes it possible to make a good prediction for photovoltaic power generation. At the same time, this paper uses mean square error(mse) and mean absolute error(mae) as the criterion of model performance. Experimental results show that the performance of the hybrid model is more accurate.

articleTitle: Research on Optimization Method of C4 Olefins Preparation by Ethanol Coupling Based on Machine Learning Model
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: As an important chemical raw material, C4 olefins are widely used in the manufacture of chemical products and pharmaceutical intermediates. In this paper, a machine learning model is established by quantifying the catalyst combination and temperature conditions in the process of preparing C4 olefins. Finally, the optimization scheme of ethanol coupling production of C4 olefins based on machine learning model was obtained. A relational function machine learning model based on CatBoostRegressor integrated regression was established to fit the relationship between different catalyst compositions and temperatures and the yield of C4 olefins. Then, all possible results were quantitatively searched and analyzed through the grid search algorithm, and the combinations of catalyst and temperatures that maximizes the yield of C4 olefins is obtained. This paper finally obtained the optimal plan for the preparation of C4 olefins.

articleTitle: A Noise Model Circuit Based On A High-Speed Pipeline ADC System
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Noise is a pivotal element in the design of analog circuits, and the analysis of noise plays a vital role in characterizing their performance. We develop a simulated noise model for an ADC system, encompassing the analog-to-digital converter, isolation amplifier, and power supply. Subsequently, we employ various analysis techniques to determine the cumulative noise within the signal chain. To aggregate the noise contributions from all devices, we analyze the model's noise characteristics in the voltage domain and evaluate them using established tools. Demonstrating the practical value and innovative aspects of noise analysis.

articleTitle: An Anti-interference Technique for Wireless Sensor Network in Transformer Substation with Complicated Electromagnetic Interference
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: To support the increasing power demand, a lot of ultra-high voltage transformer substations have been built, with wireless sensor network deployed to sense and collect the operation data. However, interference introduced by the substation environment is complicated. In this paper, an anti-interference technique for wireless sensor network in transformer substation with complicated electromagnetic interference is proposed. Three kinds of interference are considered. To deal with the complicated electromagnetic interference introduced by UHV transformation substations, a low-power SF allocation strategy is designed. To cope with the transmission interference, including the inter-AP co-channel interference and other co-channel interference, a shifting SF Allocation strategy is proposed. Simulation results show that the proposed scheme reduces the interference level in the substation, which is beneficial to improve the communication reliability of the WSNs in transformer substation.

articleTitle: Research on Sentiment Analysis and Personalized Recommendation Based on Agricultural Product Reviews
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: This paper takes the online review of Shenyou Songhua Egg in the shopping platform Jingdong as an example, introduces text sentiment analysis into e-commerce online commentary, and more accurately judges the emotional tendency of online reviews of agricultural products e-commerce based on the BERT model. Word frequency analysis and word cloud drawing of accurately classified online reviews of agricultural products can summarize the crucial criteria for the product sales and capture the key points in agricultural products e-commerce online reviews in more detail. Empirical analysis shows that by introducing text sentiment analysis into the field of online reviews of agricultural products e-commerce and using the BERT emotion model for emotional judgment, it can more accurately judge users' emotional tendencies, and take corresponding measures according to the key points of comments extracted by word frequency analysis, so as to improve users' favorability and loyalty to the platform and increase user stickiness.

articleTitle: An Intelligent Genetic Algorithm-based Neural Network Method for Intrusion Detection Systems in the Network
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Recently, both academics and the military have been actively researching intrusion detection systems (IDS). However, it is difficult to extract important features and categorize the various types of traffic due to the unpredictable character of network traffic. To address this issue, this paper proposed a technique based on feature selection using a genetic algorithm (GA) when combined with classification using a neural network (NN), where the NN's classification accuracy serves as the GA's fitness metric. Two intrusion detection datasets were used to assess the performance of the proposed approach, and performance analysis is presented in terms of various assessment metrics. According to our experimental results, the model has the advantage of global adaptivity for any detection task, without the need for professionals to adjust the neural network's parameters, and was extremely applicable with a high accuracy of 99.99% in KDDCup99 and 91.89% in UNSW-NB15.

articleTitle: CDN Load Balancing Algorithm Based on Playback Volume and Server Remaining Resources
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: When employing CDN for acceleration of streaming media, it is crucial to consider server performance limitations, as failure to do so might negatively impact acceleration results. Traditional CDN load balancing only takes into account network loads, providing limited flexibility in adjusting file servers, and consequently poor adaptability. To address this issue, this article proposes a load balancing algorithm based on Playback Volume and Server Remaining Resources, which can effectively construct a streaming media distribution network and improve CDN performance and efficiency. Specifically, this algorithm calculates the playback volume of each terminal video, dynamically selects CDN acceleration servers, optimizing the CDN network in real time. By employing this method, CDN server load can be effectively alleviated, resulting in improved file hit rates. Experimental results indicate that this algorithm can better adapt to different network environments and server resource conditions, significantly improving video transmission quality, and better meeting user needs and expectations.

articleTitle: Two Classes of Accelerated Manifold Proximal Gradient Method for Sparse PCA
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Principal component analysis (PCA) is a popular technique for machine learning and signal processing. Sparse PCA is a special and difficult case of PCA and sparsity can enhance the interpretability of pricipal component. We focus on such the sparse PCA problem, which is a typical nonsmooth and nonconvex optimization problem. To the best of our knowledge, the existing methods lack of sufficient rationality in the design of algorithm or have the disvantage on speed and iteration. In this paper, we proposed two classes of accelerated manifold proximal gradient method. Numerical experiments display the superiority of our algorithms compared to the latest methods.

articleTitle: A study on the virtual reality modeling effect and computer algorithm application of architectural space
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Research on the effects of virtual reality modeling in architectural spaces and the application of computer algorithms is a complex and flexible field that integrates virtual reality technology, three-dimensional modeling, computer graphics and algorithms. This study will conduct computer drawing and realistic simulation technology after practical measurements of real monuments, so as to help redesign the monuments using computer simulation during restoration. This research can achieve high-precision architectural space models and virtual reality living experiences. These technologies can be used to create accurate 3D models of architectural spaces, including indoor and outdoor spaces. At the same time, high-quality rendering algorithms can be used to achieve virtual light and shadow effects, making the virtual space closer to reality. Researchers can develop virtual reality interaction technology that enables users to freely navigate and operate in virtual spaces. This algorithm can complete the optimal design of building space, including structural layout, lighting design and air conditioning system optimization. In the future, users will be able to conduct real-time playgrounds and displays through the virtual environment, which will help ensure that the building design meets various technical requirements and environmental standards. The development of these research directions can not only improve the efficiency and accuracy of architectural design in real wisdom and actual design, but also provide a better virtual experience to help construction professionals and users better understand and appreciate architectural spaces.

articleTitle: Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Assisted Task Unloading and Resource Allocation Algorithm Based on NOMA System
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In order to improve the flexibility of transmission, for the mobile edge computing (MEC) system assisted by multiple UAVs, an energy-saving UAV MEC framework combined with non orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) is proposed, in which multiple UAVs are deployed as edge servers to provide computing assistance for ground users, and NOMA is used to reduce the energy consumption of task unloading. Considering the User grouping、 joint optimization of computing resources and drone trajectory planning under given computing tasks and time, the weighted system energy consumption is minimized. Due to the coupling of parameters, minimizing energy consumption is a highly non-convex problem. Therefore, the problem is decomposed into three more manageable sub problems, namely user grouping, optimal allocation of computing resources for a given drone trajectory, and trajectory planning based on a given resource allocation scheme. Use matching game algorithm to solve grouping problems separately, and then convert these two problems into convex problems through CVX and quadratic approximation. Then, an effective iterative algorithm is proposed to alternately solve these two sub problems, gradually approaching the optimal resource management of the proposed system.

articleTitle: A Binary Cryptographic Algorithm Identification Method Based on Complementary Features
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Abstract—The effective identification of binary cryptographic algorithms provides crucial technical support for encryption cracking and security mechanism analysis. However, the identification of binary cryptographic algorithms faces interferences from different instruction sets, optimizations, and obfuscations in reality. To address the challenge, two mutually compensating features (one is the high-level semantic feature of cryptographic algorithm and the other is the intuitive code execution pattern extracted from binary grayscale image) are adopted in this paper. By representing binary cryptographic algorithms from different perspectives, accurate identification of cryptographic algorithms is achieved through a two-stage classification process. The proposed method outperforms the current advanced binary cryptographic algorithm identification method, GENDA, in terms of identification performance across different compilation and obfuscation scenarios.

articleTitle: Adaptive Hello Interval Scheme for Mobile Ad Hoc Routing Protocols
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In mobile ad hoc networks (MANETs), nodes get information about neighboring nodes by broadcasting and receiving hello messages. Without hello messages, it is difficult for a node to maintain link connectivity with neighboring nodes. In traditional MANETs, nodes typically broadcast hello messages at fixed intervals, which leads to two problems. If the interval is too long, the nodes are unable to update the network topology in time, which may lead to link breakage. If the interval is too short, it will cause unnecessary network overhead. Therefore, in this paper, we propose an adaptive hello interval scheme (AH) for mobile ad hoc routing protocols. In this scheme, nodes adaptively adjust hello intervals based on the density and average relative speed of neighboring nodes, the communication distance as well as their own speeds. In addition, nodes consider both the distance of the nodes as well as hello intervals while selecting relay nodes. When the source node encounters routing voids, it considers the hello interval of neighboring nodes and the angle between nodes. Simulation results show that compared with the greedy perimeter stateless routing (GPSR) and maxduration-minangle GPSR (MM-GPSR), the GPSR-AH and MM-GPSRAH improve the packet delivery rate (PDR) by approximately 51.3% and 35.5% at most, then improve throughput (THP) by approximately 71.4% and 27.2% at most.

articleTitle: An Aircraft Landing Gear State Detection and Recognition Method based on YOLO-V4
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: To solve the problems that most landing gear state detection methods based on image recognition or detection technology need to be divided into in multiple stages, which leads to low efficiency and weak image generalization ability for complex background and different acquisition angles, an single-stage aircraft landing gear state detection and recognition method based on YOLO-V4 is proposed. By adding landing gear state labels to aircraft samples, adding landing gear state output channels to the network, and cleverly designing the loss functions for training. The proposed method makes the detection results of visible landing gears in the corresponding viewing angle and the landing gear state of the aircraft object can be obtained at the same time, which has stronger generalization ability for images from different viewing angles and is easier to be applied in engineering. The experiment on self-made aircraft dataset shows that the proposed method is not only slightly higher than the two-stage method in the average accuracy rate of aircraft landing gear state recognition, but also the average accuracy of aircraft and landing gear detection is 98.92% and 76.00% respectively, which meets the requirements of practical application.

articleTitle: Dueling DQN-based hyper-heuristic algorithm for solving the location routing problem
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In order to solve the vehicle path siting problem with capacity in the logistics system more efficiently and make the system realize the overall optimization, so a hyper-heuristic algorithm based on Dueling DQN is proposed. The algorithm uses the Dueling DQN algorithm as the high-level selection strategy of the hyper-heuristic algorithm, evaluates the advantages and disadvantages of the underlying operators, and utilizes the reward and punishment values to weigh the operators; meanwhile, the simulated annealing mechanism with rewarming operation is used as the acceptance criterion of the algorithm, so as to control and guide the algorithm to search for the solution space more effectively. In addition, encodings are constructed that guarantee the feasibility of the solution and can avoid the use of solution repair techniques. Finally, a standardized algorithm for the capacitated siting path problem is computed and compared with other algorithms to verify the effectiveness and robustness of the algorithm on this problem.

articleTitle: Albert Based Policy Topic Classification Model
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: As an important government information resource, polices are the sum of rules and actions customized by the governments, political parties or other organizations to achieve their goals. In today’s explosive growth of data, in order to quickly retrieve policies related to established topics from massive data, we proposed a policy topic classification model based on the pretrained language model Albert. The model first pre-trained on an unsupervised large corpus, and then fine-tuned in a small amount of labeled data to improve the classification effect of policy topics. The experimental results show that this method can achieve automatic classification of policy topics, with classification results of macro average precision 92.74%, macro average recall 91.68%, and macro average F-Score 92.21%.

articleTitle: Blockchain-based Privacy-preserving Crowdsourcing Scheme
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: This paper presents a blockchain-based decentralized crowdsourcing framework that addresses challenges in traditional crowdsourcing systems, such as user identity, privacy, centralized servers, and service fees. The framework ensures anonymity, transparency, and fairness in crowdsourcing services by leveraging blockchain technology. To tackle linkability issues in blockchain-based systems, the paper proposes using cryptocurrency accounts with enhanced privacy features to protect user reputation while preserving privacy. Strategies to prevent private transactions and free-riding behavior are also proposed to enhance the crowdsourcing process integrity. The contributions of this work include a secure and anonymous crowdsourcing platform design, smart contract implementation, and feasibility evaluation through experiments on a local Ethereum blockchain. The experimental results demonstrate the practicality and efficiency of the proposed solution.

articleTitle: Swarm Intelligence Joint Optimization Algorithm for Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Wireless sensor networks consist of a large number of sensor nodes with limited energy. Because wireless sensor networks are mainly deployed in complex environments, it is difficult to charge or replace nodes. Therefore, the main concern of wireless sensor networks is the effective use of node energy. In this study, we propose a joint optimization algorithm based on the characteristics of Grey Wolf optimization algorithm, butterfly algorithm and ant colony algorithm. The algorithm uses the distance to the base station and the remaining energy to select the appropriate cluster head and the best data forwarding path. The simulation results show that the algorithm is superior to LEACH algorithm, grey wolf optimization algorithm and particle swarm optimization algorithm in network lifetime and residual energy.

articleTitle: Experimental Evaluation of UG2AG Wireless Communication Channel for LoRaWAN-based Underground Infrastructure Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: LoRaWAN-based wireless underground sensor networks (WUSNs) for underground infrastructure monitoring often need to operate in the presence of multiple layers of complex media, including water, air, soil, and pipes, etc. These media can cause complex refraction and reflection of signals during electromagnetic (EM) propagation, altering the signal’s wavefront. However, existing channel models do not account for the continuity of signal diffusion loss across multi-layer media, which can significantly affect the signal loss estimation. In this paper, we derive the diffusion loss of wireless signals in multi-layer media. Based on this derivation, we propose a new underground-to-aboveground (UG2AG) channel model for WUSNs. Furthermore, we deployed a small-scale WUSN system with ten nodes to experimentally verify the validity of the proposed model. These nodes were placed either directly in soils or inside a hollow underground pipe to simulate two distinct real-world burial scenarios. It is demonstrated that although LoRaWAN-based WUSNs can maintain nearly a 100 % packet delivery ratio (PDR) in both small-scale yet EM-complex environments, the multi-layer media has strong effects on UG2AG EM propagation.

articleTitle: A study on the application of visualization technology in virtual product design
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Smart communication technology and automation technology have brought many innovations and applications to the improvement of the field of virtual product design. The following are possible application research areas in virtual product design, including team members using remote conferencing and collaboration platforms for instant communication, while using smart technologies to share design concepts and communicate details. Such apps can speed up product development cycles, reduce communication costs, and facilitate the exchange of ideas. Design teams can create virtual prototype presentations. These virtual sample demonstrations can be shown to stakeholders remotely or at physical meetings to help them better understand product concepts and design details. Such applications help reduce the cost and time of actual sample production. Designers can create virtual reality simulated testing environments. Such an environment can be used for product functional testing, human-computer interaction testing and user experience evaluation. Through such simulation tests, the design team can detect problems early and perform corresponding design optimization. These demonstrations can use film, animation, or virtual reality technology to show various aspects of the product, including appearance, functionality, and operating procedures. Product dynamic display can help improve customers' understanding and confidence in products, thereby promoting product sales and promotion. This study uses the integration of two-dimensional and three-dimensional drawing techniques to practice image simulation technology and will share this practical research on computer image processing to provide a drawing reference for future designers.

articleTitle: Phase design and trajectory optimization of IRS-assisted UAV-ISAC system
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In this paper, an integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) system with intelligent reflector assistance (IRS) in the unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) scene is studied. For the system, the optimization problem of maximizing the minimum beam gain at the desired sensing angle of the target is proposed under the constraints of the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), the maximum transmit power of the UAV and the trajectory of the UAV to ensure the normal communication with the ground user. An enhanced reinforcement learning algorithm is used to optimize the UAV trajectory and solve the problem. The simulation results show that the performance of UAV-ISAC system deployed by IRS has certain advantages, and the perception performance can be improved.

articleTitle: Fundamental Localization Limits of Quantized Uplink mmWave MIMO Systems in Moving Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In this paper, we present the Cramér-Rao bound (CRB) analysis regarding the estimation of user’s position and velocity in uplink millimeter wave (mmWave) massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems, in which low-resolution analog-to-digital converters (ADCs) are implemented at the base station (BS). Specifically, we elaborately derive the Fisher Information matrices (FIMs) for not only the channel parameters, but also the localization-related parameters, i.e., position and velocity. With these matrices, we can obtain the fundamental estimation accuracy limits on the position and the velocity. Under various situations, numerical results are provided to show the impacts of the system setup on the localization, which enables us to gain some insights into the design of the localization system.

articleTitle: Secrecy Analysis in UAV-aided CR-NOMA Networks with Artificial Noise
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In this article, physical layer security is investigated in a non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) network with unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) relay in the context of underlay cognitive radio (CR). The secondary transmitter transmits the mixed signal incorporated with NOMA to the two legitimate users via the aid of a UAV relay in the presence of an eavesdropper. To enhance the system secrecy performance, the joint of artificial noise (AN) and decode-and-forward (DF) technique is applied. Considering all the channels undergo Nakagami-m fading with path loss, along with the interference of the primary transmitter, we derive the secrecy outage probabilities (SOPs) of both legitimate users to evaluate. Simulation results are presented and analyzed to verify the accuracy of derived expressions as well as to show the effectiveness of the proposed scheme and some critical parameters.

articleTitle: Specific Emitter Identification Based on IQ Imbalance and PA Nonlinearity Joint Estimation
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Specific emitter identification (SEI) plays an important role in both civil and military communication fields, offering the means to distinguish individual radio emitters. The intrinsic hardware distortions incurred by manufacturing imperfection can be used to identify emitters as radio frequency fingerprints (RFFs). However, RFFs extraction is highly challenging due to the coupling effects of the transmitter’s components, especially for the mixer and power amplifier (PA). This paper proposes a novel SEI scheme targeting in-phase/quadrature (IQ) imbalance and PA nonlinearity for quadrature amplitude modulation (QAM) systems. Our algorithm decouples IQ imbalance and PA non-linearity by leveraging the amplitude distribution characteristics of the QAM system before we estimate each of them, and then classify individual emitters by training a traditional classifier. Simulation results indicate that when handling 72 emitters characterized by randomly distributed IQ imbalances and PA nonlinearities, the proposed scheme can achieve a classification accuracy rate exceeding 90%.

articleTitle: User Grouping and Power Allocation for Downlink NOMA System with Statistical CSI
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In this paper, we consider a downlink non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) system over Nakagami-m fading channels. The base station (BS) serves several groups of users with hybrid multiple access scheme. A new user grouping and power allocation (UG-PA) strategy is proposed to enhance sum throughput. Based on the UG-PA strategy, we derive the exact and asymptotic closed-form expression of outage probability, and we further obtain the diversity order. Finally, we formulate a power allocation optimizaition problem to maximize sum throughput. We also design a genetic algorithm (GA) to find a suboptimal solution. Monte Carlo simulations verify the accuracy of our derived outage probability and diversity order. Comparisons with benchmark indicate the effectiveness of our proposed UG-PA strategy.

articleTitle: Out-of-Band Filter Compensation - GAMP Algorithm for clipped OFDM Signals
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The clipping and filtering (CF) method is commonly used in orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) systems to reduce the peak to average power ratio (PAPR). However, CF method also introduces substantial nonlinear distortion to the OFDM signal, leading to significant performance loss at receiver side. In this paper, a filter compensation-generalized approximate message passing (FC-GAMP) algorithm is proposed to mitigate performance losses caused by nonlinear distortions induced by the CF method. The algorithm incorporates a tailored design of out-of-band filtering and refines the approximate equations governing nonlinear processes by analyzing the probability distribution function post-distortion. Compared to the extant GAMP algorithms, the proposed FC-GAMP algorithm yields significant improvement in bit error rate (BER) performance under various conditions while maintaining computational efficiency comparable to traditional OFDM receivers.

articleTitle: Gesture Recognition Model Based on YOLOv8-AW
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: This paper proposes an improved deep model, YOLOv8-AW, based on the YOLOv8 algorithm for gesture detection. The paper enhances the feature pyramid network of the head by introducing the Asymptotic Feature Pyramid Network (AFPN). Feature fusion is conducted progressively, fostering better interaction between non-adjacent hierarchical levels to extract more valuable information and enhance the model’s perceptual capabilities for gesture features. To effectively reduce the genuine differences between predicted box dimensions and true box dimensions, modifications are made to the loss function. The Wise-IoU(WIoU) loss is introduced in the position regression loss function, focusing more on samples of ordinary quality, thereby improving the model’s generalization ability and overall performance. The WIoU loss has been introduced into the position regression loss function. Through experiments, the overall mAP of the improved model is increased by 0.2% over the basic YOLOV8, reaching 97.4%. The recall rate of gesture detection has increased by 8.3%, reaching 96.9%. The comprehensive performance shows that the improved model is more accurate in gesture recognition.

articleTitle: Global Context Interactive Learning for Group Activity Recognition
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Group activity recognition(GAR) aims to understant the activity in multi-person scenes. Previous methods have focused on individual feature inference but have not fully exploited individual-specific contextual information, which is important and useful in computer vision tasks. In this paper, we propose a global context interaction network(GCIN) with embedded Attention Pooling(AP) module and Context Encoding(CE) modules to bridge the gap between group activities and the visual environment. The Attention Pooling module extracts more representative individual features from extracted features, while the CE module encodes global contextual information into a individual feature and refines aggregated information to enhance individual representations. A graph network is then constructed through a multi-graph spatiotemporal graph convolutional network to generate semantic representations. Additionally, we further design a dual-branch model that integrates the designed modules into a pipeline. The effectiveness of each module on each branch is demonstrated through extensive experiments. Furthermore, our method achieves state-of-the-art results on two widely-used benchmark datasets.

articleTitle: Can Image Quality Metrics Detect Face Liveness?
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In this research paper, we delve into the impact of image quality metrics on face liveness detection. We conducted evaluations on eight distinct image quality metrics across four widely utilized face liveness detection databases. The experimental findings reveal that the chosen image quality metrics are initially unable to effectively differentiate between bona fide and spoofed face samples in their original state. Nevertheless, their performance demonstrates a significant improvement and becomes comparable to state-of-the-art traditional face liveness detection methods after fine-tuning them with liveness detection datasets.

articleTitle: Cluster Based Channel Estimation for mmWave Massive MIMO Systems With Lens Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Millmeter wave massive multiple-input multipleoutput (MIMO) systems with lens antenna is a promising architecture in the future communciation. We propose a new channel estimation scheme for uplink channel in mmWave massive MIMO systems with lens antenna in this paper, where the cluster sparisty and structure prior are both considered. In our proposed scheme, we utilize a non-uniform grid to quantize the angle of arrival(AoA) and characterize the cluster sparsity through the structure prior. We model the uplink channel estimation problem as a multiple measurement vector (MMV) problem, which is solved by our proposed algorithm based sparse Bayesian learning (SBL) considering structure prior. Finally, simulation results verify the effectiveness of our proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: A RISC-V On-chip Operating System Based on Rust
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Embedded devices have increasing demands for system security and reliability. In order to pursue performance, most operating system kernels developed today are still built using the C language, which is inherently unsafe. In contrast, Rust can provide both performance and safety almost without compromise. This article uses Rust to implement a general operating system kernel-MCore based on the RISC-V32 architecture. The kernel ensures memory safety and concurrency safety at compile time, avoiding data races during system runtime. The kernel is tested and run on QEMU and K210 development boards. The compiled kernel is only 6.8MB and is suitable for on-chip systems. MCore implemented dozens of POSIX system calls, tested them using Busybox and lmbench, and compared them with the distribution version Debain to demonstrate its performance and security.

articleTitle: An Enhanced Trajectory Optimization Approach for Equirectangular Camera-based Visual SLAM
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Compared to other cameras, panoramic cameras offer the advantages of rich feature points and enhanced robustness in tracking texture-deficient regions within visual SLAM solutions. However, the accuracy of their estimated trajectories can be significantly affected by invalid feature points. To mitigate this influence, this paper proposes a trajectory optimization method based on OpenVSLAM incorporating object detection and mask filtering techniques. Specifically, we introduce a mask-generated network to effectively filter out invalid feature points from the captured images. Additionally, an object detection mechanism is implemented to enable real-time rejection of dynamic character feature points through socket communication. Experimental results obtained in various site scenes demonstrate that the proposed algorithm improves trajectory accuracy and validates the effectiveness of our approach.

articleTitle: Ka-Band Reflective-Type Phase Shifter Using Multi-Resonant Loads and Digital Assistive Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: This paper presents a compact Ka-band reflective-type phase shifter (RTPS) that covers a continuous phase shift range. This RTPS consists of a broadband 3dB coupler and two identical fifth-order resonant loads, featuring lower insertion loss variation, and offering a compact chip. With the assistance of digital switches in loads, the robustness of the RTPS is further enhanced. The results show that RTPS can cover a range over 270°, demonstrating an insertion loss variation under ±2.5 dB at 41GHz. The RTPS is designed by 65-nm CMOS technology and die area is 0.19mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> excluding pads.

articleTitle: A Multi-Dimensional Joint Anti-Jamming Satellite Communication Method for Time Slot System
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: With the widely use of various electronic equipment and the intensification of electronic countermeasures, anti-jamming is the bottleneck problem that needs to be solved urgently in the field of satellite communication. In the face of dynamic and intelligent jamming environment, a multidimensional joint (MDJ) anti-jamming satellite communication method is proposed based on the time slot system. The best anti-jamming performance of the communication satellite system can be achieved by jointly considering several anti-jamming strategies such as channel coding, diversity combining and adaptive frequency hopping. Firstly, the multi-dimensional domain anti-jamming decision space model under the time slot system is established. The decision space is divided into two parts: waveform parameter space and channel parameter space, where the waveform parameter space includes the anti-jamming strategies of signal aspects such as modulation, channel coding and diversity combining. Then, based on the analysis of the transmission rate adaptive strategy and adaptive frequency hopping strategy, the MDJ anti-jamming algorithm is proposed. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by simulation analysis. Compared with existing methods, the proposed method can achieve higher communication capacity with less resource consumption.

articleTitle: Cryptoanalysis of Pairing-free Certificateless Aggregate Signcryption Schemes*
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: certificateless aggregate signcryption offers improved efficiency, scalability, flexibility, and security compared to traditional certificate-based signcryption schemes, which makes that it becomes a preferred solution for ensuring secure communication in various applications.Recently, to solve network congestion, feedback delay and privacy leakage during transmission in internet of vehicles, Xie et al. proposed an efficient certificateless aggregate signcryption with online/offline encryption. They claimed that their scheme is secure against the attacks from Type I and Type II adversaries, and can trace the real identity of a malicious vehicle. However, by analyzing it, we found that their schemes can not satisfy the claimed security. Finally, we give the corresponding attacks and the detailed improved scheme.

articleTitle: Self-supervised Object Detection Network From Sound Cues Based on Knowledge Distillation with Multimodal Cross Level Feature Alignment
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Sound, as one of the inherent attributes of objects, can provide valuable information for object detection. At present, the method of object location only by monitoring ambient sound is less robust. To solve this problem, a multimodal self-supervised knowledge distillation object detection network with cross level feature alignment is proposed. Taking RGB and depth images as input of teacher network and audio as input for student network, a multi-teacher cross-level feature alignment loss based on attention fusion is designed. It integrates students ’deep and shallow features to learn teachers’ corresponding middle layer features, so as to extract comprehensive knowledge with more efficiency. Positioning distillation loss is also added to obtain more localization information. In the multimodal audio-visual detection MAVD data set, the mAP value of the network increased 11.6% compared with the baseline network, demonstrating the superiority of the detection network.

articleTitle: Corruption-Robust Deep Convolutional Networks Inspired by Primary Visual Cortex
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: While deep convolutional neural networks (DCNNs) make impressive progress in object classi fi cation, they often struggle to recognize objects in images corrupted with different common noise patterns. Recent studies show that simulating a primary visual cortex (V1) at the front of DCNNs leads to improvements in noise-robustness. We develop a corruption-robust DCNN model inspired by V1 orientation selection receptive fields. In this study, we use the ImageNet-C dataset to evaluate the classification accuracy under four categories of image corruption. Our model exhibits an average improvement of 5.1% over the baseline DCNN on the perturbation benchmarks of common image corruptions. Compared with the VOneResNet, the model shows enhanced robustness against all corruption categories except for the digital effect. The experimental results demonstrate that introducing a more accurate V1-inspired model will further improve the robustness of DCNNs against image perturbations.

articleTitle: YOLOv5s-SLAM: A Monocular Visual SLAM method in Dynamic Environments
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: To deal with the problem that traditional visual SLAM methods in dynamic environments are susceptible to the influence of moving targets, which leads to a decrease in the system's localization accuracy. This paper presents a dynamic visual SLAM system named YOLOv5s-SLAM. YOLOv5s is embedded in the ORB-SLAM3 system to recognize dynamic targets in the surrounding environment by deep learning methods and simultaneously extract ORB feature points with the SLAM system at the front end as a way to improve real-time performance. Combined with the constructed dynamic object detection rules, the dynamic feature points are divided and removed, which effectively reduces the mismatching in the feature extraction process and the impact on the system performance, and achieves the optimization of the visual SLAM localization performance. Tests on the TUM dataset show that the proposed method has smaller trajectory errors and higher position estimation accuracy, which can effectively enhance the robustness of localization.

articleTitle: Low Complexity Deep Learning Method for Base Graph of Protograph LDPC Decoding
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Deep learning-based decoding algorithms have emerged as a focal point currently in contemporary research. Neural Offset Min-Sum Belief Propagation decoding algorithm is one of the traditional deep learning methods rooted in model-driven approaches. However, with the gradual increase in codeword length, there is an inevitable surge in the training cost and time complexity of such kind of deep learning algorithms. Addressing this issue, a novel deep learning algorithm based on the structural characteristics of the base graph in protograph LDPC codes is proposed. By strategically training the base graph and introducing a unique bit decoding allocation strategy, we endeavor to harmonize the Deep Learning algorithm with the intrinsic structure of the base graph itself. This approach contrasts favorably with several existing methods that utilize conventional segmental deep learning decoding algorithms for protograph LDPC codes. Simulation results demonstrate that, compared to other model-driven based deep learning algorithms, the proposed algorithm significantly reduces the number of parameters required for storage and training, while the loss in decoding performance remains within acceptable bounds.

articleTitle: Microservice Partitioning for Cloud Computing via Constrained Graph Neural Network Clustering
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: With the rise of cloud computing, microservices architecture has become the preferred choice for modern software design. Microservices are inherently suited for cloud environments, as they allow for the dynamic allocation of resources based on demand, facilitating elastic scalability.
